W7172243644.abstract: Abstract The influence of annealing on the dry reciprocating tribological behavior of fused filament fabrication (FFF)-printed neat polylactic acid (PLA) and graphene-reinforced PLA was investigated. Specimens were annealed at 90, 100, and 120 °C for 60, 120, and 240 min and tested under dry reciprocating sliding against a 6-mm Al 2 O 3 ball according to ASTM G133. Friction was obtained from the tangential-to-normal force ratio, while the specific wear coefficient was determined from gravimetric volume loss normalized by normal load and sliding distance. Worn surfaces were examined by stereomicroscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Annealing substantially improved the wear resistance of both materials: relative to the as-printed condition, the specific wear coefficient decreased by up to approximately 74% for neat PLA and 93% for graphene-reinforced PLA. Friction followed a different trend: among the annealed conditions, the mean coefficient ranged from approximately 0.51–0.73 for neat PLA and from 0.48 to 0.54 for graphene-reinforced PLA. The wear reduction was associated with concurrent annealing-induced changes in crystallinity and mechanical properties; these relationships are therefore interpreted as phenomenological correlations rather than independent causal relationships. Graphene-reinforced PLA exhibited lower wear than neat PLA throughout the investigated conditions; the separation between the two material datasets was not fully described by the bulk properties considered here. Microscopy showed surface morphologies consistent with extensive plastic deformation, tearing, and delamination-like damage in neat PLA and with milder grooving, localized cracking, and compacted debris in graphene-reinforced PLA. Under the investigated dry reciprocating sliding conditions, annealing and graphene reinforcement were associated with lower wear.

W7211872634.abstract: Patient-specific dressings for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) must follow the individual lesion, yet pub- lished image-to-fabrication pipelines rely on depth sensing and seldom report the accuracy of the fabricated object. We present IMTOP, a low-cost pipeline that turns a single calibrated RGB photograph into a printable patient-specific patch, with a validation framework centred on the patch itself. Abso- lute scale is recovered from two operator-placed points on a reference of known length; the wound contour is offset by a perilesional margin and extruded to a watertight STL solid. The patch error is decomposed into segmentation, scale and printing terms, measured on 149 public clinical DFU images (uncalibrated, in pixel units) with three segmenters and on 18 printed phantoms of known geometry, the scale term coming from a Monte Carlo simulation of calibration-point placement. By mean magnitude segmentation was the largest term (6.4% for the Segment Anything Model, against 5.0% for scale at an assumed 3 px placement noise and 0.69% for printing; combined 8.1%), whereas by variance scale prevailed for two of three segmenters; phantoms were reconstructed to 0.32% area error, pointing to wound-border ambiguity as the main clinical error source. Mask overlap correlated with, but did not determine, the patch error, and the residual under-coverage sized a segmenter-specific perilesional offset covering the wound in 95% of the evaluated cases.

W7220124432.abstract: This paper presents an academically rigorous, multi-layered digital preservation framework designed for tangible cultural heritage, utilizing a proposed case study of historic Islamic cemeteries (specifically focusing on batu nesan or Jawi-inscribed tombstones) in Kuching, Sarawak. Tangible architectural assets and epigraphical records globally face accelerating degradation caused by tropical weathering, biological colonization, urbanization, and vandalism. Traditional documentation methods—such as subjective hand-drawing, standard photography, or invasive chemical molding and charcoal rubbings (frottage)—are either metrically insufficient or cause physical wear on fragile stone matrices. To establish an objective, contactless, and permanent archival record, we outline a paradigm shift from static 3D models to dynamic, Heritage Building Information Modeling (HBIM)-based Digital Twins (Akyol & Avci, 2025; Devetakovi? & Djordjevi?, 2022). Our geomatic capture methodology evaluates the optical performance of Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) phase-shifting sensors against Structured Light Scanning (SLS) systems (Arias et al., 2022; Tenschert et al., 2018). Crucially, we address the optical limitation of laser-based ranging on polished, crystalline stone surfaces (such as marble and granite), where subsurface scattering and reflection generate significant depth measurement bias and geometric noise, obscuring sub-millimeter engravings. We propose the deployment of high-resolution blue LED Structured Light Scanning (SLS), achieving a 3D point resolution of up to 30 µm to capture fine calligraphic details contact-free. To decipher heavily weathered or eroded inscriptions, we apply Morphological Residual Models (MRM) as a trend-removal mathematical filter on reconstructed meshes (Pires et al., 2015). MRM isolates micro-relief surface details (residuals) from the backdrop geometry and renders them as distinct, color-coded vertex attributes. We then integrate these color-coded datasets into a Virtual Polynomial Texture Mapping (V-PTM) workspace. This allows epigraphists to use an interactive Reflectance Transformation Imaging (RTI) viewer to simulate virtual light domes and sweep raking light across the color-coded inscriptions, resolving overlapping strokes and recovering illegible texts. Finally, we describe a fabrication pipeline to translate these digital twins into physical, scaled didactic resources using multi-material Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) 3D printing (Arias et al., 2022). By employing polylactic acid (PLA) for the model and water-soluble polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) for the support structures, the fragile physical Jawi reliefs are preserved from structural wear during chemical post-print cleanup. To support global collaborative research, we advocate for archiving finalized datasets in lossless Wavefront .OBJ and Stereolithography .STL formats under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial (CC BY-NC) licenses in open-access library repositories (Groenendyk, 2013).

W7221461028.abstract: Abstract Paraquat (PQ) is a widely used herbicide categorized as an environmental contaminant due to its high toxicity and risk to aquatic ecosystems and human health. In this study, we developed a Screen-printed Disposable Polyethylene Terephthalate (SD-PET) sensor using a green sodium alginate/graphite conductive ink. To maximize performance, the electrode surface was modified with a bamboo biochar composite incorporating copper nanoparticles (BC-CuNPs). Under optimized differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) conditions, the BC-CuNPs sensor outperformed the other configurations, displaying excellent linearity for PQ detection from 10 to 250 µmol L −1 (R 2 = 0.988), a sensitivity of 0.0234 µA µmol −1 L, and limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) of 7.65 µmol L −1 and 25.48 µmol L −1 , respectively. Selectivity studies against common aquatic interferents (chloroquine, levofloxacin, and sulfamethoxazole) and tap water assays indicated mild matrix effects, though the device successfully quantified the analyte under competitive conditions. UV–Vis spectrophotometry validated the accuracy of the proposed method as an independent reference technique. Furthermore, the environmental sustainability of the device was quantitatively confirmed by green chemistry metrics, achieving a high AGREE score of 0.71 and a favorable ComplexGAPI profile. Despite presenting a limited shelf life over 21 days, the developed SD-PET/BC-CuNPs sensor stands out as a highly efficient, eco-friendly, and viable alternative for on-site environmental monitoring of paraquat.

W7221503846.abstract: The coffee-making process generates substantial quantities of organic residues. Spent Coffee Grounds (SCG) represents a major waste stream produced after beverage preparation. Its rich composition in lipids, lignocellulosic fractions, proteins, phenolics and other bioactive compounds makes it a promising feedstock for integrated biorefineries. This review critically evaluates SCG valorisation routes for biofuels and value-added products, with particular attention to oil extraction, biodiesel production, defatted SCG (DSCG) utilisation and biorefinery development. Literature indicates that SCG generally contains approximately 10–20wt.% oil, with a biodiesel conversion efficiency of ∼95%. Nevertheless, biodiesel scalability remains constrained by high acidity, moisture removal, solvent recovery and feedstock logistics. Anaerobic digestion is promising, as DSCG can generate higher methane yields than SCG, with reported values of 336±7 mLCH4/gVS and 310±2 mLCH4/gVS, respectively. Pellet, biochar and activated carbon pathways appear more scalable because they require fewer high-purity separation steps, whereas bioethanol, nutraceutical, bioactive compound and bioplastic routes require more intensive pretreatment, extraction, purification and product validation. Technology Readiness Level, techno-economic feasibility, environmental benefit and scalability indicate that integrated biorefineries are more realistic than single-product valorisation. Coupling Techno-Economic Analysis with Life Cycle Assessment is essential for identifying SCG valorisation pathways that are technically feasible, environmentally beneficial and commercially viable.
W7221503846.title: Valorisation of Spent Coffee Grounds in integrated biorefineries: a comprehensive review of biofuels and value-added products potential

W7221505068.abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) lattices are attractive cellular architectures owing to their smooth, curvature-continuous geometry, high surface-to-volume ratio, and efficient load-bearing behavior. TPMS structures are widely investigated for lightweight and energy-absorption applications, including impact-resistant protection systems and medical scaffolds. In this work, dual-nozzle fused deposition modeling (FDM) is employed to fabricate single-phase TPMS specimens from polylactic acid (PLA), while a complementary phase structure (CPS) is fabricated from polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG). The combination of these phases results in an interpenetrating phase composite (IPC). Four sheet-based TPMS topologies, namely Primitive, Gyroid, Diamond, and I-graph-wrapped package (IWP), are investigated. Quasi-static compression experiments are conducted to characterize and compare the compressive performance of the interpenetrating architectures and their constituent-phase counterparts. The results demonstrate that IPC architectures outperform the TPMS and CPS phases, revealing a strong synergistic effect induced by phase interpenetration. This structural synergy promotes more uniform deformation and mitigates strain localization. The IWP, Gyroid, and Primitive topologies exhibit the greatest improvements in stiffness, whereas the Primitive and Gyroid architectures achieve the highest yield stress and energy absorption capacity.

W7221516045.abstract: This study investigates the structural and thermal responses of maleic anhydride-modified polylactic acid (PLA) prepared through peroxide-initiated reactive melt processing using integrated Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The objective was to determine how MA content is associated with the local spectral environment, thermal-transition and crystallization behavior, and thermal stability of PLA. FTIR analysis revealed progressive variations in band intensity, broadening, asymmetry, and localized spectral distribution with increasing MA content, particularly in the carbonyl and fingerprint regions, while the characteristic PLA absorption framework remained identifiable. A weak shoulder at approximately 1630–1650 cm -1 was interpreted cautiously as a localized spectral variation rather than definitive evidence of a newly formed chemical structure. DSC showed lower glass transition temperatures (T g ) of 53.4–56.2 °C for the modified formulations compared with 64.8 °C for neat PLA and distinct cold-crystallization peaks (T cc ) at 95.3–97.5 °C, while melting temperatures (T m ) remained within 174.5–176.7 °C. TGA showed that the temperature at 5% mass loss (T 5 %) decreased from 342.1 °C for neat PLA to 320.1–339.2 °C for the modified formulations, whereas the maximum degradation temperature (T max ) remained comparatively stable at 368.8–372.5 °C. Collectively, the integrated FTIR–DSC–TGA results demonstrate that MA-containing reactive melt processing is associated with distinct changes in spectral, thermal-transition, crystallization, and early-stage thermal responses, while key PLA characteristics remain identifiable. This integrated interpretation provides a basis for understanding how formulation changes are reflected across complementary spectral and thermal responses, supporting future studies on modified PLA materials.
W7221516045.title: Integrated FTIR, DSC, and TGA analyses of structural evolution and thermal behavior in maleic anhydride-modified polylactic acid prepared by reactive melt processing

W7221543651.abstract: Kazakhstan combines a large agricultural-residue base with an expanding grain-processing sector, creating a credible platform for biodegradable polymers if feedstock availability is matched to polymer chemistry, pretreatment intensity, and realistic end-of-life routes. This critical review integrates Kazakhstan-specific production data with the chemistry of starch, cellulose, hemicelluloses, lignin, and rice-husk silica and evaluates the conversion pathways most relevant to domestic implementation. Collectible dry residues from wheat, barley, maize, and rice are estimated at about 15.1 Mt yr−1, while potato and cereal starch streams provide directly processable carbohydrates. Near-term options are thermoplastic starch (TPS), cellulose/nanocellulose reinforcement, lignin-containing functional composites, and hybrid materials using rice-husk-derived silica. PLA and PHA offer higher-value routes but require fermentation, purification, polymerization or recovery, and dedicated end-of-life infrastructure. The review emphasizes molecular limitations—hydrogen-bonded polysaccharide networks, retrogradation, interfacial polarity mismatch, lignocellulosic recalcitrance, filler agglomeration, and environment-dependent biodegradation—and links them to processing and performance tests. A staged strategy is proposed: compound and reinforce existing starch streams first, build regional fractionation and standardized intermediate platforms next, and develop PLA/PHA fermentation only after low-cost carbon streams, product markets, and life-cycle advantages are demonstrated.

W7221549859.abstract: Vascular stents, serving as a cornerstone in the interventional treatment of cardiovascular diseases, had undergone rapid technological evolution and accumulation of clinical evidence. To systematically deconstruct the global research landscape, collaborative networks, and knowledge development pathways, we conducted a bibliometric and visual analysis of 5322 relevant articles (2015-2025) from the Web of Science Core Collection using VOSviewer and CiteSpace. The results showed that the annual publication growth had entered a plateau phase characterized by deepening integration, with the paradigm transitioning from discrete technological iteration toward system integration. Besides, keyword clustering identified four major research pillars including precision decision-making in revascularization, material innovation, personalized antiplatelet therapy, and evaluation based on clinical evidence. Notably, the intersection of materials science and biology (e.g., biodegradable polymers, immunomodulatory coatings) was the key driver of cutting-edge advancements. We further pointed out that future breakthroughs would depend on the deep integration of biodegradable smart materials, artificial intelligence-empowered precision intervention, and dynamic management based on real-world data. Therefore, we believe that the constructed knowledge graph and the proposed paradigm transition framework clarify the developmental trajectory and provide an evidence-based roadmap for future innovation.

W7221559148.abstract: Abstract The growing environmental concern over petroleum-based plastics has intensified the demand for sustainable alternatives with high performance and reliable processability. Bio-based plastics have attracted considerable attention as sustainable alternatives to petroleum-derived plastics. However, despite their environmental advantages, their development and application are severely constrained by the necessity for tedious chemical modification and complex processing. Herein, we propose a covalent adaptable network strategy to transform chitosan (CS) into a thermally processable bioplastic through simple and efficient dynamic covalent enamine cross-linking. The enamine bonds enable network rearrangement upon heating, imparting hot-press processability, thermal repairability, and closed-loop recyclability to the material. The resulting bioplastic exhibits a high flexural strength of 189.8 MPa, excellent moisture and solvent resistance, favorable recyclability, high thermal stability, a low thermal expansion coefficient of 1.05 ppm k−1, superior quantitative green chemistry metrics, and rapid soil-burial disintegration. With these advantageous features, the developed bioplastic represents a promising sustainable substitute for conventional petroleum-based plastics.

W7221565239.abstract: Abstract Solar-driven photocatalytic water splitting represents a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production. However, the practical application of single-component photocatalysts is severely constrained by rapid bulk charge-carrier recombination. CdZnS (CZS) solid solutions have garnered significant interest as visible-light-active photocatalysts due to their compositionally tunable band structures. However, photocorrosion and sluggish interfacial charge transfer critically hinder their practical application. To address these limitations, we herein report an S-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst (Ni-CZS/MW), constructed by integrating Ni-doped CZS (Ni-CZS) with MnWO4 (MW). Ni-doping markedly diminishes the work function of Ni-CZS, creating a substantial work-function difference with MW that induces interfacial charge asymmetry. An internal electric field generated by the intimate contact at the Ni-CZS/MW interface directs the migration of photoexcited electrons from MW to Ni-CZS through an S-scheme charge-transfer pathway, thereby significantly enhancing charge-carrier separation efficiency. Under visible-light irradiation, the optimized Ni-CZS/MW heterostructure produces 882 μmol of hydrogen. Furthermore, this catalyst demonstrates a strong ability to catalytically reform microplastics, the hybrid system simultaneously generates 331 μmol of hydrogen and upcycles PLA into pyruvic acid (PA). Collectively, these findings elucidate the synergistic roles of S-scheme heterojunction engineering and Ni-doping in modulating charge-carrier dynamics, and provide a strategic framework for designing photocatalysts tailored for plastic waste valorization.

W7221581120.abstract: Conducting polymers have attracted significant research interest because of their excellent electrical conductivity, chemical stability, low cost, ease of synthesis, and reversible redox behavior. These organic polymers can function as semiconductors or conductors due to the presence of conjugated π-electron systems along their polymer backbone. Among the most extensively studied conducting polymers are polyaniline (PANI), polypyrrole, polythiophene, and polyphenylene vinylene. Fourier Transform Infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy of acid-functionalized carbon nanotubes (CNTs) revealed a broad absorption peak between 3750–4000 cm⁻¹, corresponding to free hydroxyl groups, confirming successful functionalization. FT-IR analysis of pure PANI exhibited characteristic quinoid and benzenoid ring vibrations, indicating its conductive emeraldine structure. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis demonstrated that the modified CNTs retained their cylindrical morphology and crystalline structure, while PANI displayed a highly ordered crystalline arrangement associated with enhanced electrical conductivity. Electrical conductivity measurements of polycaprolactone (PCL), CNT-g-PANI, and CNT-g-PANI-g-PDO composites showed that CNT-g-PANI-g-PDO possessed the highest conductivity. Pure PCL acted as an electrical insulator, whereas polydioxanone (PDO) improved the dispersion of CNTs and PANI within the PCL matrix, resulting in superior conductive pathways. Among the tested formulations, the composite containing 1 wt% CNT exhibited the highest conductivity. These findings demonstrate that dual covalent and noncovalent functionalization of CNTs through PANI and PDO effectively enhances the electrical performance of biodegradable polymer composites.
W7221581120.title: Dual functionalization of Carbon Nanotubes/Polyaniline in Polydioxanone nanocomposites: An improved dispersion for conducting fibers

W7221596481.abstract: With the rapid growth of plastic production, plastic pollution has become increasingly widespread and persistent in the environment. This persistent pollution poses potential risks to ecosystems and human health. Microbial biodegradation offers a promising approach to plastic waste management because it operates under mild reaction conditions and has potential for sustainable application. This review summarizes recent advances in the major microbial groups involved in plastic biodegradation, methods for assessing degradation efficiency, underlying mechanisms, and strategies for improving degradation performance. Assessment methods are discussed, from physicochemical characterization to biochemical validation. Meanwhile, it emphasizes that real plastic biodegradation and degradation efficiency require multiple complementary lines of evidence to judge in a more complete and objective way. The complete process and molecular mechanisms of microbial plastic degradation are then described, including microbial attachment and biofilm formation, enzymatic degradation, intracellular metabolism, and mineralization of degradation products. In addition, it summarizes various efficiency optimization strategies for degradation, including plastic pretreatment, bioaugmentation, and regulation of environmental parameters. The lack of standardized assessment, limited practical translation, and ecological risks are the identified key challenges. Finally, standardized efficiency evaluation strategies, plastic upcycling, and emerging technologies for subsequent development were discussed. This review aims to provide a reference for understanding microbial plastic degradation.
W7221596481.title: Microbial Biodegradation of Plastics: Methods for Assessing Degradation Mechanisms and Optimization Strategies

W7221633271.abstract: Background and purpose: 5‑fluorouracil (5‑FU) is a widely used antimetabolite chemotherapeutic agent. However, it has substantial cytotoxicity and may cause serious adverse effects, including gastrointestinal toxicity, myelosuppression, and, less commonly, cardiac and neurologic toxicity. To achieve sustained release and reduce systemic exposure and administration frequency, 5-FU can be microencapsulated in biodegradable, non-toxic polyhydroxyalkanoate matrices. Experimental approach: In this research, 5-FU-loaded poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (P3HB) and poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (P3HBV) micro- and nanoparticles were prepared via spray drying and single emulsion solvent evaporation methods. The obtained particles were characterized in terms of their average hydrodynamic size, zeta potential, surface morphology, drug loading, encapsulation efficiency, release patterns, hemolytic activity, and cytotoxicity to HeLa cervical cancer cells. Key results: The obtained 5-FU-loaded micro- and nanoparticles had a regular spherical shape without surface defects. The nanoparticles were nearly identical in size regardless of the presence of 5‑FU. In contrast, the encapsulation of 5‑FU into microparticles by spray drying caused measurable increases in particle size, with the average hydrodynamic diameter increasing by 21.0 % for P3HB and by 28.6 % for P3HBV. Although the single emulsion solvent evaporation technique did not achieve therapeutically relevant 5‑FU loading, spray-dried microparticles showed satisfactory drug loading and sustained release of 5-FU over 48 h. The microparticles exhibited pronounced cytotoxicity against HeLa cervical cancer cells while demonstrating lower hemolytic activity than free 5‑FU. Conclusion: In this study, the promising drug-loaded systems based on polyhydroxyalkanoate microparticles were prepared and characterized for sustained 5-FU delivery in the therapy of cervical cancer.

W7221658274.abstract: The growing demand for sustainable materials in landscape architecture has highlighted the potential of polylactic acid/polybutylene adipate-terephthalate (PLA/PBAT)-based wood-plastic composites. However, poor interfacial compatibility between the hydrophilic plant fibers and the hydrophobic polyester matrices, coupled with susceptibility to hydrolytic degradation, limits their outdoor applications. This study presents a synergistic modification strategy for bamboo powder using a silane coupling agent (KH550) and nano-silica (Nano-SiO2), integrating all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with accelerated aging experiments to elucidate the enhancement mechanism of "chemical bridging–physical filling. " MD simulations revealed that the modification forms a dense "core-shell" barrier via covalent anchoring and a robust hydrogen-bond network, reducing the interfacial free volume to 14.1 % and lowering the water molecule self-diffusion coefficient from 4.58 × 10–7 to 0.42 × 10–7 cm2 s–1. This microscopic moisture barrier underpins the macroscopic aging resistance. Accelerated UV-condensation aging tests (1000 h) confirmed that the modified composites preserved the polyester backbone, with a weight-average molecular weight retention of 88.4 %, a tensile strength of 84.3 %, and an impact strength of 81.2 %. The surface color change was limited to E = 4.2, markedly outperforming unmodified composites. Additionally, the initial properties were improved: water absorption decreased from 4.25 % to 1.85 %, tensile strength reached 46.5 MPa, and impact strength reached 6.2 kJ m–2, achieving concurrent rigidity and toughness enhancement. These results demonstrate that nano-synergistic modification effectively mitigates weathering-induced degradation in PLA/PBAT composites, offering a practical pathway for their sustainable application in outdoor landscape environments.

W7221673886.abstract: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) enables layer-by-layer fabrication of objects from diverse materials directly from CAD files, with increasing adaptability and speed due to technological advancements. This study focuses on optimizing the compressive properties of hollow and thin-walled Polylactic acid (PLA) structures reinforced with bamboo filler, produced via FDM 3D printing. Using the Taguchi method and Principal Component Analysis (PCA), key printing parameters are systematically analyzed. Optimal parameters from main effects analysis identified as topology design (design 2), wall thickness (1 mm), layer height (0.3 mm), infill density (20%), infill layer thickness (0.6 mm), infill flow (80%), infill pattern (octet), print speed (80 mm/s), printing temperature (210°C), bed temperature (65°C), and orientation (flat along the y-axis). ANOVA identifies topology as the most significant factor, contributing 29.998% to optimization. The bamboo filler in PLA enhances mechanical properties, particularly under flatwise compression. Experimental results show significant improvements in maximum force, stress, and compressive modulus for PLABF-10, due to optimized printing conditions and material composition. This study offers valuable insights into material modification and process optimization, advancing sustainable and high-performance 3D printed hollow and thin-walled structures.

W7221685780.abstract: The rotated triangular auxetic (RTA) lattice structure shows a stable deformation behaviour which is mainly controlled by geometric mechanisms, under compressive loading. In this study, we experimentally examine the compressive response of the RTA lattice structure made with fused deposition modelling (FDM) for four polymers: thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), acrylonitrile butadiene styrene reinforced with 20% of carbon fibre (ABS-CF), acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS), and Polylactic acid (PLA). The lattice geometry and strain limits were adopted from the previously validated RTA study. Numerical validation of a reference RTA lattice was first completed using Abaqus/Explicit to establish a reliable baseline. The compression tests were conducted up to 40% strain. PLA lattices showed the highest average engineering compressive stress of 25.18 MPa at 40% strain whereas ABS-CF showed highest initial stiffness of 93.12 MPa despite premature brittle failure. The ABS lattices displayed an average compressive strength of 4.42 MPa and an effective compressive modulus of 58.93 MPa, demonstrating stable progressive deformation up to 40% strain. The compressive strength and effective compressive modulus for TPU was 7.60 MPa and 45 MPa respectively. PLA demonstrated the highest specific energy absorption (SEA) value of 4.36 kJ/kg among the tested materials, followed by ABS, TPU and ABS-CF showing SEA values of1.53 kJ/kg, 1.14 kJ/kg and 0.111 kJ/kg, respectively. The extent of densification differed according to the material properties, but all specimens exhibited similar initial deformation and progressive collapse behaviour. The findings provide experimental insights on the compressive behaviour and energy absorption performance of polymer-based RTA lattices and offer benchmark values for future numerical studies for energy absorption applications.
W7221685780.title: Experimental investigation of the compressive behaviour of FDM-fabricated rotated triangular auxetic lattices for energy absorption applications

W7221691162.abstract: Electrocatalytic oxidation of ethylene glycol (EG), a key component recoverable from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic waste streams, offers a promising strategy to couple plastic upcycling with energy-efficient hydrogen production and value-added chemical synthesis. However, the development of catalysts that simultaneously deliver high activity and controlled product selectivity remains a critical challenge. Here, a series of phase-controlled nickel sulfide catalysts were synthesized via a facile hydrothermal method and evaluated for the EG oxidation reaction (EGOR). Their catalytic performance was found to correlate strongly with the electron occupancy of the Ni e g orbitals. Combined electrochemical analysis, magnetic characterization, and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy reveal that Ni 3 S 2 possesses a mixed-valence electronic structure with moderate e g occupancy, abundant unpaired electrons, and enhanced electronic delocalization, enabling efficient charge transfer and favorable EG adsorption/activation. This structure–activity relationship is further supported by density functional theory calculations, which show that Ni 3 S 2 exhibits a high density of states near the Fermi level and stronger EG adsorption than the other investigated nickel sulfide phases. As a result, Ni 3 S 2 delivers superior EGOR activity and high selectivity toward formate, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of up to 86%. Operando infrared spectroscopy further elucidates the reaction pathway from EG to formate, confirming efficient C–C bond cleavage and rapid oxidation of EG-derived intermediates. This work identifies e g occupancy as a useful electronic descriptor for nickel sulfide catalysts and provides mechanistic guidance for the selective electro-upgrading of PET-derived EG, biomass-derived polyols, and other oxygenated carbon feedstocks into value-added products.

W7221710525.abstract: Purpose The primary aim of this research is to investigate the extent to which standard Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) 3D printers can be explicitly controlled to fabricate flexible microstructures. Specifically, the study seeks to determine if manipulating automated toolpaths via geometric code (G-code) generation can consistently produce extruded strings significantly smaller than conventional nozzle diameters. Furthermore, it aims to explore multidisciplinary applications for these micro-lattices, transitioning them from theoretical novelties to functional components in fields such as biomedical engineering and filtration. Design/methodology/approach The methodology utilises FullControl G-code (FCG) to bypass conventional slicing software, explicitly programming hardware movements to control extrusions. An iterative experimental process was employed using a BambuLab P1P printer with a standard 0.2mm nozzle to test polylactic acid (PLA) and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU). Parameters such as pull height, travel speed and extrusion rate were systematically varied and evaluated to achieve optimal string generation. These single micro-extrusions were then layered into complex, multi-axis planar meshes, which were subsequently baked to achieve structural adhesion. Findings The study demonstrates that carefully manipulated G-code enables the consistent production of precise microlattices with string diameters of 30–50 µm using a 0.2mm nozzle. PLA extrusions achieved diameters as fine as 20 µm with high consistency. TPU proved more challenging due to its flexibility and porosity, yet successfully yielded 30 µm strings under optimal parameters (1.2–1.6mm pull height). Applying radiant heat to the layered TPU strings ($180ˆ{\circ}C$ for 10 min) successfully induced uniform adhesion, transforming isolated strings into cohesive, functional planar meshes. Research limitations/implications A primary limitation is the difficulty in maintaining uniform string diameters across varying lengths within complex overlapping mesh designs. Furthermore, the employed stringing method lacks inherent tension during printing; combined with TPU's flexibility, this occasionally results in inconsistent gaps between woven strings rather than a perfectly rigid grid. The manual nature of programming G-code via FCG also introduces time constraints. Future research should investigate more precise heat application methods for adhesion and further refine the parameter algorithms to improve uniformity in multi-layered lattice structures. Practical implications The ability to fabricate micro-lattices on standard, consumer-grade FDM hardware significantly lowers the barrier to entry for micro-manufacturing, negating the need for highly specialised, expensive machinery. This methodology can be immediately applied to produce bespoke, flexible micro-structures for various industries. Proven use cases include high-resolution water or air filtration systems and acoustic dampening. In biomedical contexts, these scalable meshes offer a viable foundational framework for custom medical wound dressings or cellular tissue interaction arrays, where mechanical stretch is required for drug administration. Originality/value While previous research has demonstrated the use of FCG for micro-extrusions using rigid materials like PLA, this study pioneers the application of these techniques to elastic polymers, specifically TPU. By successfully establishing an optimised parametric framework for flexible micro-stringing, this paper proves that highly intricate, functional soft-material microstructures can be consistently fabricated without conventional slicing constraints. This expands the theoretical boundaries of standard FDM printing, bridging the gap between accessible desktop prototyping and advanced multidisciplinary fabrication.
W7221710525.title: Investigating parameters to control 3D-printed extrusions at the micro-level using PLA and TPU

W7221726593.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are not environmentally static particles; aging, fragmentation, contaminant acquisition, organic conditioning, and microbial colonization progressively convert them into dynamic particle–chemical–microbial interfaces. This transformation is central to their environmental fate and risk because plastisphere communities can alter particle transport, contaminant partitioning, nutrient cycling, antimicrobial-resistance dynamics, and polymer transformation. Experimental evidence shows that MP biofilms can increase conjugative transfer of antibiotic-resistance genes by approximately 7.2–19.6-fold relative to suspended bacteria, illustrating that microbial colonization can modify ecological function rather than merely change community composition. However, microbial presence, functional-gene enrichment, surface deterioration, and polymer mass loss should not be interpreted as equivalent evidence of biodegradation. Stable-isotope studies show that even biodegradable polymers may mineralize slowly and incompletely; approximately 65% mineralization of 1 3 C-labeled PBS required 425 days, whereas direct mineralization of persistent polyolefins remains far more limited. Ecotoxicological effects are similarly conditional on particle size, morphology, aging, associated chemicals, exposure duration, and environmental context, and evidence for trophic transfer is stronger than that for generalized biomagnification. Interpretation is further constrained by substantial analytical heterogeneity in sampling, size cut-offs, recovery, contamination control, polymer identification, and number-vs.-mass reporting, making methodological harmonization and uncertainty assessment essential for cross-study comparison. Remediation should therefore distinguish particle capture from destruction and biodeterioration from depolymerization, microbial assimilation, mineralization, and true upcycling. Although enzymatic and microbial conversion technologies show considerable promise, most high-performance demonstrations involve defined polymers, post-consumer plastics, or prepared hydrolysates rather than heterogeneous environmental MPs. Safe application consequently requires carbon and contaminant mass balances, residue and product safety testing, microbial containment, and life-cycle verification. Climate-sensitive transport and toxicity further reinforce the dynamic nature of MP exposure, while circular-economy strategies should prioritize prevention, low-shedding design, reuse, and recovery before attempting energy-intensive reclamation of dispersed environmental particles. Overall, a microbiology-informed assessment of MPs requires progression from microbial identity to demonstrated function, from particle detection to exposure relevance, and from apparent removal or degradation to verified net risk reduction.
W7221726593.title: Microplastics as evolving particle–chemical–microbial interfaces: plastisphere ecology, ecotoxicity, and safety-informed remediation

W7221727623.abstract: ABSTRACT With pressing global concerns, such as climate change and global warming, it is essential to advance research on renewable energy sources and cleaner agricultural strategies. Plant microbial fuel cells (PMFCs) are bioelectrical systems that utilize root exudates from plants and metabolic activities of microorganisms in the rhizosphere, driven by photosynthetic processes, to generate bioelectricity and mitigate methane emissions in rice paddies. This study investigated the effects of 18 3D‐printed conductive polylactic acid PMFC cells, connected through copper wires in both individual and stacked configurations, on PMFC power density and assessed methane mitigation when integrating PMFCs into growing Oryza sativa, using literature results for scenario‐based analyses. Through cumulative stacking, the third stacking configuration generated a higher power density than the other configurations, maximizing the power generated at 26 µW/m 2 . Despite the minimal electricity generation, integrating PMFCs in paddies through scenario‐based analyses will yield simulated methane reductions of 0.012 and 0.016 kg, considering 38% and 50% methane reduction studies, for 1 m 2 of land used for rice cultivation. This study emphasizes that PMFCs have the potential to be a global warming solution, especially given that rice cultivation is one of the country's key sectors.
W7221727623.title: Stacking Efficiency of Oryza sativa Plant Microbial Fuel Cells in Paddy Fields: Power Generation and Methane Reduction as Measures for Greener Technology

W7221735745.abstract: In the present study nanocomposites based on biodegradable polymers, namely poly(lactic acid) (PLA) and polycaprolactone (PCL), were developed and characterised. Various nanofillers, such as graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) with different geometrical characteristics, multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) and organically modified nanoclays (NCs), were incorporated into PLA and PCL through dry mixing of both phases in powder form. Subsequently, melt compounding in a single-screw extrusion system took place, where the produced materials were processed into filaments, and finally into specimens by fused filament fabrication (FFF). The effect of nanofiller type and concentration on the mechanical, thermal and morphological properties of the resulting materials was then evaluated. Mechanical performance was assessed through tensile testing according to EN ISO 527-1, while differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was employed to investigate the thermal transitions, crystallization behaviour and melting characteristics of the neat polymers and their nanocomposites. Furthermore, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to examine the fracture surface morphology. The results demonstrated that the incorporation of nanofillers can modify the mechanical and thermal response of the biodegradable polymers, with the magnitude and nature of these changes depending strongly on the filler type, concentration and morphology. Among the investigated systems, PLA containing 0.3 wt.% GNP H5, exhibited the most significant improvements in tensile strength (TS), Young’s modulus (E) and strain at break (EAB), which increased by 25.2%, 22.1% and 28.4%, respectively, compared with neat PLA. In the case of PCL, the same nanofiller and concentration increased the yield strength (YS) and Young’s modulus by 29.8% and 29.0%, respectively. The incorporation of GNP H5 did not significantly affect the thermal transitions of PLA, as only minor changes were observed in the glass transition, cold crystallization, and melting temperatures. Similarly, the addition of the same nanomaterial to PCL did not result in any notable change in its melting temperature. Last but not least, for the system exhibiting the most favourable overall mechanical performance, namely PLA reinforced with 0.3 wt.% GNPs, SEM analysis of the fracture surfaces revealed evidence of folding of the graphene nanoplatelets and pull-out from the polymer matrix. These features suggest the activation of additional energy-dissipation mechanisms during fracture.

W7221754289.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the flexural performance and failure mechanisms of additively manufactured sandwich panels featuring 3D-printed corrugated cores and face sheets reinforced with E-glass fibers. The research aims to quantify the effects of core geometry, thermoplastic matrix selection and fiber reinforcement on peak load, stiffness and energy absorption, while critically evaluating the predictive accuracy of classical Gibson–Ashby models for extrusion-based composites. Design/methodology/approach Sandwich panels were fabricated using a modified dual-feed fused deposition modeling (FDM) process. To mitigate nozzle wear and facilitate the extrusion process, 100-tex continuous E-glass yarns were pre-coated with a styrene-butadiene rubber solution. Eight distinct sample configurations were produced and evaluated, utilizing two thermoplastic matrices (polylactic acid [PLA] and acrylonitrile butadiene styrene [ABS]) across three core cross-sections: rectangular, triangular and trapezoidal. These included both unreinforced polymer panels and continuous fiber-reinforced composites containing a ∼15% fiber volume fraction. Specimens were subjected to three-point bending tests in accordance with ASTM C393. Findings Experimental results demonstrated that structural performance is highly dictated by core geometry and matrix integrity. The trapezoidal composite panel (TRCP) achieved the highest peak flexural load (726.8 N) with stable post-peak progressive collapse. The rectangular composite panel (RCP) exhibited superior ductility and the highest specific energy absorption (SEA) at 118.9 N·mm/g due to progressive core wall buckling, dramatically outperforming the triangular core panel, which suffered a brittle, premature collapse at 558.8 N with an SEA of only 12.5 N·mm/g. Regarding matrix selection, PLA-based panels significantly outperformed their ABS counterparts (e.g. RCP peak load of 706.3 N versus RCA at 448.8 N) due to ABS’s susceptibility to severe intra-face layer delamination under compressive bending loads. Furthermore, the addition of continuous glass fibers improved the peak load by ∼19% and SEA by ∼24% compared to unreinforced PLA equivalents (RPP). Furthermore, while classical Gibson–Ashby theory predicted global core shear failure due to the high face-thickness-to-span ratio (t/L = 0.022), experimental observations revealed premature localized face indentation. Quantitative analysis confirmed that the printed cores only utilized 13% to 83% of their theoretical shear capacities, highlighting the critical limitations of applying continuous-foundation analytical models to discrete 3D-printed corrugated topologies. Originality/value This research provides robust quantitative benchmarking for continuous glass-fiber FDM sandwich structures. It demonstrates that classical sandwich theories require adjustment before application to 3D-printed composites, as they fail to account for real-world discrete support conditions, epoxy interface compliance and localized post-buckling behaviors. The findings offer vital, application-specific design guidelines for the geometric optimization of additively manufactured lightweight structures.
W7221754289.title: Flexural performance and failure mechanisms of 3D-printed corrugated-core sandwich panels reinforced with glass fibers

W7221774415.abstract: This work investigates the recovery of H 2 from gas streams generated during plastic waste pyrolytic valorization using a dual-layer vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA) process packed with activated carbon and zeolite 5A. The influence of adsorption pressure, time and regeneration strategy (purge or vacuum) on H 2 separation performance was systematically evaluated through a design of experiments (DoE) combined with response surface methodology (RSM). The results demonstrate the characteristic purity-recovery trade-off of PSA processes, while the developed RSM models accurately represented the experimental results (R 2 > 0.99) and were subsequently used to optimize the process for H 2 purity targets of 98.000 and 99.999 vol%. Furthermore, the optimized conditions were applied to gas streams derived from pyrolysis & steam reforming of polypropylene (PP), high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET), achieved H 2 recoveries up to 96.9 and 75.9% while producing H 2 suitable for industrial and ultra-high-purity applications respectively, highlighting the potential of VPSA technology for H 2 recovery from plastic waste valorization gases.
W7221774415.title: Hydrogen purification from plastic waste valorization streams using vacuum pressure swing adsorption

W7221777986.abstract: ABSTRACT Natural fiber‐reinforced bioplastics represent a viable strategy for valorizing agricultural waste; however, the combined reinforcement of lontar palm ( Borassus flabellifer ) leaf and sugarcane bagasse fibers in a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix remains underexplored. This study investigates the effects of varying PVA concentrations (15, 30, and 45 wt%) on the physical, mechanical, thermal, and interfacial properties of hybrid biocomposite films. Extracted cellulose fibers served as structural reinforcement. Tensile strength increased with higher PVA loading, peaking at 1.79 MPa at 45 wt% PVA, while elongation reached an optimal 43.36% at 30 wt.% PVA. Physical characterization revealed a maximum swelling of 70.3% at 45 wt.% PVA, whereas water solubility decreased from 63.54% at 15 wt.% PVA to a minimum of 55.30% at 45 wt.% PVA. The 45 wt.% formulation also exhibited superior structural and thermal stability, showing the lowest soil‐burial degradation (36.80%) and minimal heat‐induced weight loss (8.99% at 120°C). Spectroscopic analyses confirmed robust interfacial bonding via hydrogen linkages (3500–3200 cm − 1 ) and prominent C─O/C─O─C vibrations (1200–1000 cm − 1 ) between the cellulose fillers and polymer chains. Overall, balancing PVA concentration with hybrid fiber reinforcement is critical to tailoring mechanical strength, water affinity, and degradation resistance in biodegradable films
W7221777986.title: Influence of PVA Concentration on the Properties of Lontar Palm Leaf‐Sugarcane Bagasse Hybrid Biocomposite Films

W7221779507.abstract: Abstract Consumer awareness of bioplastic packaging is gaining significance in Bangladesh's journey towards a circular economy due to the rising amount of plastic waste generated by packaging and the scarcity of end-of-life infrastructure. This study explores the factors that influence willingness to pay a premium (WPP) for bioplastic packaging, and the intervening effect of green purchase intention (GPI) on this relationship. The study is based on cross-sectional survey data of 208 consumers in urban Bangladesh, and employs a hierarchical multiple regression analysis with heteroscedasticity-consistent robust standard errors. Bioplastic lifecycle literacy proved to be the most consistent and strongest predictor of WPP (Willingness to Pay Premium), whereas environmental concern was positively correlated with WPP (Willingness to Pay Premium) but the relationship was greatly reduced after the inclusion of GPI (Green Purchase Intention), suggesting partial mediation and an attitude–behaviour gap. GPI (Green Purchase Intention) was a significant predictor of WPP (Willingness to Pay Premium), while perceived consumer effectiveness and perceived greenwashing risk were not significant. The visual attractiveness of packaging was found to have a significant positive direct effect on WPP (Willingness to Pay Premium), but did not moderate the relationship between GPI (Green Purchase Intention) and WPP (Willingness to Pay Premium). The results highlight the need to provide clear and lifecycle-specific sustainability information and also to keep a credible and premium packaging proposition in Bangladesh.
W7221779507.title: Consumer Purchase Intention and the Packaging Lifecycle: Evaluating End-of-Life Literacy for Bioplastics in Bangladesh

W7221801415.abstract: Polylactic acid (PLA), a biopolymer derived from bio-based monomers, has attracted considerable attention in fused deposition modeling (FDM) because of its good printability, dimensional stability, and potential for sustainable polymer applications. This study experimentally, theoretically, and numerically investigates the tensile fracture of U-notched and blunt V-notched (BV-notched) diagonally loaded square plate (DLSP) specimens FDM-printed from PLA. To assess the effects of filament architecture and notch geometry, two raster configurations, called cross-ply [0/90] s and quasi-isotropic [0/90/+45/−45] s , and three notch-root radii of 1, 2, and 4 mm are considered. The virtual isotropic material concept (VIMC) is employed to indirectly account for printing-induced anisotropy, while the equivalent material concept (EMC) or modified equivalent material concept (MEMC) is combined with VIMC according to the nonlinear response of each raster configuration. Fracture loads are predicted using the stress-based maximum tangential stress (MTS) and mean stress (MS) criteria, the energy-based averaged strain energy density (ASED) criterion, and the cohesive zone model implemented through the extended finite element method (CZM-XFEM). Incorporating EMC improves the predictions for the cross-ply specimens: VIMC-EMC-ASED provides the best results for the U-notched specimens, with an average absolute discrepancy of 5.6%, whereas VIMC-EMC-MS is the most accurate for the BV-notched specimens, with a discrepancy of 4.5%. For the quasi-isotropic specimens, MEMC produces a more pronounced improvement, and VIMC-MEMC-MS yields the most accurate predictions for both U- and BV-notched specimens, with average absolute discrepancies of 3.6% and 1.7%, respectively. Overall, the proposed simplified framework efficiently predicts the fracture loads of notched FDM-printed PLA components while accounting for printing-induced anisotropy and nonlinear material behavior. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is also used to examine the fracture-surface morphology and dominant fracture micro-mechanisms. The observations show that the quasi-isotropic configuration provides slightly greater energy dissipation before final failure than the cross-ply configuration, consistent with the slightly higher fracture loads measured for geometrically similar quasi-isotropic specimens.
W7221801415.title: Tensile fracture analysis of FDM-printed polylactic acid notched plates using simplified material concepts: Effects of raster configuration

W7221817066.abstract: ABSTRACT Chitosan is a promising alternative to petroleum-based plastics. However, their limiting mechanical and barrier properties have made its chemical modification a spot of interest nowadays. This work evaluates the effect of different degrees of octenyl succinic anhydride (OSA) modification, including single- and two-step functionalization, on the physicochemical properties of chitosan and its behaviour during compression moulding. FTIR analysis confirmed the successful grafting of OSA onto both amino and hydroxyl groups, achieving degree of substitution (DS) values ranging from 0.124 to 0.585, which resulted in changes in the internal molecular organization observed by XRD. These structural rearrangements contributed to matrix free volume and increased chain mobility, which led to improved thermo-mechanical processability and enabled the production of uniform and flexible films. Films prepared from single-step OSA-modified chitosan exhibited enhanced mechanical performance compared to native chitosan, with tensile strength increasing from 20.68 to 36.42 MPa and elongation at break from 5.36 to 11.48%. In contrast, two-step OSA-modified samples displayed higher elasticity (up to 34.05%) but significantly reduced tensile strength (13.28-14.32 MPa), indicating that high degrees of modification lead to an excessive plasticization and decreased matrix cohesion. Moreover, OSA modification improved water vapour barrier properties by up to 67% compared to native chitosan, attributed to the hydrophobic character of the alkenyl side chains. Overall, the combination of OSA modification and compression moulding represents a feasible strategy for the scalable production of chitosan-based bioplastics suitable for food packaging applications.
W7221817066.title: Characterization of single-step and two-step OSA-modified chitosan and performance of thermo-compression moulded films
