W7221827595.abstract: This study describes the development of a multifunctional coating designed to enhance the antibacterial and photoprotective properties of 3D-printed Polylactic Acid (PLA). The strategy involves the synthesis of a β-cyclodextrin polymer (P-βCD) covalently functionalized with kojic acid (K) via a green aqueous-based process, followed by the supramolecular inclusion of xanthopterin (X) to yield the P-βCD-K-X complex. Structural confirmation was achieved through 1 H NMR, UV, and IR spectroscopy, while SEM analysis revealed a densely packed, particulate surface morphology. Broth microdilution assays demonstrated a stepwise functional enhancement, achieving a low minimum inhibitory concentration against Staphylococcus aureus (MIC = 0.18 mg/mL) and extending activity toward Gram-negative strains such as Klebsiella pneumoniae (MIC = 0.375 mg/mL) and Escherichia coli (MIC = 1.5 mg/mL). Surface-contact assays on coated PLA (5 mg/mL) revealed rapid antibacterial activity, achieving 88% bacterial inhibition within 5 min of contact and total bacterial suppression below the limit of detection (<100 CFU/mL) after 24 h. In vitro assays confirmed high cell viability (≥80%) in A549 cells across concentrations of 0.37–3.0 mg/mL. Optical characterization showed that coatings obtained from 5 to 10 mg/mL formulations lowered UV transmittance down to ≈1% near 350 nm and significantly boosted the Ultraviolet Protection Factor (UPF) of PLA from 9.2 (pristine PLA) up to 26.5 (10 mg/mL formulation), providing an “Very Good Protection” rating (BS EN 13758-1) by attenuating over 96% of harmful solar UV radiation. During accelerated weathering tests (96 h), while neat PLA photo-oxidized significantly (Carbonyl Index increased from 2.74 to 4.10), the functional coating prevented any net increase in surface oxidation (ΔCI = 0.00, maintaining a stable Carbonyl Index of 2.15). These quantitative findings highlight the potential of functionalized cyclodextrin polymers for engineering advanced, durable, and biocompatible antibacterial and photoprotective surface coatings.
W7221827595.title: Xanthopterin-loaded kojic acid–functionalized β-cyclodextrin polymer coatings for UV shielding and antibacterial functionalization of 3D-printed PLA

W7221830271.abstract: The increasing use of biopolymer derivatives raises concerns about their actual environmental sustainability, which remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we adopted an integrated approach combining microbial and ecotoxicological perspectives to evaluate their impact in marine ecosystems. We investigated the plastisphere composition of conventional petroleum-based High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA), polyhydroxybutyric acid (PHB), and polylactic acid (PLLA) scaffolds after 60 days of exposition in marine ecosystem or microcosm, by high throughput metagenomics 16S rRNA gene sequencing and culture dependent approach. A variation in terms of composition and abundance of plastisphere, between petroleum-derived and bio-based degradable scaffolds, was observed. A high abundance of Proteobacteria was detected in all polymers, with Alpha and Gamma Proteobacteria dominant. At the genera level, high abundance of sequences assigned to hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria (i.e. Oleibacter, Labrenzia, Alcanivorax) was detected in biopolymeric plastic compared to petroleum-based plastic. To link microbial colonization and material degradation with biological effects on marine fauna, the impact of biopolymer-derived micro- and nanoparticles on the mussel Mytilus galloprovincialis was assessed. Both in vitro and in vivo assays demonstrated immune system activation through phagocytosis and encapsulation, while in vivo exposures influenced several biomarkers (phagocytosis, haemocyte density, lysozyme, glutathione peroxidase, phenoloxidase, alkaline phosphatase, esterase), suggesting potential detrimental effects after 72 h. By bridging microbial ecology with immunological responses in a bioindicator species, this multidisciplinary study provides novel insights into the complex ecological footprint of biodegradable plastics in marine environments.
W7221830271.title: Integrated assessment of bioplastic materials effects on microbial communities and macroinvertebrate model, Mytilus galloprovincialis, in marine ecosystems

W7221831889.abstract: Multilayer coating technologies offer a promising strategy to enhance the performance of bio-based food packaging materials. In this study, active multilayer materials composed of six alternating layers of chitosan and cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) were developed on polylactic acid (PLA) films using two coating techniques: ultrasonic spray coating (USC) and dipping. The aim was to evaluate how the coating deposition method influences the multilayer structure formation and, consequently, the physicochemical, barrier, functional, and safety properties of the resulting films. The results showed that the coating technique strongly affected film morphology. USC produced a droplet-like deposition pattern that encouraged the formation of small chitosan/CNC aggregates, while dipping produced more homogeneous but less defined multilayer structures. These differences significantly affected film performance, with USC-coated films showing superior barrier properties, decreasing water vapour permeability by 99.76% and reducing gas permeability by up to 65%. CNC migration was evaluated according to European food contact regulations using different food simulants, with values ranging from 0.03 mg/kg in isooctane to 1 mg/kg in 3% acetic acid, providing one of the first insights into the specific migration behaviour of cellulose nanocrystals in food simulants. Safety evaluation was performed using Caco-2 human intestinal cells, including cytotoxicity (resazurin assay) and genotoxicity (alkaline comet assay), which confirmed no adverse biological effects at the tested concentrations. Finally, the active multilayer packaging was tested on cheese, showing reduced yeast growth and extended shelf-life to 29 days at 4 °C, with a modest reduction in yeast growth compared to commercial packaging due to its lower gas permeability. Overall, the results demonstrate that coating-induced multilayer architecture plays a critical role in determining the functional performance of PLA-coated films, highlighting the potential of USC as an effective technique for developing active bio-based food packaging.
W7221831889.title: Chitosan/cellulose nanocrystal multilayer coatings on PLA films: Influence of deposition method on barrier properties, migration behaviour and active food packaging performance

W7221833425.abstract: Inter-raster voids formed during fused deposition modelling (FDM) printing are among the primary microstructural features governing the directional elastic behavior of unidirectional printed parts. In the present work, a measurement-driven representative volume element (RVE) homogenization framework is developed to predict the elastic constants of FDM-printed polylactic acid (PLA) under a 0° raster configuration as a function of two key process parameters: layer height and material flow rate. A full factorial design of experiments (DoE) is conducted, and cross-sectional microscopy images at each design point are analyzed to extract void fraction, void base width, and void height. A curvilinear triangle void model is fitted to the measurements, and response surfaces are calibrated from the DoE points, enabling complete void geometry prediction for new process parameter combinations. The homogenization pipeline is verified against two independent implementations from the literature, with Young's moduli agreeing within 3.7%, shear moduli within 5.3%, and Poisson ratios within 6.2%. The through-thickness modulus E 3 is identified as the dominant process-sensitive constant, ranging from 2176 to 3146 MPa across the design space, governed primarily by layer height, while E 1 remains nearly constant at 3119–3331 MPa. Poisson ratios are found essentially insensitive to process parameters. Framework predictions are validated numerically against RVE homogenization results at four hold-out design points, with deviations within 2.1%. Experimental validation of the three orthotropic Young's moduli is further carried out through tensile tests at the same points, with values consistently below predictions by up to 12.5% across all directions and process conditions.
W7221833425.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part L Journal of Materials Design and Applications
W7221833425.title: RVE homogenization of fused deposition modeling (FDM) printed parts: From microscale void characterization to elastic property prediction

W7221835740.abstract: Cupriavidus necator H16 was found capable of using crude fish oil and waste cooking oil as main carbon sources for poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) production. In this study, the biosynthesis of value-added polyhydroxyalkanoate copolymer by C. necator H16 was investigated. Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-4-hydroxybutyrate) [P(3HB-co-4HB)] was synthesized when γ-butyrolactone was added as a precursor to the culture medium; however, the content of the 4HB fraction in copolymer P(3HB-co-4HB) was low. The biosynthesis of poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) [P(3HB-co-3HV)] was achieved by adding sodium propionate to the culture medium. P(3HB-co-3HV) containing 1.6 to 10.9 mol% 3HV fraction (in case of crude fish oil) and 1.2 to 11.5 mol% 3HV fraction (in case of waste cooking oil) was accumulated when supplemented propionate concentrations increased from 1 to 5 g/L. This study demonstrates the side-by-side production of P(3HB-co-4HB) and P(3HB-co-3HV) from crude fish oil and waste cooking oil by Cupriavidus necator H16. We establish a dose–response trade-off between precursor level, copolymer composition (4HB/3HV), and productivity (CDW, PHA%), thereby defining a practical operating window for composition-tunable PHAs from waste lipids.
W7221835740.journal: VNU Journal of Science Natural Sciences and Technology
W7221835740.title: Biosynthesis of polyhydroxyalkanoate copolymer by Cupriavidus necator H16 using γ-butyrolactone and sodium propionate as precursors

W7221854039.abstract: Microencapsulated beadlets are versatile multiparticulate drug delivery systems designed to incorporate active pharmaceutical ingredients within polymeric matrices, core–shell structures, or functional coatings to achieve improved stability and controlled drug release. These systems combine the advantages of microencapsulation with the flexibility of multiparticulate dosage forms and can be formulated to provide immediate, sustained, delayed, pulsatile, biphasic, or site-specific drug delivery. The present review provides a comprehensive overview of the formulation strategies, preparation techniques, characterization, evaluation, and pharmaceutical applications of microencapsulated beadlets. Various manufacturing methods, including solvent evaporation, coacervation-phase separation, fluid-bed coating, extrusion–spheronization, ionotropic gelation, spray drying, spray congealing, melt-based processes, microfluidics, and electrohydrodynamic atomization, are discussed. Particular emphasis is given to the selection and role of natural, semi-synthetic, synthetic, and biodegradable polymers in controlling drug loading, encapsulation efficiency, particle morphology, mechanical strength, and release behavior. Critical quality attributes, including particle size, size distribution, sphericity, surface morphology, density, porosity, drug content, encapsulation efficiency, swelling behavior, drug–polymer compatibility, solid-state properties, and in vitro drug release, are reviewed. Drug release mechanisms involving diffusion, swelling, erosion, dissolution, pore-mediated transport, and polymer degradation are also examined. Microencapsulated beadlets offer significant advantages, including improved patient compliance, flexible dosing, reduced dosing frequency, enhanced stability, taste masking, and the ability to combine different release profiles within a single dosage form. Despite challenges related to manufacturing reproducibility, scale-up, coating uniformity, and process control, emerging technologies such as quality-by-design, continuous manufacturing, advanced polymeric materials, and microfluidics are expected to further enhance their pharmaceutical applications. Keywords: Microencapsulation; beadlets; microbeads; microspheres; multiparticulate drug delivery; controlled release.
W7221854039.journal: Journal of Drug Delivery and Therapeutics
W7221854039.title: Microencapsulated Beadlets: A Comprehensive Review

W7221861040.abstract: ABSTRACT The accumulation of non‐biodegradable plastics is driving the search for environmentally friendly, low‐cost alternatives. This study investigated the production of biodegradable bioplastics using starch extracted from Ipomoea batatas and Manihot esculenta tubers. The tubers were pulverized, and starch was extracted. Bioplastic was produced by reacting the starch with ethanoic, methanoic, and propanoic acids in the presence of glycerol and water at 80°C for 25 min. The starch yield and the physicochemical, mechanical, and degradability properties of the bioplastics were determined. The results showed starch yields (57.5%; 52.26%), moisture content (12.38%; 13.74%), pH (6.9; 6.7), amylose content (20.4%; 20.67%) and amylopectin content (79.6%; 80.2%) for Ipomoea batatas and Manihot esculenta tubers, respectively. The mass of bioplastic produced was directly proportional to starch content and the number of carbon chains present in the organic acid. The mechanical properties showed that tensile strength was significantly ( p < 0.05) higher than that of the control, except for the 15 g bioplastic produced. Shear strength also showed a trend similar to tensile strength. The elongation/break properties significantly ( p < 0.05) increased in the methanoic acid‐derived bioplastic. The bioplastic degradation rates were (0.0059, 0.0056 and 0.0043 mg/ml/h) for Ipomoea batatas and (0.0099, 0.0098 and 0.0091 mg/ml/h) for Manihot esculenta‐derived biodegradable plastic, respectively , using Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The results of this study show that starches from Ipomoea batata and Manihot esculenta tubers could be a good source for bioplastic production because they are inexpensive, renewable, and readily biodegradable when disposed of in the environment.
W7221861040.title: The Production, Characterization, and Biodegradation Kinetics of Bioplastics From Starch Extracted From Ipomoea batatas and Manihot esculenta Tubers

W7221865336.abstract: Understanding snap-through instability and dynamic behavior is vital for designing lightweight, damage-tolerant components and preventing catastrophic failure in structural applications. This study presents a comprehensive analytical, experimental, as well as numerical investigation of the nonlinear snap-through instability and dynamic behavior of 3D-printed architected sandwich spherical meta-shells with bamboo fiber-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) composite face-sheets. The proposed structure combines lightweight architected star-shaped cellular cores with sustainable bio-composite face-sheets to achieve enhanced stiffness, stability, and vibration performance. Using Hamilton’s principle, a nonlinear shell model is established within the framework of the First-Order Shear Deformation Theory (FSDT), while geometric nonlinearity is represented through the von-Kármán formulation. The governing equations are solved through the Ritz method employing Chebyshev polynomial expansion, while the cylindrical arc-length technique is adopted to accurately trace complex snap-through equilibrium paths. The present work investigates the influence of two practically important loading conditions, namely concentrated loading (CL) and uniformly distributed loading (UDL), on the nonlinear snap-through response of architected spherical meta-shells. The analytical model is first verified against benchmark solutions available in the literature. Additionally, a 3D finite element model is developed to capture the true physical dynamic behavior of the complex architected geometry, which is evaluated experimentally through impact hammer modal testing on a baseline pure PLA fused deposition modeling (FDM)-fabricated specimen. Following these evaluations, an extensive parametric study is carried out to examine the influence of shell geometry, architected core characteristics, thickness ratio, fiber volume fraction, loading scenarios, and support conditions on nonlinear vibration and snap-through responses. The developed bio-inspired architected sandwich meta-shells offer an efficient lightweight alternative for multifunctional structural systems that demand enhanced stability, excellent energy absorption, and outstanding dynamic performance.
W7221865336.title: 3D-printed architected sandwich spherical meta-shells with bamboo fiber reinforced PLA composite face-sheets: Snap-through instability and dynamic performance

W7221866532.abstract: This work is focused on the development of structured Pd-Ni catalysts for the continuous hydrodehalogenation (HDH) of diclofenac (DCF). Bimetallic Pd-Ni nanoparticles (NP) were synthesized, fully characterized and tested on HDH reaction, revealing a pronounced synergistic effect. Remarkably, PdNi_5050 maintained the catalytic activity of monometallic Pd while reducing noble metal content by 50%. These selected NPs were immobilized onto different polymeric supports, a 3D-printable polylactic acid (PLA) support and a high-density polyethylene (HDPE) membrane. The PdNi@PLA system clearly outperformed PdNi@HDPE due to the superior active site accessibility, attributed to the open helical morphology of the PLA support. Kinetic studies indicated a preferential reaction pathway toward the non-chlorinated product, thereby minimizing the formation of toxic byproducts. As a proof of concept, the optimized system was evaluated under continuous long-term operation, achieving a high and stable DCF conversion (~90%) over 80 h on stream. These results highlight the potential of the proposed system as a scalable, sustainable, and economically attractive solution for continuous-flow HDH
W7221866532.title: Structured Pd–Ni polymeric catalysts for cost-efficient continuous hydrodehalogenation

W7221900150.abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer films composed of biodegradable polymers containing lignocellulosic fillers have been identified as good candidates for substitution for conventional petroleum‐derived packaging materials. In the current study, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) biofilms containing 5–25 wt% alkali‐treated Sapindus mukorossi shell filler (at. SMSF) were synthesized through the solution casting method. The objective of this study is to explore the structure of PVA biofilms, thermal behavior, mechanical behavior, optical, surface, and antibacterial properties. The removal of amorphous parts through alkali treatment exposed cellulose‐filled microfibrils, resulting in the development of strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds with the PVA matrix. FTIR showed improvement in interfacial compatibility without the creation of any new chemical bond. On the other hand, XRD analysis depicted an increase in crystallinity from 32.5% to 54.8% and crystallite size from 18.2 to 31.3 nm. Thermal analysis proved that the biofilms exhibited good thermal stability and high degradation temperatures, along with a reduction in heat flow and an increase in char formation. SEM and surface roughness analysis depicted uniform dispersion of fillers and compact morphology, especially in the case of medium loading of fillers. There was significant enhancement in mechanical properties, where tensile strength and Young's modulus increased from 23.5 to 46.8 MPa and from 29.5 to 62.3 MPa, respectively. The contact angle of water increased from 51.3° to 92.5°, showing remarkable improvement in water repellence. Moreover, PVA/25 wt% at. SMSF showed significant UV‐blocking efficiency and very good antibacterial properties toward Escherichia coli and Bacillus cereus . The results showed that alkaline‐treated SMSF can be a very good bio‐component to develop mechanically tough, thermally stable, moisture‐resistant, and antibacterial PVA biofilm for use as a packaging material.
W7221900150.journal: Journal of Vinyl and Additive Technology
W7221900150.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Poly (Vinyl Alcohol) Biofilms Reinforced With Alkali‐Treated Sapindus mukorossi Shell Filler

W7221908721.abstract: Spirulina, scientifically classified as Arthrospira platensis, is a filamentous cyanobacterium widely recognized for its exceptional nutritional value and diverse biological properties. It is a rich source of proteins, essential amino acids, polyunsaturated fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, carotenoids, phenolic compounds, polysaccharides, and phycobiliproteins, particularly C-phycocyanin. The present review provides a comprehensive overview of the taxonomy, morphology, geographical distribution, cultivation systems, phytochemical composition, nutritional properties, pharmacological activities, and potential applications of Spirulina. Several bioactive constituents of Spirulina contribute to its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, anticancer, antiviral, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, hypolipidemic, anti-obesity, hepatoprotective, nephroprotective, neuroprotective, and radioprotective activities. C-phycocyanin and phycocyanobilin play important roles in scavenging reactive oxygen species and modulating oxidative and inflammatory pathways, while other bioactive compounds contribute to metabolic regulation and cellular protection. Evidence from preclinical and clinical studies indicates the potential of Spirulina as a nutraceutical and functional food for supporting human health and preventing various chronic disorders. In addition, its high protein content and digestibility make it a promising alternative protein source in aquaculture, where it can partially replace fishmeal and improve growth, feed utilization, and disease resistance. Spirulina also has emerging applications in food technology, environmental bioremediation, bioplastics, biofuels, and other biotechnological fields. Overall, the diverse nutritional, pharmacological, environmental, and industrial properties of Arthrospira platensis highlight its potential as a multifunctional natural resource with promising applications in health, food, feed, and biotechnology.
W7221908721.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
W7221908721.title: ARTHROSPIRA PLATENSIS: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW ON RECENT ADVANCES IN THE BIOLOGICAL ACTIVITIES OF SPIRULINA

W7221955161.abstract: Breast cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Although doxorubicin is widely used in chemotherapy, its clinical application is limited by cardiotoxicity, systemic toxicity, and non-specific drug distribution. pH-responsive polymeric nanoparticles offer a promising approach for targeted drug delivery by releasing doxorubicin in the acidic tumor microenvironment while maintaining stability under physiological conditions. Biodegradable polymers, including PLGA, PEG, chitosan, and poly(β-amino esters), have been investigated for developing these nanocarriers. Preclinical studies indicate improved intracellular drug delivery, enhanced antitumor activity, and potential reductions in systemic toxicity. This review highlights recent advances in the design, development, and therapeutic applications of pH-responsive polymeric nanoparticles for doxorubicin delivery in breast cancer, along with challenges in safety, clinical translation, and regulatory approval. These systems hold considerable potential for improving targeted cancer therapy.
W7221955161.journal: Open Access Research Journal of Biology and Pharmacy
W7221955161.title: Development of pH-Responsive Polymeric Nanoparticles for Targeted Doxorubicin Delivery in Breast Cancer: Advances, Design Strategies, and Future Perspectives

W7221982889.title: Interlocking modular assembly for scalable composite metamaterials with intrinsic self-sensing capability

W7222010916.abstract: Multi-material fused-filament fabrication (FFF) enables the integration of two or more materials within a single printed component, offering significant potential for producing functionally graded and hybrid structures with tailored mechanical properties. However, the effects of processing conditions on interfacial quality and fracture behavior in multi-material FFF remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the Mode-I interfacial fracture behavior of multi-material FFF using compact-tension (CT) specimens through combined experimental testing and finite-element simulation. CT specimens were fabricated from polylactic acid (PLA), thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), and polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG) using five raster configurations, including rectilinear 0°/90°, ±45° and aligned-rectilinear 0°, 45°, 90° configurations. The load-extension response, peak load (Pmax), critical stress-intensity factor (KIC), and critical strain-energy release rate (GIC) were evaluated. Two-way ANOVA showed that material pairing was the dominant statistically significant factor affecting peak load, whereas raster orientation and its interaction with material pairing were not statistically significant. The PETG–TPU interface exhibited the highest fracture resistance, with the AR-45 orientation producing an average Pmax of 130.90 N, KIC of 0.761 MPam, and GIC of 375.5 N/m. Fracture-surface observations supported these findings, revealing greater deformation, material transfer, surface roughness, and mechanical interlocking in the PETG–TPU specimens. The calibrated cohesive-zone model demonstrated the stress contours and the localized interfacial damage patterns. Overall, material pairing primarily governed interfacial fracture resistance, whereas raster orientation showed no statistically significant effect under the tested conditions.
W7222010916.title: Experimental and Numerical Investigation of the Interfacial Bonding in Multi-Material Fused-Filament Fabrication Using Mode-I Fracture Toughness

W7222109314.abstract: This study evaluates processing via fused granulate fabrication (FGF) of nanocomposites based on virgin polylactic acid (PLA) and thermomechanically reprocessed polylactic acid (rPLA), incorporated with 0 wt%, 5 wt%, and 10 wt% of silicon dioxide (SiO2) nanoparticles. Rheological analysis revealed that rPLA exhibited a 42.4 % increase in melt flow rate compared to PLA, which can be attributed to thermomechanical chain scission occurring during reprocessing. At 10 wt% filler loading, the tensile strength along the XZ build direction tended to decrease. Scanning electron microscopy analysis suggests that this trend is related to nanoparticle agglomeration. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that adding 5–10 wt% SiO2 restored the lower initial thermal degradation onset of rPLA (T5%loss=313°C) to values equal to or exceeding PLA (323–324°C), while overall crystallinity remained near 0% owing to rapid convective cooling during FGF printing. Short-term soil respirometry trials using extruded granule samples revealed that rPLA exerted a temporary respirometric inhibition, reducing soil basal respiration by 22.5%. The incorporation of 10 wt% SiO2 recovered 96.3% of the native soil metabolic activity by increasing extruded granules surface wettability and water availability at the particle interface. These findings demonstrate that the control of SiO2 loading enables the tuning of mechanical performance, establishing a framework for sustainable, large-format PLA components with tailored end-of-life properties.
W7222109314.journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
W7222109314.title: Fused Granulate Fabrication of Virgin and Reprocessed PLA/Silicon Dioxide Nanocomposites: Processing, Mechanical Integrity, and Soil Microbial Respiration Response

W7222117144.abstract: Dimensional accuracy in material-extrusion polymer additive manufacturing depends on feature geometry and process settings. This study evaluates a replicated, feature-resolved framework for polylactic acid (PLA) benchmark parts. A Taguchi L9 design varied layer height, print speed, and nozzle temperature across 45 independent builds, yielding 1575 measurements of 35 components across 16 features. Analyses combined build-level uncertainty, additive models, bootstrap intervals, exhaustive residual-permutation sensitivity, and clustered tolerance models. Inclined-surface roughness was summarized from five specimen means per condition. Mean absolute error (MAE) ranged from 0.0773 to 0.1263 mm. Layer height accounted for 91.8% of the decomposed condition-mean MAE variation (95% bootstrap interval: 90.0–93.2%). The additive-model effect had a Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.001; the nine-condition sensitivity analysis gave p = 0.093. Compliance odds ratios at ±0.10 mm were 0.51 and 0.32 for 0.2 and 0.3 mm layers relative to 0.1 mm. Nominally dominant factors persisted after dimension normalization. Dimensional utility, including slicer-estimated time, selected R2 (0.1 mm, 50 mm/s, 210 °C), while roughness-inclusive preferences made R1 competitive. Feature-specific tolerances and build-level uncertainty support process selection within the investigated PLA window.
W7222117144.title: Geometry-Dependent Process Sensitivity and Tolerance Compliance in Material-Extrusion Polymer Additive Manufacturing: A Replicated Feature-Resolved Study

W7222147283.abstract: Biodegradable polymer-based microneedle (MN) patches enable self-administered, long-acting drug delivery. Controlled drug release from MNs requires controlled material distribution and minimal porosity in the MNs. MN detachment in the skin requires MNs without film formation beyond the MN base. To achieve these goals, we studied solvent removal dynamics during MN patch fabrication by a solvent-casting method to better control distribution of polymer and drug in the MN patch mold. More specifically, we designed casting solvents to control (i) solvent evaporation rate, (ii) solvent absorption rate into polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) molds, and (iii) solubility of biodegradable polymer (poly (lactic acid)) and drug (etonogestrel, for long-acting contraception) in the solvent. We found that polymer film formation was prevented by using solvents with minimal mold absorption and moderate evaporation rates. We further demonstrated that solvent-nonsolvent mixtures titrated to the solubility limit of the polymer and beyond the solubility limit of the drug (forming a suspension of fine precipitate) also produced MNs without films. This occurred even when using solvents that absorbed into the molds. To better achieve sustained drug release, we showed that centrifuge-based casting and heat annealing reduced surface and bulk MN porosity. The resulting MNs achieved efficient detachment in porcine skin and sustained release of etonogestrel for two months in-vitro. This study establishes a framework to control solvent removal dynamics during MN patch fabrication to optimize biodegradable polymer MNs for long-acting delivery of etonogestrel and other drugs.
W7222147283.title: Controlled solvent removal dynamics during fabrication of microneedle patches for the sustained release of etonogestrel

W7222150585.abstract: Biodegradable mulch films are recognized as promising eco-friendly alternatives, yet their high costs and uncertain field performance constrain adoption. Systematic cost–benefit comparisons with traditional polyethylene films across thickness gradients remain limited. This study compared white and black low-density polyethylene (LDPE) films (0.006–0.015 mm; the 0.015 mm film in 2023 only), biodegradable Polylactic Acid/Polybutylene Adipate Terephthalate (PLA/PBAT) films (0.008 mm in all years and 0.010 mm in 2024) and a bare-soil control in a three-year (2022–2024) randomized complete block trial with three replicates on peanut in Shandong, China. Field experiments were conducted. Peanut yield and quality, economic inputs and returns, and visible mulch residue and recovery were comprehensively evaluated using the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) and Data envelopment analysis (DEA). Microplastics were not directly quantified; therefore, environmental assessment was based on visible residual film mass and recovery rate. All mulched treatments out-yielded the control (p < 0.05). Net returns ranged from 12,609 to 27,272 CNY ha−1. After the current 1800 CNY ha−1 subsidy, biodegradable films still cost 280–330 CNY ha−1 (1.7–2.0%) more than the matching conventional films. The black 0.010 mm LDPE film left the lowest residue (5 kg ha−1 in 2023; 29 kg ha−1 in 2022) with recovery up to 97.2%; microplastics were not directly quantified. TOPSIS rankings identified white biodegradable film as the highest-ranked treatment under the evaluated economic and agronomic criteria, while DEA revealed white 0.008 mm polyethylene film and white biodegradable film as consistently strong and efficient. Optimal mulch selection depends on farmers’ risk preferences and environmental priorities. This study provides systematic thickness-gradient cost–benefit comparisons and measured visible residue and recovery assessments for biodegradable versus traditional films. Targeted incentive policies combining subsidies with risk-mitigation instruments are recommended.
W7222150585.title: Multi-Criteria Economic and Environmental Assessment of Biodegradable and Plastic Mulch Films in Peanut Production Systems

W7222193294.abstract: Nanospheres are sub-micron-sized solid colloidal particles, typically ranging from 10 to 200 nm in diameter, that have emerged as highly effective carriers for targeted drug delivery and diagnostic applications. Owing to their unique physicochemical properties, including high surface area, tunable particle size, controlled drug release, and excellent biocompatibility, nanospheres have gained considerable attention in pharmaceutical research. These nanocarriers can encapsulate, adsorb, or conjugate therapeutic agents within a polymeric matrix, thereby protecting drugs from premature enzymatic and chemical degradation and enhancing their stability, bioavailability, and therapeutic efficacy. Researchers have used various biodegradable and biocompatible materials, such as albumin, gelatin, starch, polylactic acid, poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid), and dextran-based polymers, to fabricate nanospheres. Surface modification strategies, including polymer coating and ligand conjugation, have been extensively explored to overcome the challenges associated with opsonization and rapid clearance by the reticuloendothelial system, thereby prolonging systemic circulation and improving site-specific drug accumulation. Advanced nanosphere platforms, including magnetic, immunological, and immunomagnetic nanospheres, show strong potential in precision medicine by enabling targeted delivery, enhanced cellular uptake, and real-time monitoring of therapeutic responses. In oncology, nanosphere-based delivery systems have revolutionized cancer diagnosis and treatment by selectively transporting anticancer agents to tumor tissues while minimizing off-target toxicity and adverse effects on healthy cells. Furthermore, nanosphere-assisted biosensing technologies have shown significant promise for early cancer detection by identifying tumor- associated biomarkers, circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and specific proteins. These multifunctional nanoplatforms integrate diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities, paving the way for personalized, theranostic approaches to cancer management. This review comprehensively discusses the classification, preparation methods, physicochemical characteristics, and biomedical applications of nanospheres, with a particular focus on their emerging roles in cancer diagnosis, targeted drug delivery, and precision therapeutics. It also critically examines current challenges, recent technological advances, and future perspectives on the clinical translation of nanosphere-based systems.
W7222193294.journal: Recent Advances in Drug Delivery and Formulation
W7222193294.title: A Comprehensive Review on Nanosphere-Based Drug Delivery System for the Identification and Prevention of Cancerous Cells

W7222212103.abstract: ABSTRACT This study focuses on developing sustainable polylactic acid (PLA)‐based composites reinforced with recyclable fillers, such as sawdust, medium‐density fibreboard (MDF), and textile waste, for advanced 3D printing applications. Following circular economy principles, this study looks to enhance the mechanical, structural, and environmental qualities of PLA by incorporating waste‐derived reinforcements and optimizing processing with compatibilizers. The composites were produced through extrusion and compression molding, then thoroughly analyzed using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, contact angle measurements, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). Results indicated that the recycled fillers dispersed evenly without modifying the PLA matrix. Mechanical testing showed that certain filler types increased the composite's stiffness and energy absorption. All samples exhibited a single glass transition characteristic of PLA‐based materials. Higher UV exposure caused different degradation patterns. The type and pretreatment of fillers influenced surface hydrophobicity and mechanical performance. Overall, the findings highlight the potential of waste reinforcements to improve the practical properties and durability of PLA, encouraging the use of sustainable materials in furniture and other 3D‐printed products.
W7222212103.title: Physicochemical and Mechanical Characterization of PLA Composites With Waste‐Derived Reinforcements for 3D ‐Printed Applications

W7222235610.abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic disease characterized by impaired insulin secretion, reduced insulin sensitivity, and hyperglycemia. Diabetic wounds are among the major complications of T2DM and can lead to chronic wounds due to challenges in the normal healing process. In this study, a three-layered tissue scaffold incorporating microneedles (MNs) was developed for diabetic wound management. The scaffold was fabricated using digital light processing (DLP) for the GelMA-based layers and electrohydrodynamic atomization (EHDA) for the surface coating, combining antibacterial, metabolic, and antioxidant functions within a single platform. The first two layers were designed using gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) and produced via DLP. The first layer was loaded with the antibiotic amoxicillin to prevent infection at the scaffold application site. In the second layer, MNs containing metformin were designed. For the outermost layer, polylactic acid (PLA) microparticles containing antioxidant and antibacterial salicylic acid (SA) were produced via the EHDA method and coated onto the scaffold surface. This three-layered scaffold was characterized by SEM, FT-IR, DSC, and mechanical, swelling, degradation, and penetration analyses. In vitro studies of single-drug-loaded model formulations demonstrated biphasic drug-release behavior over 72 h, effective antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, and favorable cytocompatibility. Oxidative-stress assays showed lower Total Oxidant Status (TOS) levels and higher Total Antioxidant Status (TAS) values in the drug-loaded formulations, while the scratch assay demonstrated increased wound-gap closure under hyperglycemic culture conditions. Overall, the multilayer microneedle platform exhibited antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones of up to 23 mm, and favorable cytocompatibility, with cell viability remaining above 77% across all formulations. These findings provide in vitro proof-of-concept evidence for the multifunctional design of the platform but do not demonstrate wound-healing efficacy in diabetic tissue.
W7222235610.title: 3D-Printed GelMA Microneedles with Multilayer Therapeutic Properties for Diabetic Wound-Relevant Drug Delivery

W7222259223.abstract: As a photocatalyst, silver phosphate (Ag3PO4) features high quantum yield and strong photocatalytic ability, demonstrating great potential in water splitting and the treatment of water pollutants. However, its own photo-corrosion and low solubility in water limit its application. To address these issues, the combination of Ag3PO4 with other semiconductor materials to form composite photocatalysts can enhance its catalytic activity and structural stability, facilitating the photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants in wastewater. In this work, Ag3PO4/g-C3N4/C composite photocatalytic materials were successfully prepared using biochar (C), g-C3N4, AgNO3, and Na2HPO4·12H2O as raw materials through a co-precipitation method. The Ag3PO4/g-C3N4/C (mass ratio 4:1:0.1) composite photocatalyst exhibited excellent degradation performance for MB and RhB and maintained good stability. During the degradation of MB and RhB, the main active species were h+ (holes), •O2− and •OH. The MB removal efficiency reached 97% in 40 mL of 10 mg/L MB aqueous solution within 60 min of visible light irradiation, and the removal efficiency of RhB reached 96% in 40 mL of 10 mg/L RhB aqueous solution within 80 min of visible light irradiation. After three cycles of reuse, the removal efficiencies of MB and RhB photocatalyzed by Ag3PO4/g-C3N4/C (4:1:0.1) still reached 79% and 74%, respectively. The Ag3PO4/g-C3N4/C composite photocatalyst can be applied to the degradation of organic pigment in the environment dye wastewater, contributing to environmental remediation and the green development of the ecological environment.
W7222259223.title: Preparation and Photocatalytic Performance of Ag3PO4/g-C3N4/Biochar Composite Materials

W7222294250.abstract: Organic modified montmorillonite (OMMT) and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) were incorporated into polylactic acid (PLA) nanocomposite films to develop packaging for postharvest preservation of fresh blueberries. Blueberries (10 g/pouch) were packaged within 2 h of harvest and stored under ambient dry conditions for 7 days. Three treatments were evaluated: unpackaged control, neat PLA film, and PLA/OMMT/PVA nanocomposite film. Weight loss, fungal growth, total phenolic and flavonoid contents, and antioxidant- and browning-related biochemical parameters were monitored during storage. These included catalase (CAT), ascorbate peroxidase (APX), peroxidase (POD), superoxide dismutase (SOD), polyphenol oxidase (PPO), and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂). Visible fungal growth occurred in the control and neat-PLA treatments within 7 days, whereas the PLA/OMMT/PVA film significantly suppressed fungal proliferation. PPO activity in the PLA/OMMT/PVA treatment declined to approximately 3.1 U/g on Day 5 before increasing to 10.6 U/g on Day 7, remaining lower than neat PLA (15.5 U/g) and control (16.3 U/g). APX activity decreased from approximately 0.86 U/g to 0.10–0.22 U/g between Days 1 and 3 (p < 0.05) and remained lower in the PLA/OMMT/PVA treatment (0.11 U/g) than in neat PLA (0.41 U/g) on Day 7. H₂O₂ accumulation reached approximately 1150 μmol g⁻¹ on Day 5 and declined to 420 μmol g⁻¹ by Day 7. TSS decreased from 14.0% to 10.0% in PLA/OMMT/PVA, compared with 8.0% in the control. Overall, PLA/OMMT/PVA nanocomposite packaging improved blueberry preservation and reduced fungal growth and browning-related biochemical changes compared with neat PLA and unpackaged storage.
oa_topics: Postharvest Quality and Shelf Life Management
W7222294250.title: Effects of PLA/OMMT/PVA Nanocomposite Films on Postharvest Quality and Enzymatic Browning Mitigation in Fresh Blueberries

W7222296917.abstract: Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a common condition caused by increased carpal tunnel pressure and compression of the median nerve. Wrist–hand orthosis is widely used as a nonsurgical treatment to maintain the wrist in a near-neutral position and reduce pressure within the carpal tunnel. However, conventional orthosis often suffers from poor comfort, inadequate ventilation, localized pressure, and low patient compliance. This study aimed to design and evaluate a customized, multi-material 3D-printed wrist-to-finger orthosis that incorporated individual finger supports, perforated regions, and a volar clearance zone intended to avoid direct shell contact over the carpal tunnel region. A customized proof-of-concept orthosis was designed using a dual-material structure consisting of a rigid polylactic acid (PLA) outer shell and a flexible thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) inner liner. The TPU liner was incorporated at skin contact regions to improve comfort, while the PLA shell provided structural support. Perforated lattice patterns were integrated to enhance ventilation and reduce weight, and a dedicated clearance zone was created on the volar side of the wrist to minimize direct pressure on the carpal tunnel area. Finite element analysis (FEA) was conducted under three loading conditions to evaluate stress distribution and deformation. The design refinement reduced the calculated mass from 258.27 to 205.36 g, corresponding to a 20.5% reduction. The maximum sampled von Mises stresses on the final PLA shell were 1.04 MPa on the upper surface and 0.99 MPa on the lower surface. Flexural testing demonstrated that the orthosis possessed adequate stiffness and maintained structural integrity under applied loads. The developed customized proof-of-concept orthosis demonstrates the feasibility of combining multi-material fused filament fabrication (FFF), personalized design, and FEA to produce a lightweight, breathable, comfortable, and mechanically reliable device for CTS management. The incorporation of a TPU liner and a carpal tunnel clearance zone has the potential to improve user comfort while maintaining the mechanical support required for effective treatment.
W7222296917.title: Design and Finite Element Evaluation of a Customized 3D-Printed Wrist-to-Finger Orthosis Targeting Carpal Tunnel Pressure Reduction

W7222313686.abstract: This paper focuses on reducing the negative impacts of traditional plastics in the production of meltblown filters by using poly lactic acid (PLA) as an environmental friendly biodegradable polymer. In this study the impacts of collector drum speed, die to collector distance (DCD) and die hole diameter on the basis weight, thickness, air permeability, solidity, fiber diameter, water contact angle, and air filtration characteristics of microfibrous PLA nonwovens prepared by meltblowing were investigated. Statistical analyses was conducted by using SPSS software. PLA meltblowns prepared in this study had an average fiber diameter of 2.17 to 3.11 micrometers. The results have shown that, by tailoring the properties of PLA meltblown, filtration performance can be improved while also reducing the environmental impact. This research provides important insights into the production of sustainable meltblown nonwovens by integrating a biodegradable polymer and focusing on the effect of production parameters on material properties.
W7222313686.title: Production and Characterization of Poly Lactic Acid (Pla) Meltblown Nonwovens For Air Filtration

W7222352554.abstract: Abstract In this report, a systematic study on the antibacterial activity of poly(β-quaternary ammonium esters) (PBQAEs), a unique class of cationic polymers, is presented. The effects of main-chain ammonium groups and the chemical structures of side chains (e.g., hydrophilic ethylene glycols and hydrophobic alkyl chains) on the antibacterial performance are systematically examined. The results show that the polymer with a long alkyl side chain (P5Q) is a potent antibacterial agent with low MIC values against various Gram (+) bacterial strains, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). The interaction of P5Q with the bacterial cells has been evaluated by a membrane depolarization assay to elucidate the mechanism of antibacterial action. The results indicate that P5Q interacts with and subsequently disrupts bacterial cell membranes by hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions, resulting in instant cell death. The in vitro cytotoxicity of P5Q against MCF-7 human breast cancer and HUVEC normal human umbilical vein endothelial cells is further evaluated by MTT assay. P5Q shows almost no acute mammalian cell toxicity in the concentration range between 2.0 and 32.0 μg/mL. To demonstrate the practical applicability of P5Q, polylactic acid (PLA) based electrospun nanofibers doped with P5Q have been successfully fabricated via electrospinning. The resulting composite fibers exhibit potent antibacterial activity, as characterized and validated by the disk diffusion assay.

W7222463627.abstract: Abstract The study explores the influence of layer thickness, infill pattern, and nozzle temperature on tensile strength, hardness, and relative density of FDM printed specimens of polylactic acid (PLA). Eighteen different sets of parameters were explored during the study, including two layers of thickness (0.1 and 0.2 mm), three different infill patterns (concentric, rectilinear, and octogram spiral), and three nozzle temperatures (210, 220, and 230 °C). The tensile test was done following ISO 527-2, the hardness test according to ASTM D2240, and the measurement of relative density was done using the Archimedes principle. From the results, it can be observed that the effect of layer thickness is significant where samples of 0.1 mm exhibited tensile strengths of 35–49 MPa compared to samples of 0.2 mm with tensile strengths of 34–48 MPa. The highest tensile strength was exhibited by concentric infill pattern due to its continuous load-bearing capacity, followed by rectilinear while the lowest was recorded by octogram spiral infill pattern. There was a significant correlation between the tensile strength and relative density ( r = 0.89, p < 0.001), and it reached its maximum at a value of 99 %. Analysis of the failure showed that rectilinear pattern had ductile failure, while octogram spiral pattern failed by delamination.
W7222463627.title: Experimental analysis and optimization of the influence of layer height, infill pattern, and nozzle temperature on tensile strength, hardness, and relative density of FDM-PLA prints

W7222475354.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Surgical repair of pelvic organ prolapse and stress urinary incontinence frequently relies on polymeric biomaterials in sutures, meshes, and membranes to provide structural support during tissue healing and beyond. Polypropylene has long served as the default material owing to its strength, durability, and processability, but the chronic foreign body response and mechanical mismatch between stiff implants and viscoelastic pelvic tissue have been linked to complications, including mesh contraction, exposure, and dyspareunia. These limitations, together with regulatory actions on transvaginal mesh, have driven interest in alternative permanent polymers and, increasingly, in resorbable materials designed to provide temporary reinforcement during tissue remodeling. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this review was to summarize the characteristics, advantages, and limitations of polymers currently used or under investigation for load-bearing and reinforcement urogynecologic implants. STUDY DESIGN: This is a narrative review of polymeric biomaterials for urogynecologic mesh, membrane, and suture applications, based on a search of PubMed and Web of Science for in vitro and in vivo studies of polymer-based devices. RESULTS: Permanent materials covered include polypropylene, polyvinylidene fluoride, polytetrafluoroethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polyamide, and polyurethane. Resorbable materials include lactide- and caprolactone-based polyesters, polydioxanone, polyhydroxyalkanoates (notably poly-4-hydroxybutyrate), and natural polymers such as silk fibroin, bacterial cellulose, and collagen. The use of advanced manufacturing techniques and functionalizing strategies to improve tissue reinforcement and healing is also highlighted. CONCLUSIONS: The review provides a reference point for the design of next-generation urogynecologic implants, which requires integrated consideration of polymer properties, scaffold architecture, and host biology across the course of tissue remodeling.
W7222475354.title: Polymers for Pelvic Floor Repair: Current State and Future Prospects.

W7222521427.abstract: Abstract Additively manufactured carbon fiber-reinforced polylactic acid (CF-PLA) composites are increasingly used for lightweight components that require improved flexural performance. However, their mechanical response is strongly governed by the combined effects of printing parameters, making systematic modeling and multi-response optimization essential. In this study, the flexural behavior of CF-PLA composites was investigated using a central composite design (CCD) based on four material extrusion parameters: printing speed (PS), printing temperature (PT), layer thickness (LT), and number of outer shells (OS). Eight flexural responses were analyzed to describe stiffness-, strength-, strain-, and energy-related performance indicators. The results showed that PT, LT, and OS had dominant but response-dependent effects, whereas PS exhibited a comparatively lower influence. Flexural stress at break was significantly affected by interaction terms, indicating strong process-parameter interdependencies, while flexural strain at break showed a more independent response, with no significant interaction effects. The developed response surface models showed high predictive accuracy, with coefficients of determination (R 2 ) ranging from 93.06 to 96.64%. To account for the unequal importance of the flexural responses, MEREC and CRITIC objective weighting methods were integrated with Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Desirability Function Approach (DFA). Among the investigated strategies, GWO-MEREC-DFA achieved the highest composite desirability value (0.9899), outperforming GWO-CRITIC-DFA (0.9756) and equal-weight optimization (0.9751). The optimized condition also produced superior flexural performance and the most compact, least disrupted damage morphology. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of hybrid GWO-based approaches for optimizing MEX-printed CF-PLA composites.

W7222521427.title: Multi-response optimization of flexural performance in additively manufactured carbon fiber-reinforced PLA composites

W7222531323.abstract: Abstract Plastic straws are extensively utilized across various sectors owing to their ease of manufacture and low cost, yet their improper disposal raises significant environmental concerns due to their persistent, non-biodegradable nature. While biodegradable alternatives exist, they still face significant challenges, including low mechanical performance, poor water stability, high prices, and complex chemical treatment processes. Herein, a facile, green process for fabricating polysaccharide straws is reported. These straws are produced by physical cross-linking via electrostatic interactions and Ca2+-mediated coordination of polysaccharides, thereby reinforcing the cross-linked network. The resulting straws demonstrated excellent mechanical performance, near-hydrophobic surface behavior, and superior hydrostability, comparable to plastic straws or much superior to present degradable straws (polylactic acid and paper straws). Moreover, the polysaccharide-based straws fully degraded naturally within 90 days. Given their comprehensive performance, these straws represent viable alternatives to plastic straws and offer a promising avenue for the future development of sustainable commercial straw products.
W7222531323.title: A Facile and Green Fabrication of High-Performance Biodegradable Polysaccharide-Based Straws for Sustainable Plastic Replacement

W7222540514.abstract: The transition from fossil-based plastics to bioplastics in food packaging requires not only technological advances but also coherent regulatory frameworks and economic support mechanisms. This review examines how policies, production costs, and industrial initiatives shape the large-scale adoption of biopolymers such as polylactic acid (PLA), polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA), and starch-based materials. The regulatory comparison indicates substantial differences in legal scope and implementation across jurisdictions, while also showing that the existence of binding legislation does not by itself demonstrate bioplastic-specific circular-performance outcomes. Although the high production cost of bioplastics remains a major barrier to widespread implementation, strategies including agricultural residue valorization and green fiscal instruments may contribute to improving competitiveness. Overall, the evidence reviewed suggests that the transition toward sustainable food packaging depends on the combined development of material performance, regulatory coherence, industrial integration, and life-cycle accountability, highlighting the need for greater coordination across these dimensions.
W7222540514.title: Bioplastics Beyond Materials: A Review on Regulatory, Economic, and Circular Pathways Toward Sustainable Food Packaging

W7222541841.abstract: High-performance textiles demand fibre architectures that combine mechanical integrity, efficient moisture transport for wearer comfort, and scalable processing, all while meeting stringent sustainability expectations in one of the world’s most environmentally burdensome industries. Here we present a proof of concept for engineering capillary moisture transport into polyethylene by melt-spinning bicomponent fibres with a high-density polyethylene (HDPE) core and polylactic acid (PLA) shell that was selectively dissolved after weaving. Fibres collected at winding speeds of 1000 and 2000 metres per minute (mpm) exhibited mean diameters of 11.96 ± 0.85 μm and 9.63 ± 0.94 μm, respectively, and HDPE crystallinities of 65.6% and 68.7% by DSC. TGA showed that PLA degraded first, with an onset at 293 °C, compared with 395 °C for the fibres recovered after dissolution (HDPEAD). After selective PLA removal, SEM revealed aligned inter-fibre channels and longitudinal surface ridges consistent with along-the-fibre water transport, and infra-red thermography showed that the resulting woven HDPEAD fabrics wick water, reaching saturation in 7-8 min (n = 3), compared with 4 min for cotton and 2 min for polyester, whereas TyvekTM (a commercial nonwoven of flash-spun HDPE) showed no uptake under the same conditions.
W7222541841.title: Melt-spun HDPE/PLA core–shell fibres: a sacrificial-shell route to capillary moisture transport in polyethylene textiles

W7222600295.abstract: Abstract Fused filament fabrication (FFF) produces strong, direction-dependent elastic anisotropy that conventional uniaxial testing cannot fully capture. This study introduces a multiaxial ultrasonic methodology that identifies the complete orthotropic stiffness tensor of FFF-printed polylactic acid (PLA) and PLA/wood-flour (PLA/WF) composites and uses it to quantify how layer thickness, infill density and infill pattern control their directional elastic response. Chamfered cubic specimens (72 in total, 24 processing configurations, three replicates each) were tested along three principal axes and three face-diagonal directions to obtain the nine independent stiffness coefficients, with a within-configuration repeatability of 1.2–6.2 %. Infill pattern is the principal driver of elastic anisotropy: the in-plane stiffness ratio E2/E1 reaches 2.9 for the Line pattern at low infill density, against near-unity values for the Combined pattern. Wood flour redistributes stiffness preferentially transverse to the filaments at low infill density, recovering E₁ by up to 110 % and reducing in-plane anisotropy by up to 41 %, while the build direction remains intrinsically softer than the in-plane directions regardless of raster orientation. Compliance-matrix inversion further suggests apparent near-zero or negative Poisson’s ratios (ν₁₂ as low as −0.06) for one Line-pattern configuration at low infill density; this auxetic-like response is reported as a working hypothesis requiring direct strain-field validation. A four-way ANOVA on the raw replicate measurements confirms these trends quantitatively, with highly significant effects of infill density and material on all nine stiffness coefficients (p < 0.0001) and significant material × density interactions for eight of the nine coefficients (p < 0.05). Acoustic microscopy supports these findings by revealing inter-raster voiding, wood-flour-mediated bridging and layer-thickness-dependent interlayer features. The proposed framework offers a non-destructive route to the complete elastic characterization of FFF-printed biobased composites and quantitative guidance for the design of structurally anisotropic components.
W7222600295.title: Process-microstructure-anisotropy relationships in FFF-printed PLA/wood flour composites: Multiaxial ultrasonic determination of the orthotropic elastic tensor

W7222699158.abstract: Oral drug delivery remains the most widely preferred route of drug administration owing to its convenience, patient compliance, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for long-term therapy.However, the oral delivery of many therapeutic agents is significantly limited by poor aqueous solubility, low intestinal permeability, gastrointestinal degradation, extensive first-pass metabolism, and efflux transporter activity, resulting in inadequate bioavailability and inconsistent therapeutic outcomes.Polymeric nanospheres have emerged as a promising nanotechnology-based platform capable of overcoming these physiological and biopharmaceutical barriers through enhanced drug protection, controlled release, improved mucosal interaction, and targeted intestinal absorption.The selection of appropriate biodegradable polymers, together with advances in formulation technologies such as nanoprecipitation, solvent evaporation, microfluidics, and continuous manufacturing, has considerably improved the physicochemical properties and therapeutic performance of oral nanosphere formulations.Furthermore, recent developments in surface engineering, stimuli-responsive polymers, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted formulation design, machine learning (ML), and Quality by Design (QbD) have accelerated the optimization and translation of polymeric nanospheres from laboratory research toward industrial manufacturing.This review comprehensively summarizes the fundamental principles, classification, formulation strategies, characterization techniques, drug release mechanisms, surface functionalization approaches, and smart polymeric nanosphere systems developed for oral drug delivery.In addition, recent therapeutic applications in cancer, diabetes, infectious diseases, inflammatory disorders, neurological diseases, and biological therapeutics are critically discussed.The review also highlights current translational challenges, regulatory considerations, clinical perspectives, and future research directions with particular emphasis on intelligent nanomedicine, precision drug delivery, and sustainable pharmaceutical manufacturing.Overall, polymeric nanospheres represent a versatile and rapidly evolving oral drug delivery platform with significant potential to improve drug bioavailability, therapeutic efficacy, and patient outcomes while facilitating the development of next-generation oral nanomedicines.

W7222752631.abstract: Abstract Pulp fiber-reinforced polymer nanocomposites have received considerable R&D interest, with a notable challenge in achieving good nanofiber dispersion. One particularly successful approach is through the in situ fibrillation of the pulp fibers into nanofibers in the presence of polymers during extrusion compounding. The extrusion fibrillation of bleached/unbleached pulp fibers and old corrugated container was investigated with polylactic acid (PLA) for improving fiber dispersion. Extrusion fibrillation generated both fibrillated nanofibers and unfibrillated pulp fibers, which were well dispersed in the PLA matrix. PLA’s crystallinity increased as fiber loading increased, attributable to the nucleating effect of cellulose. Heat deflection temperature increased from 53 °C to 57 °C with fiber presence at high loading. Higher fiber loading also increased the viscosity of composite melts because of increased fiber−fiber and fiber−polymer interactions. The biocomposites formed were found to have improved tensile strength (∼75 MPa) and stiffness (∼5.5 GPa) by 15% and 53%, respectively, at a 30 wt. % fiber loading relative to the neat PLA polymer, without any loss in impact strength. The improvement in composites’ mechanical properties comes from well-dispersed nanofibers, increased interfacial interaction, and higher polymer matrix crystallinity. This research shows the potential of extrusion fibrillation for recycling old corrugated containers as a reinforcing material in PLA composites.

W7222827048.abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a novel material design approach for wear‐resistant sandwich‐structured hybrid composites fabricated using dual‐nozzle fused deposition modeling (FDM). By co‐printing commercially available mono‐filaments, this approach prevents the compounding difficulties and enables the strategic placement of nanoparticles and micro‐fibers layers. Two hybrid architectures were produced by combining a nano‐copper polylactic acid (nano‐Cu PLA) phase with either a carbon flake (CF PLA) or short carbon fiber (SCF PLA) reinforced phase. The additive manufacturing process was optimized for flexural performance, followed by systematic tribological evaluation using pin‐on‐disc dry sliding tests under different normal pressures and sliding velocities. Micro‐Computed Tomography revealed an interconnected carbon‐filler network with a dispersed nanoparticle phase and a transition band that enhances mechanical interlocking. The hybrid composite filled with copper nanoparticles and SCF achieved a flexural strength of 97.30 MPa, outperforming its base components. At a contact pressure of 1 MPa and a sliding velocity of 0.2 m/s, the specific wear rate decreased to 3.4 × 10 −7 mm 3 /Nm. Microscopic analysis suggests that copper nanoparticles released at the interface act as rolling agents for exposed fiber tips, and change the contact mode, leading to synergistic wear reduction. These findings provide insights for designing high‐performance tribological components via additive manufacturing.
W7222827048.title: Tribological Behavior of Additively Manufactured Dual‐Material Polymer Composites

W7222843342.abstract: The proliferation of 3D-printed firearms has raised interest worldwide into the forensic capacity for the source determination of items seized in relation to the manufacture, trade, firing and concealment of these weapons. Given the limited success achieved from conventional firearms toolmarks analysis, recent interest has focussed on the physiochemical characterisation of the polymers used. This study demonstrates the first research, to our knowledge, exploring the thermal properties of 3D-printing polymers used for the manufacture of privately made firearms in a forensic context. Twenty-eight polylactic acid (PLA) 3D-printing filament samples, sourced from the Australian market, were analysed via differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and chemometric analysis to investigate the degree of variability in their thermal properties. DSC proved successful in discerning twenty-six PLA filament samples, including same-colour filaments of different brands, using characteristic features in their thermograms. This methodology was also applied to acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) and polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG) 3D-printing filament samples, however, limited useful information was provided due to their amorphous nature. The impact of thermal history on the thermal properties of PLA initially limited the ability to establish links between filament and printed samples. However, heat treatment was subsequently used to control the thermal history of the PLA samples, allowing printed samples to be correctly associated with the corresponding filament material. The outcomes of this research will help to inform a material-specific approach for the analysis of semicrystalline 3D-printing polymers when seized in relation to a criminal investigation.
W7222843342.title: Same polymer, different story: DSC analysis of commercial PLA 3D-printing filaments for forensic comparisons

W7222892980.abstract: This study reports the development of fully bio-based polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites reinforced with short Ampelodesmos mauritanicus (Diss) fibers using a powder-based processing route. To improve fiber-matrix compatibility, the fibers were subjected to sequential HCl/NaOH treatment to modify their surface morphology. A fixed concentration of 10 wt.% was selected to isolate the effect of surface treatment on fiber-matrix interaction rather than to optimize the reinforcement level. Multiscale characterization using SEM, AFM, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, and DSC showed that the treatment improved interfacial adhesion by promoting mechanical interlocking and molecular interactions between PLA and the exposed cellulose-rich fiber surface. AFM observations confirmed a marked increase in surface roughness, while DSC analysis revealed that treated fibers influenced PLA crystallization through the combined effects of heterogeneous nucleation and restricted chain mobility at the interface. These microstructural changes enhanced load transfer, with the treated-fiber composite reaching a Young’s modulus of 4.24 GPa and a tensile strength of 46.8 MPa. The powder-processing route also promoted homogeneous fiber dispersion and may help reduce thermal and shear-induced degradation compared with conventional melt processing. Overall, the results demonstrate that combining interfacial engineering with powder processing provides an effective strategy for designing lightweight, high-performance, and sustainable PLA/Diss biocomposites.

W7222899462.abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates are a family of biopolymers that accumulate inside microorganisms as primary storage polymers in response to nutrient stress. This family of biopolymers can be used as bioplastics instead of synthetic plastics because it biodegrades into CO2 and H2O. This study aimed to isolate a new bacterial strain that can accumulate PHAs when cultured under unbalanced nutrient conditions of excess carbon and a depleted nitrogen source. Screening for PHAs accumulating bacterial isolates was based on culturing the bacteria on minimal salt medium containing Nile red as a fluorescent dye. Positive PHAs bacterial colonies displayed bright orange fluorescence under ultraviolet light while PHA- negative isolates failed to exhibit fluorescence. Extraction of PHAs was achieved using a dispersion of sodium hypochlorite-chloroform solution and quantified by conversion into crotonic acid through boiling in concentrated sulfuric acid and measured by UV spectrophotometer at 235 nm. The most potent isolate was selected to optimize cell growth and PHAs production conditions using the ``one- factor-at-a-time'' method. The newly isolated strain Corynebacterium variabile M11 was identified using the 16S rRNA gene and characterized as a positive PHAs-accumulating bacterium using staining and fluorescent tests. Granules were observed inside the cytoplasm by (TEM). The structure of extracted PHAs was analyzed by FTIR and 1H-NMR spectroscopy, and the results confirmed the similarity with standard PHAs and were characterized as poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3- hydroxyvalerate). The optimum pH, temperature, and incubation period for maximum PHA production using dextrose and ammonium chloride were 7, 30 °C, and 72 h, respectively.
W7222899462.title: Production and Optimization of Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) by Corynebacterium Variabile M11: A Newly Reported PHAs-Producing Bacterium

W7222903619.abstract: Porous titanium scaffolds for bone repair require coordinated control of pore architecture, mechanical behavior, and surface bioactivity. Here, we report a sacrificial-template route based on polymer 3D printing that produces orientation-controlled porous titanium scaffolds with hierarchical macro- and microporosity without direct metal additive manufacturing. Polylactic acid lattices printed by fused deposition modeling are infiltrated with a titanium powder slurry and then subjected to template removal and sintering. The process yields ortho-grid, tri-lattice, and quad-lattice structures with approximately 26% isotropic linear shrinkage, 65%-67% porosity, preserved geometric fidelity, and a relative density of approximately 95% in the sintered strut walls. Uniaxial compression tests reveal architecture-dependent behavior along the tested loading direction, whereas finite element simulations predict lower directional sensitivity under off-axis loading as strut-orientation diversity increases. Micro-arc oxidation forms a Ca-P-containing microporous oxide layer and improves cell spreading, proliferation, and alkaline phosphatase activity relative to untreated titanium scaffolds in vitro. In a rat calvarial defect model, uncoated titanium scaffolds achieve bone regeneration comparable to commercial porous tantalum, while micro-arc oxidation further enhances bone formation. Fabrication of cone augments and other non-prismatic geometries further demonstrates the adaptability of the approach to complex implant-relevant structures.
W7222903619.title: Sacrificial‐Template Fabrication of Orientation‐Controlled Porous Titanium Lattices With Bioactive Surfaces

W7222919189.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to report the implementation and initial experimental evaluation of an adaptive infill method for fused deposition modeling that combines cross-section-driven variable-density assignment with an explicit transition-layer branch triggered at detected geometric discontinuities, all operating at the slicing stage without external geometry modification or load-path input. Design/methodology/approach A continuous exponential mapping converts the slice-wise cross-sectional area sequence into a layer-specific infill density bounded by user-defined limits. A dual-criterion detection module identifies abrupt geometric transitions using area-change rate and centroid displacement; a sliding-window slope-exclusion rule prevents false detection on continuous gradients; densified reinforcement layers are inserted only at flagged abrupt interfaces. The two algorithmic branches were exercised separately on two test geometries – compression specimens with circular necked profiles and tensile specimens with rectangular stepped profiles – printed in polylactic acid (PLA) at 20\% baseline infill density with five specimens per group. Findings The adaptive group showed a marginal trend toward higher first peak force on compression specimens (5.6∼kN to 5.9∼kN, +5.4\%; Welch’s t-test, p = 0.054) and a statistically significant 15.4\% higher peak load on tensile specimens (803.2∼N to 926.8∼N; p = 0.043), with mass increases of 0.5\% and printing time increases below 7\%. A directional check with glycol-modified polyethylene terephthalate (PETG) at three specimens per group gave +14.2\% tensile peak-load difference (p = 0.0045), consistent in direction with the PLA result. Sparse-infill toolpath length differed from the uniform baseline by less than 1.5\%. The algorithm transferred without modification to three geometries of greater complexity. Originality/value This work presents an integrated implementation that combines an existing class of cross-section-driven variable-density assignment with an explicit transition-layer detection and reinforcement branch within a single slicing-level pipeline, together with per-layer diagnostic data that make the algorithm’s geometric decisions inspectable.
W7222919189.title: Adaptive infill method for FDM based on cross-section features and transition layers

W7222920298.abstract: The shortage and high cost of autologous bone grafts have created an urgent need to the development of biocompatible materials for bone defect repair. Bone is a natural piezoelectric tissue that generates electrical stimulation to induce osteogenic differentiation. However, most biodegradable polymers lack inherent piezoelectric properties, making the design of controllably degradable piezoelectric biomaterials particularly significant. In this work, poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) was used as a raw material to synthesize a polyurethane (PU)-based bio-ink consisting of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and hydroxyapatite (HA) via a one-step method. Personalized composite scaffolds (PU/PVDF/HA) were then fabricated by extrusion-based 3D printing. Characterization results from FTIR, XRD, water contact angle, and degradation tests confirmed the successful formation of PU/PVDF/HA composite scaffolds and demonstrated that the incorporation of HA effectively enhanced the bioactivity of the composite material with pronounced piezoelectric properties, suggesting potential relevance for osteogenic applications. Further, the PU/PVDF/HA15 group (containing 15 wt% HA and 5 wt% PVDF) had a good biocompatibility, which was clearly reflected by CCK-8 detection and live/death fluorescence imaging compared with the other groups. Overall, the synergistic action of piezoelectricity and bioactivity in PU/PVDF/HA scaffolds improved the physicochemical characteristics of the material-tissue interface, and then promoted the osteogenic activity. This study provides experimental evidence supporting the feasibility of integrating piezoelectric functionality and bioactivity into polymer-based scaffolds for bone tissue engineering.
