W7222920298.title: Piezoelectric-bioactive coupling of PVDF and hydroxyapatite for enhancing the interfacial bioactivity and osteogenic potential of the 3D-printed polyurethane scaffolds

W7222924175.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis remains the world's leading infectious cause of death, with an estimated 10.8 million people falling ill and about 1.25 million dying in 2023. Isoniazid has anchored first-line therapy for seventy years, yet it is given orally for months, distributes throughout the body, and reaches the infected lung only after a long detour through the gut and liver. Objective: This review examines whether biodegradable polymeric nanoparticles delivered directly to the lung can improve the therapeutic index of isoniazid, and sets out what the formulation, aerosol and preclinical evidence actually supports. Methods: Published work on pulmonary barriers, isoniazid pharmacology, polymer selection, nanoparticle fabrication, aerosol engineering, controlled release, characterization and preclinical testing was surveyed from PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus and Google Scholar, then synthesized into comparative tables. Key Findings: PLGA, PLA, chitosan, alginate, gelatin and albumin have all been used to encapsulate isoniazid, though its high water solubility keeps encapsulation efficiency low in hydrophobic polyesters and pushes formulators toward polyelectrolyte systems or modified emulsion methods. Nanoparticles alone aerosolize poorly; nanoparticle-in-microparticle powders solve the aerodynamic problem while preserving nanoscale behaviour after deposition. Animal studies report prolonged lung and plasma drug levels and reduced dosing frequency, but most used drug combinations rather than isoniazid alone, and none has reached clinical trial. Conclusion: Inhaled polymeric isoniazid nanoparticles are pharmaceutically feasible and preclinically promising. Translation now depends on raising drug loading, controlling burst release, proving aerosol and storage stability, and generating long-term pulmonary safety data. Keywords: Isoniazid; Tuberculosis; Polymeric nanoparticles; Pulmonary drug delivery; PLGA; Chitosan; Dry powder inhaler; Alveolar macrophages; Controlled release
W7222924175.journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
W7222924175.title: Polymeric Nanoparticle-Based Pulmonary Delivery of Isoniazid: Advances in Formulation Design, Controlled Release, and Tuberculosis Therapy

W7222927468.abstract: Postbiotics and paraprobiotics are emerging microbial-derived bioactive agents for sustainable food packaging, offering alternatives to plant extracts and essential oils, which face limitations from resource-intensive extraction, variability, and sensory drawbacks. Postbiotics comprise non-viable microbial preparations and functional metabolites, including organic acids, bacteriocins, exopolysaccharides, enzymes, and peptides. In contrast, paraprobiotics are inactivated cells that retain structural and biological functionality without requiring viability. This review examines their biological activity, incorporation methods, and food applications in active and biodegradable packaging. Both agents exhibit antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anti-biofilm effects against pathogens such as Listeria monocytogenes, Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Staphylococcus aureus, primarily via membrane disruption, intracellular acidification, competitive exclusion, and radical scavenging. However, their antimicrobial efficacy is highly variable and strongly context-dependent, being governed by the microbial strain inactivation method. These processing variables and matrix interactions must be systematically optimized when integrating these non-viable bioactives into functional packaging systems. Incorporation into biopolymeric matrices such as chitosan (CH), alginate, starch, bacterial nanocellulose (BNC), gelatin, and polylactic acid via solvent casting, dip coating, electrospinning, and encapsulation enhances antimicrobial performance, barrier properties, and oxidative stability. However, mechanical effects depend on the microbial source, inactivation method, and formulation. Real-food trials in meat, seafood, dairy, and produce demonstrate reduced pathogen loads, delayed lipid oxidation, and shelf-life extensions from several days to over two weeks. Key challenges include food-matrix interference, inconsistent terminology and preparation protocols, unclear dose–response and migration behavior, sensory changes, regulatory uncertainty, and scale-up feasibility. Interestingly, postbiotics and paraprobiotics represent a clean-label, sustainable platform for multifunctional packaging. Progress requires standardized production, strain-specific optimization, controlled-release design, migration and safety testing, empirical life-cycle assessments, and regulatory harmonization to enable safer, more sustainable packaging systems that valorize fermentation byproducts and support circular food-system innovation.

W7222933525.abstract: Nanoparticles improve protective characteristics of biodegradable packaging. The aim of this study was to investigate physicomechanical characteristics of polylactic acid film containing 1, 2 and 3% silver nanoparticles synthesized using photo-assisted and ultrasound-assisted methods and aqueous extract of nettle ( Urtica dioica ). Formation of silver nanoparticles was verified using UV-vis spectroscopy. Photochemical and sonochemical synthesized silver nanoparticles were monodisperse with particle sizes of 91.28 and 68.06 nm and polydispersity indices of 0.382 and 0.371, respectively. Solubility and water absorption decreased with silver nanoparticles, especially ultrasound-assisted synthesized ones, into polylactic acid films ( p < 0.05). Nanocomposites containing 2 and 3% of ultrasound-assisted synthesized silver nanoparticles showed the highest tensile strength and elongation at break. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy verified the role of nettle extract as a decreasing, stabilizing and capping agent of silver nanoparticles. In fingerprint region of the spectra, presence of Ag-O bonding and synthesis of silver nanoparticles were verified. Silver nanoparticles improved the thermal stability of polylactic acid nanocomposite films. Therefore, use of silver nanoparticles is recommended to improve physicomechanical and thermal characteristics of polylactic acid films.

W7222953519.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Herpes zoster (HZ) results from reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus and disproportionately affects older adults. Antiviral therapy and systemic analgesia are well established, but local wound care of the eroded skin remains largely empirical: no dressing has been validated in controlled trials for this indication, and denuded HZ lesions are frequently mismanaged with dry gauze that adheres to the wound bed and aggravates pain. Case Presentation: An 85-year-old man with no known chronic disease presented with a one-week history of thoracic HZ unresponsive to outpatient antiviral therapy, requiring admission for uncontrolled pain (9/10 on the Numeric Rating Scale, NRS), vomiting, asthenia, and hyporexia. Examination revealed confluent, superficial-partial-thickness erosions across the T6–T8 dermatomes (12.5 × 24 cm). After a negative wound culture, a single polylactic-acid-based membrane (Suprathel®250) was applied over the entire denuded area. Pain decreased from 9/10 to 2/10 on the NRS within seven days and complete re-epithelialization was observed by day 12, under concurrent antiviral and systemic analgesic therapy and the patient resumed independent daily activities by the third week without scarring. Conclusions: In this single uncontrolled case, pain reduction and wound closure followed one application of a polylactic acid membrane to an extensive HZ lesion. Because antiviral and analgesic therapy were given concurrently and HZ improves spontaneously over time, no causal or comparative inference is possible; the observation is hypothesis-generating and supports further controlled investigation. Suprathel® is CE-marked and FDA-cleared for burn and wound care, so its use for HZ erosions extends an established burn indication.

W7222954418.abstract: Fused deposition modelling (FDM) is a widely adopted additive manufacturing technique to fabricate three-dimensional components from thermoplastic feedstock. The investigation is carried out for the effect of layer thickness, nozzle temperature, infill density, and sisal fibre weight fraction on the tensile and flexural properties of sisal fibre-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) composites fabricated through FDM. A Box-Behnken Design (BBD) within the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) framework was employed to investigate and optimize these four experimental factors. The parameter ranges considered were 0.1–0.3 mm for layer thickness, 190–210°C for nozzle temperature, 60–100% for infill density, and 3–9 wt% for sisal fibre content. ANOVA indicated that fibre weight fraction was the most influential factor for tensile strength, while infill density was the dominant factor affecting flexural strength. The regression models established R 2 values of 98.81% and 92.04% for tensile and flexural strength, respectively. Among the experimental design points, 6 wt% sisal fibre produced the highest tensile strength of 46.50 MPa and flexural strength of 78.38 MPa. The RSM-based multi-response optimization identified an optimum combination of 0.2357 mm layer thickness, 209.61°C nozzle temperature, 78.89% infill density, and 6.41 wt% fibre content, with predicted tensile and flexural strengths of 43.50 MPa and 53.55 MPa, respectively. Confirmatory experiments at the optimized condition yielded tensile and flexural strengths of 40.68 MPa and 50.09 MPa, respectively. The results demonstrate the applicability of RSM for identifying a balanced combination of material composition and FDM processing parameters for sisal fibre-reinforced PLA composites.

W7222954418.title: Mechanical property optimization of sisal fiber-reinforced PLA composites fabricated by fused deposition modelling using response surface methodology

W7222955620.abstract: Marine algae sustain primary productivity, nutrient cycling, and coastal carbon regulation, yet warming, salinity fluctuations, acidification, and nutrient/metal loading increasingly challenge their physiology, and evidence linking adaptation to biotechnological value remains fragmented. This narrative review synthesizes physiological, biochemical, and transcriptomic studies (2016–2026) on marine micro- and macroalgae exposed to thermal, saline, light/oxidative, nutrient, heavy-metal, and acidification stress; a few non-marine extremophile taxa are included and flagged as mechanistic comparators. Across taxa, algae rely on recurrent strategies—osmolyte accumulation, antioxidant/photoprotective pigments, fatty-acid desaturation, metal chelation, and phytohormone-mediated (ABA, SA, MeJA) signalling coupled to ribosome-biogenesis upregulation—that appear to restore redox and osmotic homeostasis. These phenotypes underpin biofuel, bioremediation, blue-carbon, and bioplastic applications, ranked on a Technology Readiness Level scale from wastewater bioremediation and aquaculture co-culture (TRL 6–7) to biodiesel and blue-carbon crediting (TRL 3) and photoprotection-trait transfer (TRL 2). We propose a reaction-level conceptual framework in which ribosome-biogenesis control and ABA/SA/MeJA signalling act as a testable stress-integration hub, presented explicitly as a hypothesis rather than an established mechanism. Stress tolerance and circular-economy value may be mechanistically linked, but most evidence derives from short-term, single-species laboratory exposures, remains taxonomically narrow, and macroalga-specific comparative laboratory data are scarce.
W7222955620.journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
W7222955620.title: Physiological and Biochemical Mechanisms of Marine Algae in Response to Environmental Stress: Adaptive Strategies and Applications in Circular Bioeconomy—A Narrative Review and Conceptual Synthesis

W7222961533.abstract: Phosphate enrichment of surface waters is a major cause of eutrophication, creating demand for low-cost materials that support phosphorus removal and recovery. In this study, Conocarpus waste biochar (CBC) was modified with iron (Fe-CBC), magnesium (Mg-CBC), and both metals (FeMg-CBC) to improve phosphate adsorption. FTIR, XRD, SEM, and elemental analyses confirmed clear changes in surface chemistry and mineral composition after modification. FeMg-CBC showed the strongest overall performance, with higher surface area, faster uptake, and greater adsorption capacity than the mono-metallic materials. Phosphate removal was strongly influenced by pH, adsorbent dosage, and contact time, with optimum performance near pH 6. Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second-order model (R2 = 0.997), while equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir–Freundlich model. FeMg-CBC achieved Langmuir and Sips capacities of 86.2 and 106.5 mg g−1, respectively. Its enhanced performance was attributed to combined electrostatic attraction, ligand exchange, Mg-phosphate precipitation, and possible interlayer anion exchange within the Fe-Mg layered phase. These findings highlight its potential for wastewater treatment and nutrient recycling.

W7222967078.abstract: The use of polylactic acid (PLA) and polycaprolactone (PCL) as film-forming components in composites with thermoplastic starch (TPS) was investigated. An optimal composition of the functional additive in TPS was developed using chitosan and lactic acid (chitosan lactate, LC). The physical and mechanical properties of the PLA/TPS and PCL/TPS composites were determined. The structure of the composites and its changes following thermomechanical treatment were studied using FT-IR spectroscopy. Mass spectrometric analysis was performed, and the characteristic mass spectra of ion fragments resulting from the thermal decomposition of PLA, LC, and PLA/TPS were analyzed; their intensities at the peak region were measured. Structural changes in the compositions were studied using DSC and TGA methods, and the mass loss and rate of mass loss during thermal decomposition were quantitatively determined.
W7222967078.title: Analysis of structural transformations in biodegradable polymer composites as a function of film-forming components and functional additives

W7222968137.abstract: Abstract Subarachnoid hemorrhage after cerebral aneurysm rupture has a 50% first-month fatality rate. Endovascular flow diversion is the primary treatment modality. However, no prior study has compared stents, coils, and the Woven Endo-Bridge hemodynamically integrating hemodynamic results with structural device behavior in one framework. An aneurysm model was reconstructed from computed tomography imaging of a patient, and computational fluid dynamics evaluated multiple hemodynamic metrics across three flow-diversion strategies. Finite element analysis assessed stent geometries with 50%, 55%, and 60% porosity in 316L stainless steel, poly-L-lactic acid, and nitinol. Universal testing machine tests validated the models with printed polylactic acid and thermoplastic polyurethane analogues. Dimensional and elastic-tube analyses tested scale equivalence between the FEA and UTM geometries and the rigid-wall CFD assumption. Patient-specific CFD confirmed a high-risk hemodynamic profile. The stent yielded the lowest peak intra-sac velocity, greatest pressure reduction, near-zero wall shear stress, the only reduction in time-averaged wall shear stress, cycle-averaged TAWSS, and the largest peak-systolic reductions in velocity, WSS, and vorticity. OSI and RRT rose for all three treated configurations, consistent with the hemodynamic signature of flow diversion. FEA reproduced the expected stiffness hierarchy (Steel > Nitinol > PLLA), and TPU was the closest surrogate for Nitinol’s elastic recovery. Scaled specimens matched native-scale stiffness within 2.3%. Predicted radial distension was orders of magnitude below native wall values, supporting rigid-wall CFD. Stent-assisted diversion demonstrated the most favorable hemodynamic profile. A 50%-porosity Nitinol stent best matched target elastic mechanics, while 316L stainless steel provided the greatest resistance to radial compression.
W7222968137.title: Hemodynamic-Structural Multi-Fidelity Assessment of Endovascular Flow Diversion Strategies for Cerebral Aneurysm Treatment: An Integrated Computational and Experimental Framework

W7222970934.abstract: Melatonin (N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine) (MLT) is a naturally occurring hormone produced endogenously, primarily in the suprachiasmatic nucleus. MLT exhibits a plethora of uses particularly in the treatment of sleep disorders (sleep onset and maintenance). However, due to its short biological half-life, MLT cannot maintain effective plasma concentrations for a prolonged period when it is exogenously taken from immediate-release formulations. The present study aims at developing modified release systems capable of gradually releasing MLT, thereby sustaining its pharmacological effect over eight hours. To this end, modified-release tablets were prepared using new polymeric excipients based on polylactic acid (PLA). Both neat PLA and PLA copolymers with polyethylene glycols (PEGs) of varying molecular weights (PLLA-PEG-PLLA_4000, PLLA-PEG-PLLA_6000, and PLLA-PEG-PLLA_8000) were used, along with other excipients. Certain formulations delivered MLT comparatively fast and may therefore be useful for sleep onset problems, others matched the release behaviour of the marketed product Circadin®, and the rest released the hormone in a more prolonged manner.
W7222970934.title: Probing Melatonin’s Release Pattern from Oral Solid Dosage Forms Using Synthetic Biopolymers

W7222975636.abstract: Abstract Temporary plugging and diverting technology is an effective method for enhancing fracture complexity during repeated fracturing operations. PLA-based temporary plugging agents have attracted extensive attention due to their high mechanical strength and environmental friendliness. However, their relatively low softening temperature and poor balance between stiffness and toughness significantly restrict their applicability in deep reservoirs. In this study, a composite biodegradable temporary plugging agent (CB-TPA) with stable interfacial adhesion morphology and excellent physical properties was prepared by a two-step reactive blending with polylactic acid (PLA), polyglycolic acid (PGA), polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT), and a reactive elastomer (ADR). Experimental results indicated that at a PLA/PGA (70:30) to PBAT mass ratio of 3:1, the tensile strength, Vicat softening temperature, and impact toughness reached 64.4 MPa, 110 °C, and 7.7 kJ/m2, respectively. The material had a lower stiffness loss due to the improved compatibility, demonstrating well-balanced heat resistance, toughness, and stiffness. The simulated plugging experiments showed that CB-TPA could effectively withstand pressures up to 20 MPa at 160 °C, which is superior to that of commercial PLA temporary plugging agents. Under aqueous conditions at 160 °C, the weight loss of CB-TPA reached 96.7% within 4 h. The successful development of this composite biodegradable temporary plugging agent provides a new sustainable solution for the exploitation of deep unconventional oil and gas resources.
W7222975636.title: Strong, Tough, and High-Temperature-Resistant Biodegradable Temporary Plugging Agents for Refracturing in Deep Reservoirs by Two-Step Reactive Extrusion

W7222978400.abstract: The development of protein-based bioplastics from renewable agricultural resources provides a promising route towards alternative polymeric materials derived from non-petroleum feedstocks. This study investigated the effect of maleic acid concentration on the structural, morphological, and spectroscopic characteristics of sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) protein bioplastic films. Sesame protein isolate was prepared through alkaline extraction followed by acid precipitation and subsequently modified with 4% and 5% maleic acid to obtain 4MX and 5MX formulations, respectively. The modified protein materials were plasticised with glycerol and processed into films before characterisation by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. XRD patterns exhibited broad diffraction features characteristic of predominantly disordered protein-based structures. The principal reflection shifted from 2θ = 16.800° for 4MX to 17.800° for 5MX, corresponding to calculated interplanar spacings of 5.2778 and 4.9835 Å, respectively. Thus, increasing maleic acid concentration produced a 1.000° shift in the principal reflection and an approximately 5.57% reduction in calculated d-spacing. SEM examination revealed concentration-dependent differences in surface organisation, including variations in surface texture, interconnected regions and voids. FTIR spectra retained characteristic protein amide absorptions, while the broad O–H/N–H stretching band shifted from 3261.46 cm−1 for 4MX to 3248.38 cm−1 for 5MX, representing a 13.08 cm−1 shift. The combined XRD, SEM and FTIR findings demonstrate that increasing maleic acid concentration from 4% to 5% alters the structural organisation, surface morphology and molecular environment of the sesame-protein matrix. However, the available data do not independently establish covalent esterification, increased crosslink density, or improved functional performance. Further mechanical, barrier, thermal and controlled chemical analyses are required to establish the structure–property relationships of the resulting films.

W7222978400.title: Sesame Seed Protein Bioplastic Films Modified with Maleic Acid: Structural, Morphological and Functional-Group Characterizations

W7222983953.abstract: Injectable biodegradable polymers and micronized acellular dermal matrix (mADM) have potentially complementary regenerative properties, but how their combination shapes the host response remains poorly defined. In many systems, polymers provide persistent material-associated stimulation that may sustain macrophage-driven foreign-body responses, whereas mADM provides tissue-derived extracellular matrix (ECM) cues that support cellular infiltration, vascularization, and remodeling, with persistence dependent on processing and host-mediated replacement. This narrative review evaluates whether changes in macrophage population states could help explain potential polymer–mADM synergy. Across the reviewed polymer–ECM hybrid studies, most evidence is indirect, and temporal sampling rarely resolves sequential state changes. No included study establishes temporal coupling as a causal mechanism. We therefore propose a temporal macrophage-switching model in which both components act from implantation and their relative contributions change over time; their spatiotemporal overlap may shape macrophage population trajectories and remodeling outcomes. We further define a functional macrophage polarization window using biological landmarks rather than fixed time points. The model remains a testable hypothesis whose applicability depends on material and tissue context. Validation requires polymer-only, mADM-only, and hybrid comparisons across independent mADM lots, with systematic variation in polymer persistence, mADM processing, component ratio, spatial organization, and degradation/remodeling kinetics.
W7222983953.title: Micronized Acellular Dermal Matrix and Synthetic Polymers: Temporal Macrophage Transition as a Mechanistic Framework

W7222988324.abstract: The growing demand for sustainable materials in landscape architecture has highlighted the potential of polylactic acid/polybutylene adipate-terephthalate (PLA/PBAT)-based wood-plastic composites. However, poor interfacial compatibility between the hydrophilic plant fibers and the hydrophobic polyester matrices, coupled with susceptibility to hydrolytic degradation, limits their outdoor applications. This study presents a synergistic modification strategy for bamboo powder using a silane coupling agent (KH550) and nano-silica (Nano-SiO2), integrating all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with accelerated aging experiments to elucidate the enhancement mechanism of "chemical bridging–physical filling. " MD simulations revealed that the modification forms a dense "core-shell" barrier via covalent anchoring and a robust hydrogen-bond network, reducing the interfacial free volume to 14.1 % and lowering the water molecule self-diffusion coefficient from 4.58 × 10–7 to 0.42 × 10–7 cm2 s–1. This microscopic moisture barrier underpins the macroscopic aging resistance. Accelerated UV-condensation aging tests (1000 h) confirmed that the modified composites preserved the polyester backbone, with a weight-average molecular weight retention of 88.4 %, a tensile strength of 84.3 %, and an impact strength of 81.2 %. The surface color change was limited to E = 4.2, markedly outperforming unmodified composites. Additionally, the initial properties were improved: water absorption decreased from 4.25 % to 1.85 %, tensile strength reached 46.5 MPa, and impact strength reached 6.2 kJ m–2, achieving concurrent rigidity and toughness enhancement. These results demonstrate that nano-synergistic modification effectively mitigates weathering-induced degradation in PLA/PBAT composites, offering a practical pathway for their sustainable application in outdoor landscape environments.

W7222994370.abstract: Abstract Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (P3HB) stands out as a microbial biopolymer with biodegradable properties, offering a sustainable alternative to petroleum-based plastic. However, its application is hindered by brittleness and processing challenges, partially attributed to its fully (R)-isotactic stereocenter configuration. The enzymes responsible for P3HB production, polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) synthases, are traditionally considered to be strictly stereospecific, causing P3HB isotacticity. In this study, we developed an in vitro assay to analyze the stereospecificity of this enzyme class. Our investigation of PHA synthases reveals that the enzymes from Allochromatium vinosum and Chromobacterium sp. USM2, despite belonging to different PHA synthase classes and having low sequence identity, share the trait of not strictly adhering to stereospecificity. Notably, they demonstrate the capability of producing stereoirregular P3HB in vitro. Furthermore, we identified two key limitations influencing the production of stereoirregular P3HB in vitro. First, PHA synthases appear to require a high (S)- over (R)-substrate ratio. Second, under (R)-limiting conditions, the resulting stereoirregular P3HB exhibits a lower molar mass compared to its isotactic counterpart. Our findings challenge the assumption of universally strict stereospecificity among the PHA synthases tested and identify factors governing stereoirregular P3HB formation under assay conditions. The developed assay may support future enzyme engineering efforts aimed at tuning P3HB stereochemistry and ultimately polymer properties.
W7222994370.title: Selected PHA Synthases Exhibit Nonstrict Stereospecificity and Produce Stereoirregular Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) In Vitro

W7222995807.abstract: Biochar composites are promising for electromagnetic wave absorption due to their renewability and low cost, but performance optimization remains a challenge. Here, hollow CoFe/CoFe2O4 composite nanoparticles, in which the CoFe and CoFe2O4 phases coexist, are grown in situ on lotus-leaf-derived porous carbon via a Kirkendall-type process during heat treatment. The optimized composite (pyrolyzed at 800 °C) exhibits a saturation magnetization of 69.20 emu/g and a coercivity of 482 Oe; a calculated minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −71.4 dB is obtained at a matching thickness of 2.70 mm, with an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 5.68 GHz at 1.70 mm, covering most of the Ku band. The enhanced microwave absorption performance is attributed to the synergy of dielectric and magnetic losses, polarization relaxations, and improved impedance matching, together with multiple scattering within the hollow structure. In addition, the exchange coupling between the FeCo and CoFe2O4 may contribute to magnetic dissipation, while hollow cavities may promote internal reflections for further energy attenuation. This work provides a biomass-derived route to high-performance biochar-based absorbers competitive with synthetic counterparts.
W7222995807.title: Boosting Microwave Absorption via Hollow CoFe/CoFe2O4 Nanoparticles Anchored on Lotus-Leaf-Derived Biochar

W7222996889.abstract: The depletion of fossil resources and increasing plastic-derived pollution have become major environmental concerns. In this context, biodegradable biopolymers such as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) have attracted considerable scientific interest. Microalgae and cyanobacteria represent promising photosynthetic microorganisms for sustainable bioplastic production. In this study, ten microalgal species (Parachlorella kessleri, Chlorella vulgaris, Chlorella minutissima, Tetraselmis tetrathele, Chromochloris zofigiensis, Acutodesmus obliquus, Euglena gracilis, Chlorococcum oleofaciens, Botryococcus braunii, and Coelastrella vacuolata) and four cyanobacterial species (Arthrospira platensis, Nostoc muscorum, Chlorogloeopsis fritschii, and Synechocystis sp.) were screened for growth and PHA accumulation. Cultivation was performed under autotrophic conditions, mixotrophic growth with acetate, mixotrophic growth in anaerobic digestion effluent, and nitrogen-depleted conditions. Arthrospira platensis showed the highest PHA content under autotrophic growth, reaching 4.3% w/w. Most species adapted successfully to anaerobic digestion effluent, achieving total nitrogen and phosphorus removal above 90% in most cases, although PHA accumulation remained low (0.6–1.3% w/w). Acetate supplementation and nitrogen limitation markedly enhanced PHA accumulation. Mixotrophic cultivation with acetate yielded up to 10.2% w/w in cyanobacteria, whereas nitrogen starvation increased accumulation further, with Synechocystis sp. reaching 14.4% w/w. Overall, cyanobacteria outperformed green microalgae, supporting their potential for sustainable bioplastic production. These findings provide a basis for species selection and future process optimization.
W7222996889.title: Microalgae and Cyanobacteria Species Valorization Towards Sustainable Bioplastics Production

W7223020977.abstract: The oral route remains the most preferred route for drug administration due to its ease and patient acceptance, but conventional dosage forms require frequent dosing which leads to fluctuations in plasma drug levels. To overcome this problem, sustained release matrix tablets have been developed as an effective alternative. In this system, the drug is uniformly dispersed within a polymer matrix that controls its release over an extended period of time. Various types of polymers such as hydrophilic polymers like hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, hydrophobic polymers like ethyl cellulose and natural polymers like xanthan gum and guar gum are used as release retardants. The release of drug from matrix tablet takes place mainly by diffusion through gel layer, swelling of polymer and slow erosion of matrix. Recently, the field has witnessed remarkable innovations including blending of natural and synthetic polymers, introduction of gastro-retentive and mucoadhesive matrix systems, application of 3D printing for personalized tablets and development of pH sensitive smart matrices. These advancements have improved the efficiency and safety of matrix systems. Looking ahead, the combination of biodegradable polymers, nanocarriers and artificial intelligence based design is expected to make matrix tablets more targeted, sustainable and patient friendly. This review summarizes the current status, release mechanisms, recent developments and future scope of matrix tablets for sustained drug delivery.

W7223020977.title: A Review on Matrix Tablet for Sustained Drug Release

W7223029906.abstract: The global prevalence of geogenically derived cadmium (Cd) enrichment poses significant risks to agricultural sustainability and food security. Micronutrients such as selenium (Se) usually co-occur with Cd in such regions but exhibit low bioavailability in soils, further causing a “hidden hunger” of nutrient depletion in the food supply chain. Through controlled field experiments, we tested strategically designed biochar-based amendments (clay-, manure-, and iron-enriched variants) at 5–20 t ha −1 on limestone-derived paddy soils to synchronously mitigate Cd mobility while enhancing grain Se accumulation. Biochar amendments decreased grain Cd bioaccumulation by 42.3–85.4% and increased grain Se bioaccumulation by 91.6–357.5% across both growing seasons, with a better effect observed in synergy with yield increase in the second growing season, reflecting longer-term soil conditioning and progressive weathering of the amendments. Among the three amendments, BC-ZVI at 10–20 t ha −1 achieved the fastest and most consistent Cd immobilization, lowering grain Cd below the national safety threshold (0.2 mg kg −1 ) in both growing seasons while increasing grain Se by 91.6–357.5%. BC-Clay and BC-Manure required the second season to reach comparable Cd performance across all application rates. Elevations in soil pH, CEC, and available phosphorus may have accounted for the (im)mobilization effect. Field and literature data further indicated a decoupling between soil total Cd-Se co-enrichment and their mobile or plant-accumulated pools. Findings from this study demonstrate a practical and effective strategy for producing Se-enriched, low-Cd rice in regions with elevated geogenic Cd-Se background.

W7223029906.title: Field application of biochar-based amendments for safe crop production in karst paddy with a high geological background: Unraveling Cd-Se dynamics

W7223032399.abstract: Polylactide (PLA) is one of the most widely studied biodegradable polymers. However, poly(meso-lactide) (PMLA), an amorphous PLA, remains poorly characterized. This study investigates the thermal, rheological behavior, and morphology of poly(l-lactide) (PLLA) and PMLA blends across a wide composition range. Characterizations were performed using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), small amplitude oscillatory shear (SAOS) rheology, and atomic force microscopy (AFM). Nanoscale heterogeneity is suspected for the 10% and 90% w/w% HMW PLLA/HMW PMLA compositions, while 30 w% HMW PLLA, 50 w% HMW PLLA, and 70 w% HMW PLLA compositions exhibited immiscibility. DSC revealed two glass transition temperatures for 30 w% HMW PLLA, 50 w% HMW PLLA, and 70 w% HMW PLLA blends, corresponding to those of the neat phases, 48.2 ± 0.1 °C for HMW PMLA and 61.8 ± 0.4 °C for HMW PLLA, and a single Tg for the 10% and 90% w/w% HMW PLLA/HMW PMLA composition blends. AFM revealed an emulsion-type morphology at 30 and 70 wt. % HMW PLLA compositions and a co-continuous structure at 50 wt. % HMW PLLA. SAOS results presented a shoulder in the low frequency storage modulus for all blends. The Palierne model was used to fit the dynamic data of the blends and estimated the dispersed phase relaxation time, reinforcing the immiscibility conclusions. Relaxation spectra were obtained for all blends, showing two distinct relaxation modes associated with PLA nature and the interfacial tension of the blend. These results suggest that PMLA and PLLA are largely immiscible.
W7223032399.title: Morphological, thermal, and rheological behavior of poly( l -lactide) and poly( meso- lactide) blends

W7223042110.abstract: Background: It is highly desirable to address the dual therapeutic needs of quickly alleviating clinical symptoms and providing long-lasting effects for motion sickness, as well as to overcome limitations of traditional electrospinning methods—such as easy drug mixing, poor zoning accuracy, and inadequate controlled-release capabilities. Methods: This study developed a self-developed trifluid electrospinning device. This device was used to create a dual-drug loaded nanofiber membrane containing diphenhydramine (DP) and scopolamine hydrobromide (SH), featuring a zoned structure composed of a polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) crescent side chamber, a round polylactic acid (PLA) sheath chamber, and a round PLA core chamber. Results: The results demonstrated that the fibers maintained an intact structure with distinct interfaces, allowing precise zoned loading of the two drugs, which were present in an amorphous dispersed state, indicating good compatibility and structural stability. The nanofiber membrane showed moderate mechanical strength and excellent hydrophilicity, making it suitable for oral mucosal drug delivery. Asynchronous drug delivery, featuring a rapid release of DP (53% at 1 h) and a sustained release of SH (85% at 12 h with no noticeable burst phenomenon), was demonstrated using two types of hierarchically structured nanofibers, each loaded with a single drug to facilitate measurement. The release mechanisms were disclosed for DP and SH from the tri-chamber hierarchical nanofibers. Cell studies confirmed its good biocompatibility. Conclusions: This work offers new insights and experimental evidence for developing an effective synergistic oral delivery system for motion sickness and advancing multifunctional nanocarrier drug delivery platforms.
W7223042110.title: An Electrospun Core–Sheath/Janus-Integrated Hierarchical Structure for Asynchronous Mucosal Drug Delivery

W7223042232.abstract: नैनोपार्टिकल-मॉडिफाइड इंट्राथिकल वायरल डिलीवरी द्वारा वंशानुगत स्पास्टिक पैराप्लेजिया (HSP) के लिए इन-विवो जीन रिपेयर और एंडोजेनस एक्टिवेशन पद्धति प्रधान आविष्कारक (Lead Inventor): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) अनुसंधान क्षेत्र (Field of Invention): नैनो-बायोटेक्नोलॉजी, जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग, न्यूरोलॉजी सारांश (ABSTRACT) यह अनुसंधान प्रधान आविष्कारक बंटी कुमावत द्वारा वंशानुगत स्पास्टिक पैराप्लेजिया (HSP) के स्थाई उपचार के लिए विकसित की गई एक क्रांतिकारी चिकित्सा पद्धति को प्रस्तुत करता है। पारंपरिक जीन थेरेपी के विपरीत, जो शरीर में बाहरी या कृत्रिम जीन प्रविष्ट कराती है, यह तकनीक मरीज के केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (CNS) के भीतर ही पहले से मौजूद निष्क्रिय, सोए हुए या म्यूटेटेड (दोषपूर्ण) जीनों को लक्षित करके उन्हें सुधारने और पुनः सक्रिय करने पर केंद्रित है। इस पद्धति द्वारा मुख्य रूप से SPAST (SPG4), ATL1 (SPG3A), REEP1 (SPG31), और SPG7 जीनों को लक्षित किया जाता है। रीढ़ की हड्डी की सुरक्षात्मक दीवार यानी ब्लड-ब्रेन बैरियर (BBB) की कठिन चुनौती को पार करने के लिए, आविष्कारक ने एक अनूठा नैनो-इंजीनियर्ड वायरल वेक्टर तैयार किया है। इसे सीधे रीढ़ की हड्डी के तरल पदार्थ (CSF) में सिंगल-डोज़ इंट्राथिकल इंजेक्शन (Intrathecal Injection) के माध्यम से पहुंचाया जाता है। यह तकनीक HSP के मूल आनुवंशिक कारण को समाप्त कर इस प्रगतिशील तंत्रिका विकार के लिए एक स्थाई समाधान प्रस्तुत करती है। 1. प्रस्तावना और समस्या का विवरण (INTRODUCTION & PROBLEM STATEMENT) वंशानुगत स्पास्टिक पैराप्लेजिया (HSP) दुर्लभ आनुवंशिक विकारों का एक समूह है, जिसमें रीढ़ की हड्डी के कॉर्टिकोस्पाइनल ट्रैक्ट (corticospinal tracts) में तंत्रिका कोशिकाएं (axons) धीरे-धीरे नष्ट होने लगती हैं। इसके परिणामस्वरूप पैरों में अत्यधिक जकड़न और कमजोरी आ जाती है। वर्तमान में चिकित्सा विज्ञान में इसका कोई प्रामाणिक इलाज नहीं है और उपचार केवल लक्षणों को कम करने तक ही सीमित है। HSP के लगभग 70-80% मामलों के लिए मुख्य रूप से चार जीन जिम्मेदार होते हैं: 1. SPAST (SPG4): यह 'स्पैस्टिन' प्रोटीन बनाता है, जो तंत्रिका कोशिकाओं के ढांचे और परिवहन के लिए अत्यंत आवश्यक है। 2. ATL1 (SPG3A): यह 'एटलास्टिन-1' प्रोटीन बनाता है, जो एंडोप्लाज्मिक रेटिकुलम (ER) झिल्ली के संतुलन को बनाए रखता है। 3. REEP1 (SPG31) और SPG7: ये तंत्रिका कोशिकाओं के भीतर माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और ऊर्जा संतुलन को नियंत्रित करते हैं। पारंपरिक जीन-रिप्लेसमेंट थेरेपी (बाहर से नया जीन डालना) में शरीर द्वारा दवा को अस्वीकार करने (Immune Rejection) और अनियंत्रित मात्रा में प्रोटीन बनने (Dosage Toxicity) का भारी जोखिम रहता है। इसके अलावा, ब्लड-ब्रेन बैरियर (BBB) के कारण सामान्य दवाएं प्रभावित मोटर न्यूरॉन्स तक आवश्यक मात्रा में नहीं पहुंच पाती हैं। 2. बंटी कुमावत द्वारा प्रस्तावित नवोन्मेषी कार्यप्रणाली (THE INNOVATIVE MECHANISM BY BANTI KUMAWAT) बंटी कुमावत द्वारा खोजी गई यह आणविक रणनीति शरीर में किसी भी प्रकार के कृत्रिम या बाहरी जेनेटिक सीक्वेंस को डालने का पूरी तरह निषेध करती है। इसके बजाय, यह तीन प्रमुख चरणों के माध्यम से शरीर के अपने ही प्राकृतिक जेनेटिक तंत्र का उपयोग करती है: क. एंडोजेनस जीन रिपेयर और क्रिस्पर एक्टिवेशन (CRISPRa) यह थेरेपी कोशिकाओं के भीतर मौजूद SPAST, ATL1, REEP1, और SPG7 के म्यूटेटेड या निष्क्रिय पड़े मूल जीनों को लक्षित करती है। इसके लिए CRISPR-Activation (CRISPRa) प्रणाली का उपयोग किया जाता है, जिसमें एक निष्क्रिय प्रोटीन (dCas9) के साथ रासायनिक एक्टिवेटर्स को जोड़ा जाता है। यह टूल डीएनए को बिना काटे, निष्क्रिय पड़े जीनों के स्विच (Promoter regions) से जुड़कर उन्हें वापस सक्रिय कर देता है। इसके साथ ही, नैनो-लक्षित बेस-एडिटिंग टूल्स जीन के भीतर मौजूद म्यूटेशन (खराबी) को उसी स्थान पर (in situ) ठीक कर देते हैं, जिससे कोशिकाएं पुनः शुद्ध और प्राकृतिक प्रोटीन बनाने लगती हैं। ख. नैनो-इंजीनियर्ड वायरल वेक्टर डिलीवरी सिस्टम इन संवेदनशील जीन-रेगुलेशन टूल्स को सुरक्षा प्रदान करने और न्यूरॉन्स के भीतर सटीक प्रवेश सुनिश्चित करने के लिए एडेनो-असोसिएटेड वायरस सेरोटाइप 9 (AAV9) को नैनोकणों (लिपिड या पॉलीमेरिक नैनोपार्टिकल्स) के साथ कम्बाइन करके एक नैनो-शेल (सुरक्षा कवच) तैयार किया गया है। यह नैनो-कोटिंग वायरस को शरीर के इम्यून सिस्टम से बचाती है और इसे विशेष रूप से केवल रीढ़ की हड्डी के प्रभावित मोटर न्यूरॉन्स कोशिकाओं के प्रति संवेदनशील बनाती है। ग. इंट्राथिकल रूट (Intrathecal Delivery Route) ब्लड-ब्रेन बैरियर (BBB) को पूरी तरह से बायपास करने के लिए, इस नैनो-मॉडिफाइड वायरल फॉर्मूलेशन को सीधे रीढ़ की हड्डी के निचले हिस्से (Lumbar space) में मौजूद सेरेब्रोस्पाइनल फ्लूइड (CSF) के भीतर इंजेक्ट किया जाता है। इस मार्ग से दवा बिना किसी जैविक रुकावट के सीधे रीढ़ की हड्डी के प्रभावित हिस्सों तक पहुंचती है और कोशिकाओं द्वारा तुरंत ग्रहण कर ली जाती है। 3. इस आविष्कार के अभूतपूर्व लाभ (ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION) • शून्य इम्यून रिजेक्शन: चूंकि थेरेपी पूरी तरह से शरीर के अपने ही आंतरिक जीनों के सुधार और सक्रियण पर आधारित है, इसलिए मरीज का इम्यून सिस्टम इस प्रक्रिया का विरोध नहीं करता। • सिंगल-डोज़ क्योर: यह एक बार दिया जाने वाला (One-time) इंजेक्शन है, जो तंत्रिका परिवहन को स्थायी रूप से ठीक करके जीवनभर के लिए HSP के बढ़ने को रोक सकता है। • प्राकृतिक जैविक संतुलन (Homeostasis): एंडोजेनस सक्रियण के कारण कोशिकाएं उतनी ही मात्रा में प्रोटीन का निर्माण करेंगी जितनी शरीर को प्राकृतिक आवश्यकता है, जिससे ओवर-एक्सप्रेशन (सीमित मात्रा से अधिक प्रोटीन बनने) का खतरा समाप्त हो जाता है। 4. निष्कर्ष (CONCLUSION) बंटी कुमावत द्वारा प्रस्तावित यह नैनो-असिस्टेड इन-विवो जीन रिपेयर तकनीक न्यूरोलॉजी के क्षेत्र में एक नए युग की शुरुआत करती है। नैनोटेक्नोलॉजी की सटीकता को आंतरिक आनुवंशिक सुधार और इंट्राथिकल डिलीवरी के साथ जोड़कर, यह आविष्कार न केवल HSP के मरीजों को पूर्णतः स्वस्थ करने का व्यावहारिक मार्ग प्रशस्त करता है, बल्कि ALS और SMA जैसे अन्य जटिल तंत्रिका विकारों के उपचार के लिए भी एक ठोस आधार तैयार करता है। वैज्ञानिक निर्माण विधि: नैनो-शील्डेड इन-विवो जीन रिपेयर इंजेक्शन आविष्कारक: बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) 1. सबसे सुरक्षित वायरस का चयन (Selection of Viral Vector) इस थेरेपी के लिए हम Adeno-Associated Virus Serotype 9 (AAV9) का चयन करेंगे। • कारण: AAV9 एक गैर-हानिकारक (Non-pathogenic) वायरस है जो इंसानों में कोई बीमारी नहीं फैलाता। इसकी सबसे बड़ी खूबी यह है कि यह रीढ़ की हड्डी की तंत्रिका कोशिकाओं (Motor Neurons) को बहुत पसंद करता है और सीधे उनके भीतर प्रवेश कर सकता है। 2. इम्यून सिस्टम से बचाने के लिए विशेष कोटिंग (Immune Shield Co-polymers) शरीर का इम्यून सिस्टम (Antibodies) वायरस को देखते ही नष्ट करने की कोशिश करता है। इसे रोकने के लिए, आपके विचार के अनुसार वायरस की बाहरी परत (Capsid) पर एक रासायनिक सुरक्षा कवच (Nano-Shield) लगाया जाएगा। इसके लिए PEG-PLA (Polyethylene Glycol - Polylactic Acid) Block Co-polymers और Lipid Nano-shells का उपयोग किया जाएगा। यह कोटिंग एक "अदृश्य चोगे" (Stealth Cloak) की तरह काम करती है, जिससे हमारी प्रतिरक्षा प्रणाली (Immunity) इसे पहचान नहीं पाती और रिजेक्ट नहीं करती। 3. इंजेक्शन बनाने की चरण-दर-चरण विधि (Step-by-Step Manufacturing Protocol) यह प्रक्रिया एक उच्च-स्तरीय बायो-लैब (Cleanroom Class 100 / ISO 5) में पूरी की जाती है: चरण 1: वायरल वेक्टर का उत्पादन (Vector Production) 1. लैब में HEK293 (Human Embryonic Kidney) कोशिकाओं का संवर्धन (Culture) करें। 2. इन कोशिकाओं में तीन प्लास्मिड (DNA मॉलिक्यूल) डालें (Triple Transfection Technique): • Plasmid 1: जिसमें AAV9 के बढ़ने के जरूरी जीन (Rep/Cap) हों। • Plasmid 2: हेल्पर प्लास्मिड (Helper Genes)। • Plasmid 3 (आपका फॉर्मूला): जिसमें SPAST, ATL1, या REEP1 जीन को सक्रिय करने वाला CRISPRa (dCas9-VPR) का जेनेटिक कोड लोड हो। 3. 72 घंटे बाद, कोशिकाओं को तोड़कर AAV9 वायरस के कणों को बाहर निकालें। 4. Ultracentrifugation तकनीक से वायरस को पूरी तरह शुद्ध (Purify) करें ताकि कोई अवांछित तत्व न बचे। चरण 2: नैनो-इम्यून शील्ड कोटिंग (Nanoparticle Encapsulation) 1. शुद्ध किए गए AAV9 वायरस को एक बफर सॉल्यूशन (PBS, pH 7.4) में रखें। 2. एक अलग बीकर में Lipids (जैसे DOTAP, Cholesterol) और PEG-PLA Polymers को ऑर्गेनिक सॉल्वेंट (Ethanol) में घोलें। 3. एक Microfluidic Mixer (नैनो-मिक्सिंग मशीन) की मदद से, वायरस वाले लिक्विड और नैनो-पॉलिमर वाले लिक्विड को बहुत तेज गति से एक निश्चित दबाव पर आपस में मिलाएं। 4. इस प्रक्रिया से नैनो-पॉलिमर स्वतः ही वायरस के चारों ओर एक 80-100 नैनोमीटर मोटी इम्यून-शील्ड परत (Stealth Nano-coating) बना लेते हैं। चरण 3: गुणवत्ता नियंत्रण और पैकेजिंग (Quality Control & Formulation) 1. Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS): मशीन से जांचें कि तैयार नैनो-वायरस का आकार 100 नैनोमीटर से कम हो, ताकि यह रीढ़ की हड्डी के फ्लूइड में आसानी से तैर सके। 2. W7223043798.abstract: The anisotropic shrinkage of wood during carbonization critically affects biochar microstructure, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We examined shrinkage behavior in the radial (R) and longitudinal (L) directions in relation to polysaccharide thermal degradation, exchangeable cation species, and cell structure, using ten wood species (five softwoods and five hardwoods) and their cation-exchanged derivatives (H + , Na + , K + , Mg 2+ , Ca 2+ ). Thermogravimetric and continuous dimensional analyses revealed that the onset of shrinkage in the R-direction is primarily associated with hemicellulose degradation, whereas shrinkage in the L-direction is linked to cellulose degradation and occurs rapidly at temperatures 10–20 °C higher than the derivative thermogravimetric peak, when most cellulose microfibrils have already decomposed. Na + and K + lowered shrinkage onset temperatures across most species, whereas in hardwoods, R-direction shrinkage magnitude increased with H + and Mg 2+ substitution. Anatomical differences, particularly in ray parenchyma morphology, explained why hardwoods generally shrank more in the R direction. These results demonstrate that anisotropic shrinkage during wood carbonization is governed by polysaccharide-specific thermal degradation, modulated by exchangeable cation species and anatomical features. Furthermore, directional shrinkage can be predictably tuned through cation control and species selection to optimize biochar microstructure.
W7223043798.title: Cell-wall chemistry governs anisotropic shrinkage during wood carbonization: roles of polysaccharide degradation and exchangeable cations

W7223047799.abstract: BACKGROUND: Filament deposition modeling (FDM) can be a practical method for producing quality control (QC) imaging resources for the clinic. However, frequent printing may degrade print quality over time. PURPOSE: To develop a process to ensure prints for the diagnostic physicist are accurate and reproducible. METHODS: Four FDM systems were evaluated by printing a custom, novel QC model on each printer 12 times over a period of 12 months. Several tests were performed, including print resolvability (lp/cm), XYZ dimension accuracy (mm), density (g/cm3), line width (mm), XY position accuracy (mm), clearance fits (mm), and thickness uniformity (mm). Polylactic acid (PLA) samples were printed, measured, and imaged with a dual energy CT scanner. Linear regression models were then created to monitor changes in QC density measurements as a function of x-ray and material property characteristics (i.e., Hounsfield units and electron density). Between monthly prints, heat uniformity across the build plate was also tested for each printer using a NIST-certified infrared thermometer and 3D printed grids. All physical measurements were obtained using a calibrated digital caliper and milligram scale. RESULTS: Mean percent error (MPE) for all tests was calculated from ground truth (CAD dimensions and filament density) and baseline values (first month of QC measurements). Among printers investigated, MPE was ± 5% of ground truth for all tests except density and thickness uniformity. Baseline MPE was also observed within ± 5% except for resolvability and clearance fit tests among printers. Subtle trend increases were presented for higher density QC prints based on DECT linear regression models. Reduced chi-squared values indicate uniform and reproducible heat bed temperature measurements. CONCLUSIONS: This work offers an innovative approach toward evaluating and monitoring FDM system performance. Future work should track performance over a longer time period and across a wider variety of printers.

W7223082439.abstract: Portland cement production contributes roughly 7–8% of global CO₂ emissions, which has driven interest in supplementary cementitious materials and carbon-sequestering additives. This study evaluates coconut-shell-derived biochar, used as a cement-weight additive at 0–5%, in a fly ash blended concrete system. Biochar was characterized by EDX (carbon 77–80%, oxygen 15–16%) and physical tests (specific gravity 1.60, fineness modulus 1.83, water absorption 15.8%). Concrete specimens were tested for compressive, split tensile and flexural strength at 7, 14 and 28 days, and for strength loss after sulphate attack, chloride attack and alternate wet–dry cycles. A 1% biochar dose gave the highest 28-day compressive strength (33.8 MPa, +7.0% over the 31.6 MPa control), and 2% gave 33.2 MPa (+5.1%). Doses of 3% and above gave no gain or a reduction. Early-age (7- and 14-day) split tensile and flexural strength improved at 1–3%, but 28-day tensile and flexural strengths were below the control for all dosages. Durability was best at 2% biochar, where strength loss was 2.2% (sulphate), 1.8% (chloride) and 2.8% (wet–dry), against 8.5%, 7.0% and 9.0% for the control. The results indicate that a low biochar dosage of about 1–2% can improve compressive strength and durability, while higher dosages are detrimental.

W7223084025.abstract: Abstract Given the population’s needs regarding the availability of treated water for communities, especially the most isolated ones, this study aimed to evaluate the behavior of physicochemical parameters: total iron (TI) and electrical conductivity (EC) as a function of pH, total dissolved solids (TDS) and temperature, in groundwater treatment, using slow filtration with cactus biochar as a filter layer. For this purpose, a hydraulic groundwater collection system (consisting of a pumping system and reservoirs) was used, coupled to a slow filter made of glass with a triple filtration layer (sand, biochar, and sand) and a constant filtration rate of approximately 3 m 3 /m 2 day, with variations in water level. Furthermore, the biochar was produced using biomass from the palm cactus, pyrolyzed at 450.0 °C for 30 min, without activation. Thus, the results indicated that EC correlated directly with temperature, with removals greater than 35% observed around 26.0 °C and pH 6.0. The TI also showed better removals (99.6%) under similar conditions, remaining below legal limits. The system was also efficient in reducing dissolved ions, evidenced by reduction in electrical conductivity. The minimal variations in pH and temperature were positive for the stability of the process. Therefore, it was observed that, although the large area required for slow sand filtration systems may limit their application in urban areas, the use of unconventional materials in this technology may represent an alternative for water treatment. Such studies may contribute to the development of more sustainable and accessible water treatment solutions for different application contexts.

W7223084224.abstract: Biochar derived from textile waste presents an opportunity in the circular economy for contaminant remediation from industrial wastewater. In this study, biochars derived from cotton and cotton-polyester blended textiles were assessed for the removal of the toxic and pervasive aqueous contaminant, hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)). Unmodified textile-derived biochars exhibited some adsorption capacity for Cr(VI) under environmentally relevant pH conditions, but removal improved substantially once modified with the cationic surfactant cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB). Adsorption experiments conducted at 50–100 mg/L as Cr showed equilibrium capacities of about 1.6–2.0 mg Cr/g BC for unmodified biochars, increasing to 10–15 mg Cr/g BC for CTAB-modified materials, with rapid adsorption in the first 5 minutes. Maximum adsorption capacity for CTAB-modified cotton and cotton-polyester biochar prepared at 450 o C was determined to be 72 and 32 mg Cr/g BC, respectively, comparable to established adsorbents. Adsorption-desorption experiments conducted using low (10 mM NaCl) and high (500 mM NaCl) ionic strength showed apparent anion exchange capacities of ~0.08 to 0.09 meq/g, suggesting that chromium retention involves ion exchange with CTAB-derived quaternary ammonium sites in addition to electrostatic attraction. Similar adsorption behavior between feedstocks suggests that surfactant modification played a larger role in overall performance than feedstock composition. These findings demonstrate that textile-derived biochar can be engineered through surfactant modification to enhance the removal efficiency of industrially-relevant anionic contaminants like Cr(VI), supporting their potential use as low-cost sorbents for industrial wastewater treatment.

W7223087136.abstract: The production of biochar from rice-husk biomass has shown significant potential to counter climate change and waste management issues. The current study assesses changes in elemental, structural and thermal characteristics of biochar produced at 380 °C, 400 °C, and 420 °C at a residence time of 2 h. The study also calculates the CO 2eq that is stored in biochar post-pyrolysis. The methodology adopted includes biochar production through pyrolysis, phase analysis, elemental analysis and CO 2eq calculations. Phase analysis revealed destruction of the cellulosic phase and development of amorphous silica following pyrolysis. CHNS analysis showed increasing carbon concentration together with decreasing H/C and O/C atomic ratios, indicating enhanced aromatic condensation and increasing carbon recalcitrance during thermal treatment. Proximate analysis demonstrated substantial devolatilization, reduction in moisture and volatile matter, and enrichment of stabilized carbonaceous fractions. Biochar yield decreased from 60.108 g at 380 °C to 40.153 g at 420 °C because of increasing thermal decomposition and volatilization losses. The calculated retained CO 2eq values ranged from 93.127 g for BC380 to 67.846 g for BC420, indicating that lower pyrolysis temperatures retained larger quantities of biomass-derived carbon despite relatively lower thermal maturity. However, the higher carbon concentration at elevated temperature did not result in greater total carbon retention because biochar yield decreased substantially with temperature. BC380 therefore retained the greatest absolute quantity of carbon despite having a lower carbon concentration than BC420. The study highlights the importance of optimizing pyrolysis conditions to maximize both carbon retention efficiency and carbon stability for sustainable biochar-mediated carbon sequestration applications.

W7223089477.abstract: Introduction Olive mill wastewater (OMW) is characterized by a high organic load and complex composition, requiring efficient and sustainable treatment strategies. This study investigates the potential of biochar (BC) derived from olive mill solid waste (OMSW) as an adsorbent for the removal of total phenols (TPh) and chemical oxygen demand (COD) from OMW. Methods OMSW-derived BC was produced by slow pyrolysis at 600°C for 5 h and characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD). The BC exhibited a carbon content of 67.21%, a BET surface area of 135.2 m 2 /g, and a total pore volume of 0.0055 cm 3 /g. Batch adsorption experiments were conducted to evaluate the effects of contact time, BC dosage, and temperature. Adsorption kinetics, isotherms, and thermodynamic parameters were evaluated using established models. Results TPh adsorption followed a pseudo-second-order kinetic model with an excellent fit (R 2 = 1), whereas COD showed a weaker fit (R 2 = 0.76), indicating more complex adsorption behavior. Increasing the BC dosage from 0.05 to 0.5 g resulted in only limited improvements in removal efficiency, with COD removal increasing from 73.79% to 77.45% and TPh removal from 75.87% to 79.30%. Temperature significantly affected adsorption performance. COD removal reached 75.61% at 25°C and 79.46% at 35°C. TPh removal from OMW increased from 0.12% at 25°C to 19.15% at 35°C and reached 24% at 45°C. For the gallic acid (GA) solution, TPh removal reached 72.28% at 35°C before declining at 45°C. Isotherm analysis showed that the Freundlich model provided a better description of TPh adsorption at elevated temperatures, with R 2 = 0.9833 at 45°C. Thermodynamic analysis indicated that TPh adsorption was spontaneous and endothermic (ΔH° = +71.37 kJ/mol), with negative entropy suggesting increased ordering at the BC surface. Discussion The results demonstrate that OMSW-derived BC has potential as a sustainable adsorbent for the treatment of OMW, particularly for the removal of COD and phenolic compounds. The conversion of OMSW into BC provides an approach for valorizing an agricultural waste stream while producing an adsorbent with useful physicochemical properties. These findings support the potential application of agricultural waste-derived BC in targeted OMW treatment and contribute to more sustainable wastewater management practices in the olive oil sector.

W7223091709.abstract: Drum kilns lose a substantial fraction of their fuel energy through the wall, and in Zambia the materials best suited to reducing this loss are locally abundant and inexpensive. This paper presents a consolidated, literature-based assessment of the insulation materials available to a rural fabricator, comprising anthill (termite-mound) clay, clay–sand and cement–sand mixtures, fired clay brick, and, as a reference case, commercial ceramic fibre. The study is a structured cross-literature synthesis rather than a new experimental characterisation, and no specimens were tested. Measured data were assembled from the peer-reviewed literature through a documented search, the measurement method, test temperature, and specimen condition behind each value were recorded, and, because no validated conversion between methods exists, the values were reported as method-stratified ranges rather than numerically normalised across the guarded-hot-plate, transient plane-source, and laser-flash methods. The resulting trends in thermal conductivity, strength, and porosity were analysed against agro-waste content and firing temperature. Published analyses of anthill clay from Ghana, Nigeria, and Kenya, used here as analogues because no Zambian analysis was found, indicate a kaolinitic refractory raw material containing approximately 52 to 63 percent silica and 16 to 31 percent alumina; local XRF and XRD testing is therefore a prerequisite for design specification. Reported composites containing 10 to 15 weight percent sawdust exhibit room-temperature thermal conductivities of 0.26 to 0.32 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, comparable to fired insulating brick and roughly one fifth or less of the value for dense cement–sand mortar, while retaining cold crushing strengths of approximately 6 to 9 MPa, above a 5 MPa screening criterion adopted here for a self-supporting lining, provided the agro-waste fraction does not exceed approximately 15 weight percent. Ceramic fibre offers the lowest conductivity, near 0.07 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, but its fragility and cost render it unsuitable for the target context. None of the locally available materials simultaneously offers the lowest conductivity, adequate strength, and durability under thermal cycling; a layered wall, in which an anthill-clay composite performs the principal insulating function behind a thin protective face, is therefore proposed as a preliminary design implication that has yet to be tested experimentally or numerically. The compiled ranges, stratified by measurement method and traceable to their sources in a supplementary dataset, are intended as bounded inputs for subsequent modelling and for the local testing that must precede design.

W7223093349.abstract: This field experiment investigated the combined effects of straw and biochar on Black Soil physicochemical properties and soybean growth in cold regions, with four treatments: total straw return (TS), high straw + low biochar (PS), low straw + high biochar (PB), and total biochar (TB). Results showed biochar amendments improved soil physical structure: TB had the lowest bulk density (1.230 g/cm 3 ) and highest porosity (52.72%), with >0.25 mm macroaggregates increased by 28.4% relative to TS. Nutrient supply differed by treatment: TB and PB enhanced nitrogen and phosphorus availability throughout growth, while TS and PS favored potassium and dissolved organic carbon. TB and PB promoted better soybean growth indices (plant height, stem diameter, LAI). PB treatment obtained the highest soybean yield value among all groups, but no statistically significant difference in grain yield was detected among the four straw-biochar combined treatments. Straw–biochar co-application synergistically improved soil structure and regulated nutrients for early promotion and late stability. The PB ratio (13 t/hm 2 straw + 6 t/hm 2 biochar) performed best, effectively improving Black Soil fertility and increasing soybean yield.
W7223093349.title: Effects of co-application of straw and biochar on soil nutrients and soybean growth in black soil of cold regions

W7223107307.abstract: Abstract High-temperature shale oil and gas drilling calls for effective and environmentally friendly additives capable of control clay hydration, shale dispersion, and wellbore instability in water-based drilling fluids. In this study, we prepared an acid-modified biochar (BC)/poly(arginyl-lysine) (JL) composite, designated JL-BC, via physical blending, and then evaluated its inhibition performance by means of linear swelling and hot-rolling recovery tests. Under treatment withJL-BC solution, the sodium bentonite (Na-BT) swelling height decreased to 4.49 mm at 150 °C for 16 h, while shale cuttings recovery reached 92.1% after aging at 220 °C for 16 h, results that outperforming those of potassium chloride (KCl), polyetheramine (PEA), 2,3-epoxypropyltrimethylammonium chloride (EPTAC), and dopamine (DA). Furthermore, the water-based drilling fluid supplemented with JL-BC maintained good rheological behavior, fluid loss control and inhibition performance after aging at 180 °C for 16 h. Mechanistic analyses revealed that JL-BC adsorbed strongly onto clay surfaces via electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonding, thereby weakening the electrostatic repulsion between clay particles and reducing the amount of hydration-related water associated with Na-BT, which contributed to the inhibition of clay hydration and swelling. An environmental friendliness assessment showed that JL-BC was nontoxic and readily biodegradable, that it did not significantly increase soil heavy metal concentrations and promoted nutrient accumulation in wheat seedlings. Collectively, these findings indicate that JL-BC is a promising environmentally friendly shale inhibitor for high-temperature applications.
W7223107307.title: Acid-Modified Biochar/poly(arginyl-Lysine) Composite as an Environmentally Friendly High-Temperature Shale Inhibitor

W7223112145.abstract: Introduction Pyrolysis of waste biomass to generate biochar (BC) is an important technology for recycling and reusing biomass carbon, which promotes carbon neutrality. BC mechanisms toward ‘Carbon Neutrality' in conservation agro-ecosystems (CAESs) remain incompletely synthesized. BC application can promote soil aeration rates, thereby enhancing the biological oxidation of methane (CH 4 ). BC promotes photosynthesis, plant biomass, and health, providing ecological and financial benefits. Methods A review search methodology was adopted to comprehensively screen and synthesize the most relevant literature on the application of BC to promote carbon neutrality in CAESs. Results This review explores BC's potential benefits to achieve carbon neutrality in Conservation Agro-Ecosystems through two major pathways: (a) overground growth improvement and (b) underground-level carbon-pool enhancement. Nevertheless, BC's endogenous contaminants and long-term persistence suggest it could pose chronic ecological and environmental problems. This work provides an initial assessment of the function and mechanism of BC in facilitating carbon neutrality in CAESs. Furthermore, because BC has positive effects on plant development and soil improvement, it is recommended to develop BC-based sustainable soils. To date, significant hurdles remain in producing environmentally friendly BC, selecting the optimal type and amount of BC to apply, and applying it in accordance with local soil characteristics. Future studies should examine the processes by which BC promotes soil carbon sequestration and its long-term environmental impacts. Conclusion The extensive synthesis of standardized biochar should be broadened to guarantee the efficient integration of waste biomass and the sustainable production of biochar. A prerequisite for the smart implementation of BC is to ensure its durable application for carbon neutrality.
W7223112145.title: Biochar potential and mechanisms for advancing carbon-neutral conservation agroecosystems

W7223112763.abstract: Abstract Chemical recycling of bioplastics like poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) promotes a circular economy by overcoming mechanical recycling limitations. This study investigated PBAT glycolysis and subsequent repolymerization of crude glycolyzed products, integrated with an early-stage life cycle assessment (LCA) using OpenLCA software with the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) impact assessment method to anticipate potential environmental impacts and sensitivity of the system. Glycolysis was conducted at 150–190 °C using Sn(Bu)2O (0.15 to 1.40 mol %) and NaHCO3 (5.0 mol %), presenting a Lewis acid coordination mechanism and a base-assisted glycolysis pathway, respectively, with ethylene glycol or 1,4-butanediol (4:1 molar ratio). Parameters including molar mass distribution (Mn, Mw, and Đ), species profile, and monomer yield were evaluated. Full conversion of the polymeric matrix was achieved within 2–5 h, leaving no detectable high-molecular-weight PBAT and yielding a mixture of oligomers and monomers, even at low catalyst concentrations (0.15 mol %), yielding oligomers with Mw of 0.6–1.4 kDa and up to 26.6 wt % monomer fraction. Notably, repolymerization without preliminary purification achieved Mw up to 10.6 kDa, comparable to 11.5 kDa reached using virgin raw materials. LCA results demonstrated improvements in 14 impact categories, with reductions between 6% and 35%. While fossil resource scarcity, ozone formation (human health and terrestrial ecosystem), and global warming potential increased due to the fossil-intensive energy baseline, the chemical proof of concept of directly utilizing crude glycolyzed products highlights the potential of this one-pot route to mitigate environmental burdens in polyester recycling, pending further property optimization.
W7223112763.title: Chemical Recycling of Poly(butylene adipate- co -terephthalate): A Glycolysis–Repolymerization Approach

W7223122292.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) is evolving from a conventional waste-to-energy technology toward a multiproduct biorefinery platform capable of producing bioenergy and value-added bioproducts. However, production pathways compete for organic carbon and energy resources, and their technical, economic, and environmental performance depends on feedstock characteristics, operating conditions, downstream recovery requirements, and market demand. This narrative and critical review synthesizes methane, biohydrogen, volatile fatty acid (VFA), polyhydroxyalkanoate, single-cell protein, and digestate-derived product pathways, together with emerging options such as microbial chain elongation, biological methanation, and biogas CO2 utilization. It critically compares pathway-specific performance evidence and examines two-stage conversion, metabolic regulation, downstream integration, techno-economic analysis, life cycle assessment, multi-objective optimization, multi-criteria decision analysis, and data-driven prediction. Based on this literature synthesis, a conceptual closed-loop decision-support framework is proposed that connects monitoring, state prediction, feasible pathway generation, trade-off evaluation, preference-based selection, switching-feasibility assessment, operational adjustment, and feedback. A hypothetical numerical scenario illustrates how changes in VFA market conditions can alter pathway rankings, while technical constraints, transition costs, and biological recovery times can prevent implementation of a higher-scoring alternative. The framework is not an experimentally validated autonomous control system; its application requires plant-specific data, uncertainty analysis, and validation of transition feasibility and long-term process stability.
W7223122292.title: From Single-Objective Optimization to Dynamic Decision-Making: Pathway Trade-Offs and Synergies in Anaerobic Digestion for Bioenergy and Bioproduct Production

W7223125348.abstract: Biochar, as a soil amendment, offers several benefits, including increased soil fertility, carbon (C) sequestration, and improved water-holding capacity in nutrient-poor soils. This study assesses the impact of adding different rates of pine biochar to sandy peach-tree orchard soils on the relative abundance and structure of soil microbial communities (bacteria and fungi) after one year. Soil samples were collected from biochar-amended plots using two distinct application methods (incorporated and surface-applied) at two rates (5% and 10% v /v) after one year of application. Bacterial and fungal communities were analyzed by sequencing, and microbial metabolic functions were measured using BIOLOG. The addition of biochar proportionally increased SOC content with increasing biochar application rate and also increased the soil mean weight diameter (MWD). The changes in microbial diversity with the addition of biochar were modest for bacterial and fungal diversity. At the same time, individual bacterial taxa were significantly affected by 10%-Inc, including N-cycling bacteria, whereas there was no overall significant difference in the relative abundance of fungal taxa. Overall findings suggest that the 10% incorporated pine-biochar significantly alters soil bacterial community structure, especially N-cycling bacteria, and enhances C storage one year after application. In conclusion, these results indicate a rapid response of the soil bacterial community to high concentrations of biochar, but no corresponding response from the fungal community.

W7223131475.abstract: Environmental change is intensifying abiotic stresses such as heat, salinity, drought, and nutrient imbalance, threatening agricultural sustainability and destabilizing soil ecosystems, whose resilience is essential for maintaining carbon dynamics, nutrient cycling, and plant stress responses. Engineering the soil’s microbiome might be a solution to these problems. However, current microbiome-engineering approaches are often reductionist, relying on individual microbial strains or short-term interventions that do not adequately account for soil heterogeneity, resident microbial communities, plant genotype, and environmental variability. In this review, we reframe soil microbiome engineering as a dynamic and adaptive process in which interventions are designed according to the functional limitations of specific soil-plant systems. We propose a Soil-Plant-Microbiome Resilience Framework that integrates soil physicochemical properties, microbial community dynamics, plant physiological responses, management practices, and environmental stressors through feedback-regulated interactions. We further translate this framework into a practical engineering pathway based on site diagnosis, selection of microbial or habitat-based interventions, field deployment, monitoring, and adaptive management. Particular, attention is given to the context-dependent performance of bacterial and fungal inoculants and to property-based selection of biochar rather than its use as a generic amendment. By linking ecological mechanisms with site-specific management, this framework provides a basis for developing more reliable, field-relevant, and resilient soil microbiome interventions under environmental change.
W7223131475.title: Reimagining Soil Microbiome Engineering for Climate-Resilient Ecosystem Functioning

W7223132159.abstract: Introduction Biochar is widely used for heavy metal immobilization in co-contaminated soil, yet the remediation performance varies greatly with feedstock. This study aimed to evaluate the efficiency of four biochars derived from apple wood (A-BC), peanut shell (P-BC), corn straw (C-BC), and wheat straw (W-BC) on Zn and Cd availability, soil enzyme activity, and Zn and Cd accumulation in Brassica chinensis L. Methods A pot experiment was conducted to investigate soil Zn and Cd fractions, metal uptake by Brassica chinensis L., and soil catalase, urease, and sucrase activities under biochar amendments. Two-way ANOVA and correlation analysis were applied to assess the effects of biochar type, application rate, and their interaction. Results C-BC and W-BC had ash contents nearly three-fold higher than A-BC and P-BC; all biochars were alkaline, with comparable pH values for A-BC and P-BC. The 5% biochar addition significantly decreased water-extractable (WA) Zn (20%-50%) and Cd (15%-35%), while residual Zn and Cd increased by 30%-90% and 110%-330%, respectively ( P < 0.05). Biochar type, application amount, and their interaction exerted extremely significant influences on soil extractable and residual Zn/Cd contents ( P < 0.001). W-BC exhibited the best Zn immobilization, reducing weak acid-extractable Zn by up to 47.8% and increasing residual Zn by up to 91.8% at the 5% application rate. P-BC was optimal for Cd stabilization and significantly increased residual Cd at all application rates (by up to 121%). Biochar type, rate, and their interaction significantly affected plant Zn and Cd uptake ( P < 0.0001). A-BC and C-BC most effectively reduced Zn and Cd accumulation in Brassica chinensis L. and lowered the corresponding dietary health risks of these two metals. Biochar amendment increased catalase, urease, and sucrase activities in a dose-dependent manner, with growth rates of 24%-38%, 17%-29%, and 22%-41%, respectively. Biochar type, rate, and their interaction significantly altered sucrase activity. Correlation analysis showed that changes in weak acid-extractable metal concentrations explained over 50% of the variance in plant metal accumulation and soil enzyme activity. Discussion Feedstock source determines the remediation performance of biochar in Zn-Cd co-contaminated soil. Biochar can immobilize soil Zn and Cd, reduce plant metal uptake and associated health risks, and restore soil enzyme functions. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting suitable biochar materials to remediate Zn-Cd co-contaminated farmland while preserving soil biochemical functions.
