W7223269900.abstract: Given the significant environmental concerns raised by the accumulation of petroleum-derived plastics, efforts have focused on developing sustainable alternatives, especially bio-based and biodegradable plastics. The excessive generation of cocoa husks as agricultural byproducts poses environmental and disposal issues, thereby necessitating the exploration of sustainable strategies for their valorization. To address plastic pollution and valorize cocoa husk waste, this study aims to evaluate the feasibility of using cocoa husk pectin (CHP) as a film-forming biopolymer for bioplastic film preparation. The production yield of CHP was determined during pectin extraction, and its physicochemical properties, including functional groups, esterification degree, methoxylation content, and ξ-potential, were characterized. Apart from producing CHP-based bioplastic films by glycerol (Gly) plasticization and casting, the effects of Gly and CHP concentration on the film-forming behavior and chromatic properties of CHP bioplastic films were examined. Furthermore, contact angle and infrared analyses showed that bioplastic films exhibited surface hydrophilicity and extensive hydrogen bonding between CHP and the plasticizer. Regarding optical properties, the CHP bioplastic films with varying CHP and Gly contents exhibited an opacity of ∼31–71 % and resistance to UVC, UVB, and UVA of ∼85–99 %, ∼68–99 %, and ∼57–95 %. The water vapor permeability (WVP) and antioxidant activity of CHP bioplastic films were determined to be ∼5.9–8.0 × 10 −8 g m∙m −2 ∙Pa −1 ∙h −1 and ∼67–88 %. Accordingly, the renewability and soil degradation of CHP-based bioplastic films were assessed. Finally, our investigation provides a nice example of valorizing agricultural cocoa pod husk byproducts into CHP-based bioplastic films.

W7223282228.abstract: ABSTRACT The influence of isobutane loading on the properties of extruded PET foam sheets for food tray applications is investigated. A biodegradable polymer‐based chain extender is used as a sustainable alternative to conventional PET‐based carriers, supporting more sustainable PET foam production. Five formulations with isobutane contents from 0.6 to 1.4 wt% are prepared under constant conditions, and characterization is performed before and after thermal treatment at 250°C for 90 s to simulate thermoforming. The 1.2 wt% formulation delivers maximum thickness (2.31 mm before oven, 3.91 mm after) and minimum density (177.3 kg/m 3 before, 116.9 kg/m 3 after), achieving an 87% density reduction relative to solid PET. This formulation also exhibits the most uniform cellular architecture, with an average cell diameter of 211.1 ± 25.7 μm. The tensile behavior, characterized by reduced strength and modulus alongside increased elongation up to 1.2 wt%, is consistent with the reduced density and increased cell expansion at higher isobutane loadings. At 1.4 wt%, cell coalescence and collapse occur. Thermal analysis shows amorphous character before oven exposure, while post‐treatment X‐ray diffraction indicates crystallization enhancement. The optimal formulation is successfully thermoformed into a tray, demonstrating industrial processability and distinguishing this work from previous laboratory‐scale PET foaming studies. This study highlights isobutane as a key parameter for tailoring PET foam properties and supports PET foam as a nontoxic, recyclable alternative to polystyrene trays.
W7223282228.title: Effect of Isobutane Content on the Properties of PET Foam Sheets Produced With a Biodegradable Polymer Based Chain Extender for Food Tray Applications

W7223295891.abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) imposes a major global health burden, with current ablation techniques limited by invasiveness and post‐treatment recurrence. Here, size‐controllable, polylactic acid/iron oxide magnetic microspheres containing 30% Fe 3 O 4 (P@Fe30 MSs) were fabricated via shirasu porous glass membrane emulsification for transarterial magnetic thermal ablation (MTA). The optimized microspheres exhibit superior magnetothermal performance under an alternating magnetic field, effectively killing tumor cells and triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Mechanistically, MTA‐induced tumor disruption cooperates with the TLR9 agonist CpG ODN to accelerate dendritic cell maturation and promote a tumor–TDLN immune‐priming cascade, featuring CD103 + cDC1 enrichment and CCR7‐associated cDC1 migration dynamics, functional CD8 + T‐cell activation, and systemic memory‐associated immune remodeling. Crucially, direct evaluation of CpG timelines reveals that early post‐MTA CpG administration significantly outperforms delayed delivery, validating a transient post‐ablation immune‐priming window. Furthermore, experiments in Batf3 − / − mice confirm that this systemic antitumor immunity strictly depends on a cDC1‐ mediated priming pathway. Finally, preclinical validation in an orthotopic rabbit VX2 liver tumor model demonstrates excellent transarterial feasibility, localized metabolic tumor suppression via 18 F‐FDG PET imaging, and a favorable safety profile. This work establishes a remotely activated transarterial ablation platform that coordinates with temporal innate immunotherapy to drive systemic cDC1‐dependent antitumor responses.
W7223295891.title: Magnetic Thermal Ablation Combined with Temporally Coordinated CpG Immunotherapy Promotes cDC1‐Dependent Immune Priming in Hepatocellular Carcinoma

W7223303851.abstract: Abstract The accumulation of polylactic acid (PLA) waste poses a growing environmental challenge, calling for sustainable upcycling strategies that transform waste plastics into value-added chemicals. Here, sulfur-vacancy-engineered In2S3 nanoflowers were synthesized through a facile hydrothermal method and applied as an efficient photocatalyst for visible-light-driven one-pot upcycling of PLA into alanine. The optimized In2S3−S0.2 catalyst exhibited an alanine formation rate of 3.32 mmol·g−1·h−1 at 50 °C under visible-light irradiation. Structural and photoelectrochemical characterizations revealed that the enhanced activity of In2S3−S0.2 was mainly attributed to the sulfur-vacancy-induced bandgap narrowing, suppressed charge-carrier recombination, and strengthened reduction capability toward imine intermediates. Combined with radical-trapping experiments and in situ EPR analysis, PLA was sequentially transformed through ammonolysis and photocatalytic amination pathways involving lactamide, ammonium lactate, carbon-centered radicals, amino radicals, and imine intermediates before alanine formation. Moreover, the catalyst exhibited excellent stability and enabled the direct conversion of post-consumer PLA products into alanine. This work demonstrates an effective defect-engineering strategy for sustainable photocatalytic upcycling of biodegradable plastics into value-added amino acids.
W7223303851.title: Sulfur-Vacancy-Engineered In2S3 Nanoflowers for Visible-Light-Driven One-Pot Upcycling of Polylactic Acid Waste to Alanine

W7223306911.abstract: ABSTRACT: Microplastics from different polymer families occur together in real waste streams, yet separation performance is usually documented for single materials. This work presents a performance evaluation of the SATOORNIK S20, a high-capacity magnetic-assisted separation system, challenged with a mixed suspension of polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), and the biopolymer polylactic acid (PLA). Three independent 5 L tests (T1–T3) were conducted to validate system reliability. Pre- and post-filtration particle content was quantified by image-based analysis using the SATOORNIK Shadowgraphy Analyzer V2.6, introduced here for the first time as the cloud-based successor to the Size and Shape V2025 software used in earlier SATOORNIK publications. Removal efficiency exceeded 99.9% in all three tests, giving an overall mean separation efficiency of 99.98% (SD ±0.02%; CV = 0.02%). These findings extend the documented performance baseline of the S20 system to mixed-polymer microplastic suspensions including a biopolymer, supporting its applicability as a sealed, proprietary unit without disclosure of internal design or mechanism.

W7223308809.abstract: High ash content in sludge corresponds to high concentration of heteroatoms (N and O), causing elevated energy consumption and reduced product quality during single-feed sludge pyrolysis. Plastics, characterized by their high H/C ratio and high calorific value, are ideal candidates for co-pyrolysis with sludge, as they can enhance bio-oil quality by increasing hydrocarbon content and reducing oxygen content. To sustainably convert sludge to high-value bio-oil, a nickel-modified HZSM-5 zeolite supported on wheat straw biochar catalyst (Ni/HZSM-5@BC) was employed for the synergistic catalytic pyrolysis of sludge and LDPE. Compared with non-catalytic pyrolysis, the catalyst with a Ni loading of 3 wt% increased the feedstock conversion rate from 70.7% to 89.1%, and reduced the selectivities of oxygenates and nitrogen-containing compounds from 65.9% and 2.8%, respectively, to 0. Meanwhile, the selectivity of aromatic compounds reached 100%, with a BTX selectivity of 88.4%. This catalyst also exhibited good stability after six pyrolysis cycles. Analyses including XRD, SEM, TEM, FT-IR, Raman spectroscopy, and TG indicated that the catalyst structure remained largely unchanged, with HZSM-5 remaining stably coated on the biochar and Ni remaining well dispersed within the hierarchical micropore-mesopore structure. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited a low coke yield (3.72 wt%) that increased only modestly with cycling (an increase of 0.52 wt% after six pyrolysis cycles). Experiments with sludge model compounds further clarified the synergistic interactions between sludge and LDPE and supported the proposed catalytic co-pyrolysis mechanism over Ni/HZSM-5@BC.
W7223308809.title: Co-upcycling of sludge and LDPE to aromatics via catalytic pyrolysis over Ni/HZSM-5@biochar

W7223312083.abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) feeds roughly half of the world’s population, yet flooded paddies are among the largest agricultural sources of methane, a short-lived but potent greenhouse gas. Carbon farming, understood here as the deliberate management of farmland to reduce greenhouse gas emissions or increase durable carbon storage under rules that allow those outcomes to be quantified and rewarded, has recently been extended from soil carbon in upland systems to methane reduction in rice. This critical narrative review examines whether the evidence base is strong enough to support that extension and how rice-based carbon farming interacts with the Sustainable Development Goals. Peer-reviewed literature and authoritative institutional sources published from January 2000 onwards were identified through multidisciplinary scholarly databases, a regional index, citation chasing and targeted searches of inventory, policy and crediting documents, and were appraised for design, measurement completeness and external validity. The evidence is strongest for water management: field studies and several independent meta-analyses agree that alternate wetting and drying and mid-season drainage reduce methane emissions by roughly half, with small average yield effects when soil drying is mild. Confidence is weaker for the net climate benefit, because nitrous oxide responses, fallow-season emissions and long-term soil carbon losses are measured inconsistently and are rarely captured together. Straw removal from the growing season, low-emission cultivars, direct seeding and optimised nitrogen management show credible but context-dependent effects, whereas biochar and soil carbon gains raise unresolved questions of permanence, scale and verification. Monitoring, reporting and verification remain the principal bottleneck: emission factors, process models and satellite approaches disagree at regional scale, and farm-level verification of water management is costly. Synergies with food security, water productivity and grain arsenic reduction are well documented, but trade-offs involving nitrous oxide, cadmium, wetland biodiversity, unequal access to irrigation control and incentive design are under-studied. Rice carbon farming is therefore best regarded as a promising but conditional mitigation pathway whose credibility depends on full-season, multi-gas accounting, conservative crediting and explicit attention to social and ecological co-impacts.

W7223316160.abstract: This work investigated the economic viability and optimization of whiteboard marker ink using central composite design (CCD) of response surface methodology (RSM). The production was achieved using biochar, bioethanol, and natural resin at the range of 10 - 50 g, glycerol from 100 - 500 mL, and 10g – 50g, respectively. The Ink produced was characterize to check the viscosity, drying time, erasability and density. The ink at optimal condition has a drying time of 3.39s, viscosity of 1.47mPa.s at 30g of biochar, 300 mL of glycerol, and 30g resin. The results were compared to those of commercial inks. The results showed that the viscosity of commercial ink was 2.1mPa∙s. and analysis revealed that the commercial marker ink had the fastest drying rate than the ink produced. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the presence of functional groups associated with the whiteboard marker ink produced. The techno-economic analysis carried out shows that it is viable and promising to invest on whiteboard marker with the raw materials understudied. The overall results show that natural sourced materials are viable and innovative material for whiteboard ink production.

W7223320636.abstract: Fused deposition modeling (FDM) has become one of the most widely used additive manufacturing technologies, while polylactic acid reinforced by short carbon fibers (PLA-CF) is increasingly applied in structural components. However, the mechanical properties of FDM-printed parts are strongly affected by printing parameters and show obvious anisotropy owing to weak interlayer bonding. In this work, PLA-CF composites with fiber mass fractions of 4 wt.%, 7 wt.%, and 15 wt.% were prepared by FDM. The effects of filling angle (0°, 45°, 90°), printing hatch (0.35 mm, 0.45 mm), and annealing treatment on tensile properties and mechanical anisotropy were systematically studied. The results show that filling angle dominates the tensile strength, which reaches the maximum at 0° filling angle due to favorable fiber alignment and load transfer. Reducing printing hatch can improve interlayer bonding and significantly enhance the strength of 45° and 90° specimens. The fiber mass fraction presents an angle-dependent influence on tensile performance. Moreover, heat treatment effectively reduces anisotropy. Vacuum annealing at 180°C for 3 h increases the tensile strength of 90° specimens by 105.6% and minimizes the strength gap between 0° and 90° specimens to only 2.5 MPa. This work provides a feasible strategy for preparing high-performance, low-anisotropy PLA-CF components.

W7223323445.abstract: Abstract The production of food waste (FW) at current scale has been emerging as a pressing critical global, environmental and socio-economic crisis with nearly one-third of food produced annually, ~ 1.3 billion tons ending up as waste. The present data not only suggests a considerable loss of valuable natural resources viz. water, energy, and land, but also led to significant increase in global greenhouse gases (GHGs) emission along with contributing to large-scale environmental pollution when inadequately managed through unsustainable landfills. This impending backdrop warrants immediate attention; therefore, the upcycling of FW has emerged as a potent transformative strategy to convert bio-waste into high-value added bio-products while simultaneously addressing the climate change, resource inefficiency, and global food insecurity concerns. Upcycling approaches are broadly classified into three groups: biological, chemical, and thermochemical strategies. The later approaches are less eco-friendly and non-sustainable. In contrast, biological strategies are eco-friendly alternatives that primarily emphasize the utilization of living organisms or their enzymes system to transform FW into value-added products with approach of using sustainable technologies. The utilization of a distinct microbiome via a diverse array of microbial-mediated upcycling strategy represents a strong opportunity to encourage a circular economy model for the management and valorisation of FW with resource recovery. The microbial upcycling technologies include anaerobic digestion, microbial enzyme-assisted hydrolysis, fermentation, composting, phototrophic valorization, and the production of microbial protein (referred as single-cell protein). These processes produce biofuels (biogas, biohydrogen, and bioethanol), organic acids (acetic, butyric, formic, propionic, and lactic acid, etc.), bioplastics (polyhydroxyalkanoates and polylactic) and nutraceuticals, while also enhancing soil fertility through compost and biofertilizers. Recent research has advanced microbial metabolic engineering, catalytic system development, and integrated biorefinery models, enhancing the efficiency and selectivity of these convergent pathways. Moreover, life-cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis support the identification of sustainable and scalable solutions. However, significant barriers remain, including heterogeneity of FW composition, high capital and operating costs, process water management and challenges in large-scale deployment. Therefore, the review describes different microbial technologies employed for upcycling of FW and converting it into various value-added bio-products of economic importance. This comprehensive overview also highlights current research progress in microbial upcycling of FW, including key advances, challenges, and future perspectives. Overall, there is a pressing need to commercialize these microbial processes for effective upcycling of FW.
W7223323445.title: Microbial approaches for sustainable upcycling of food waste and resource recovery

W7223327061.abstract: Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) is one of the most popular additive manufacturing techniques for the fabrication of polymer components. However, the process parameters strongly affect the mechanical properties and surface roughness of the printed parts. In this work, an integrated experimental and machine learning framework is proposed to predict the surface roughness, impact strength, tensile strength and hardness of FDM-printed polylactic acid (PLA), acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) and polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG) parts. An L27-run full factorial design was used to systematically investigate the effect of layer thickness, printing speed and infill density on selected response variables. In this study, four supervised machine learning models were built on the experimental dataset, namely Random forest, Gradient boosting, Support vector regression (SVR) and K-nearest neighbours (KNN). The model performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ), root mean square error, mean absolute error, feature importance analysis and residual analysis, using 5-fold cross-validation. All the developed models showed good prediction capability, with R 2 values above 0.97 for all response variables. The KNN algorithm was the best overall predictor among the tested algorithms, with an average R 2 value of 0.9972, which was higher than SVR (0.9963), Random forest (0.9903) and Gradient boosting (0.9877). This framework provides a practical, low-cost alternative to exhaustive trial-and-error printing, enabling manufacturers to reliably select optimal FDM process parameters for rapid tooling, functional prototyping and low-volume end-use production.

W7223331163.abstract: Soil fertility management influences fertilizer use efficiency (FUE), crop productivity, and greenhouse gas (GHG) outcomes, yet these dimensions are often reported separately. This study mapped and synthesized evidence linking soil fertility management with FUE and GHG outcomes using a structured analytical framework. Specifically, the study (i) assessed the distribution of soil fertility and nutrient management practices, (ii) explored reported FUE responses, (iii) evaluated GHG outcomes, and (iv) examined integration across soil, efficiency, and emission dimensions. A PRISMA-ScR-informed evidence mapping approach was applied to 40 open-access studies comprising field experiments, long-term trials, surveys, modelling studies, reviews, and meta-analyses. Evidence was extracted using a structured matrix and synthesized using a weighted Evidence Index (EI) and Integrated Evidence Score (IES). Integrated soil fertility management accounted for 12 studies, organic amendments for 10, enhanced-efficiency fertilizers and inhibitors for 9, and precision or optimized nutrient management for 9. Reported NUE values ranged from 25% to 70%, with increases of 10–40% for enhanced-efficiency fertilizers, 15–35% for organic amendments and biochar approaches, and 10–25% for precision or optimized nutrient management. Reported N₂O reductions ranged from 10% to 50% across management categories. NUE, N₂O, and soil organic carbon were reported in 70%, 65%, and 50% of studies, respectively. Category-level EI ranged from 1.79 to 2.17, whereas IES ranged from 1.89 to 2.42, reflecting differences between methodological weighting and dimensional coverage. The synthesis provides a structured basis for harmonizing soil fertility, nutrient efficiency, productivity, and GHG indicators in future evidence synthesis and agricultural management research.
W7223331163.title: Mapping and synthesis of evidence on soil fertility management, fertilizer use efficiency, and greenhouse gas outcomes

W7223334725.abstract: Continuous cropping obstacles (CCOs) severely constrain foxtail millet ( Setaria italica L.) productivity by impairing soil health and disrupting nutrient cycling. This study evaluated fourteen soil amendment treatments to determine their efficacy in ameliorating CCOs in an outdoor pot experiment. Plant growth, photosynthetic pigments, biomass allocation, yield components, nutritional quality, and the physicochemical properties of leaves, roots, and soil were assessed at the maximum biomass stage. Based on the pot experiment, compared with continuous cropping, corn stalk biochar and humic acid significantly increased plant height, stem diameter, leaf SPAD, leaf thickness, leaf area, spike length, and specific leaf weight. Rotation with foxtail millet and Sorghum bicolor improved plant height, leaf SPAD, leaf thickness, leaf area, spike length, root forking, specific root surface area, soil total nitrogen, and available potassium ( P < 0.05). Humic acid application increased leaf total nitrogen and phosphorus, root potassium, and soil available potassium. Bacillus inoculation increased leaf organic carbon when applied as B. subtilis and B. megaterium , while B. mucilaginosus increased root phosphorus. Corn stalk biochar also increased leaf tissue density and soil organic carbon, whereas earthworm castings increased soil total and available nitrogen. Rotation with Vigna radiata promoted leaf expansion, while S. bicolor rotation enhanced root elongation. Redundancy analysis and hierarchical partitioning identified stem weight (26.62%), grain total starch (7.79%), root total nitrogen (5.10%), and leaf total phosphorus (1.99%) as the primary variables associated with yield components. The results provide a theoretical basis for understanding the responses of foxtail millet and continuously cropped soils to different individual amendments under pot experimental conditions.

W7223339941.abstract: ABSTRACT Poly (lactic acid) (PLA) melt‐blown nonwovens (MBNs) toughened by in situ‐formed polyamide 12 (PA12) microfibrils were fabricated via melt compounding followed by melt‐blown technology. Polyethylene glycol (PEG) was introduced to regulate the melt viscosity of PA12 and improve the rheological compatibility between PLA and PA12. The effects of PEG content on the rheological behavior, thermal properties, fiber morphology, and mechanical performance of the blends were systematically investigated, and the mechanism of in situ fibrillation was analyzed from thermodynamic and hydrodynamic perspectives. Results showed that PEG effectively improved the rheological matching in the PLA/PA12 blend system and promoted In situ fibrillation of PA12 during melt blowing. At a PA12/PEG mass ratio of 90/10, the blend exhibited optimal fibrillation behavior and mechanical performance. Compared with neat PLA, the tensile strength and elongation at break of the corresponding melt‐blown nonwoven were increased by approximately 609% and 104%, respectively. This remarkable toughening effect is attributed to the reinforcing network and crack‐bridging mechanism provided by the in situ‐formed PA12 microfibrils.

W7223344965.abstract: Olive mill solid waste (OMSW) is a major by-product of the agro-industrial sector and can be converted into biochar through pyrolysis, with potential applications in environmental management. This study investigated the effects of pyrolysis temperature (400, 500, and 600 °C) and residence time (1, 3, and 5 h) on the physicochemical, structural, and surface properties of OMSW-derived biochar. As the temperature increased, the biochar yield decreased from 32.08% at 400 °C (1 h) to 25.18% at 500 °C (1 h) and 24.67% at 600 °C (1 h). Surface area and pore development varied considerably with the processing conditions. At 500 °C, the BET surface area increased from 6.99 m2/g at 1 h to 44.19 m2/g at 5 h, accompanied by an increase in total pore volume from 0.006 to 0.026 cm3/g. At 600 °C, the maximum Langmuir surface area (201.6 m2/g) and total pore volume (0.075 cm3/g) were obtained at 1 h, whereas the BET surface area reached 135.23 m2/g at 5 h. These differences indicate that residence time influenced the measured surface area and pore characteristics differently. Moisture content reached 4.18% at 600 °C for 5 h, while ash content reached 10.83% under the same conditions. Moisture content varied with temperature and residence time, reaching 4.18% at 600 °C for 5 h. Ash content also reached its maximum value of 10.83% under these conditions, while electrical conductivity reached 0.077 mS/cm. All biochar samples exhibited negative zeta potentials, ranging from −22.72 to −32.21 mV at 400 and 500 °C, while values at 600 °C ranged from −23.53 to −29.89 mV. Elemental analysis revealed variations in the H/C and O/C atomic ratios, with H/C values ranging from 0.2468 to 0.5984 and O/C values ranging from 0.0369 to 0.296. These variations indicate differences in elemental composition and relative carbonization characteristics among the samples. Calcium and potassium were the predominant mineral elements. Overall, the findings provide a basis for further investigating OMSW-derived biochar for potential adsorption, soil-related, and nutrient-management applications, subject to application-specific experimental validation.

W7223347281.abstract: Heavy metal pollution in agricultural soils poses serious threats to the ecological environment and food safety. Soil microorganisms are sensitive indicators of changes in soil quality. Most existing studies explore passivators’ effects on heavy metal bioavailability in contaminated farmland, yet few investigate their impacts on microbial communities. In this study, Illumina MiSeq high-throughput sequencing was used to investigate the responses of soil microbial communities to passivating agents in heavy-metal-contaminated soil through a long-term field experiment with different in situ passivating agents. The results showed that hydroxyapatite plus rice biochar (HR) and montmorillonite (M) produced the best remediation effects, and soil alkaline phosphatase (S-ALP) activity was also relatively high. Different types and concentrations of passivating agents had significant effects on bacterial α- and β-diversity. Treatments of 0.3% HR1, 0.6% M2, 1.2% M3, and 1.2% CA3 significantly reduced bacterial Chao1 and Shannon indices. The relative abundance of Chloroflexi also decreased significantly in the HR1, M2, M3, and CA3 treatments, whereas the relative abundances of Acidobacteriota, Firmicutes, Proteobacteria, Actinobacteriota, and Bacteroidota increased significantly in the treatments with HR1, HR2, HR3, M1, M2, M3, hydroxyapatite (H), wheat biochar (W), rice biochar (R), and CA1, CA2, CA3. These results indicate that passivating agent addition affects the relative abundance of different microbial groups by altering soil physicochemical properties and Cd bioavailability. This study provides field-scale observational data on microbial community shifts following four-year in-situ passivation in Cd-contaminated agricultural soil.

W7223373040.abstract: The increasing prevalence of industrial wastewater, particularly from pharmaceutical companies, poses significant environmental challenges. This study focuses on the removal of specific pharmaceutical compound tetracycline hydrochloride (THC), using sugarcane biochar beads (BCB). THC, an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections, is the target for removal in this study, aiming for a sustainable solution. BCB were developed as a recoverable material for the removal of THC from batch to continuous treatment in a fixed-bed system. Under optimum batch conditions, BCB was capable of 85% THC removal, which corresponds to an adsorption capacity of 3.43 mg g⁻¹ . The Freundlich isotherm and fractional power kinetic model were best suited to describe the equilibrium and kinetic data, respectively, and thermodynamic analysis showed that the adsorption was both spontaneous and exothermic. Breakthrough experiments were carried out in the continuous fixed-bed units, and the results were obtained for three variables of interest: flow rate, influent THC concentration and bed height. The batch-to-fixed-bed capacity ratio (1.23–1.55) further validated the relationship between the equilibrium uptake and dynamic column performance. BCB also showed regeneration potential and an Adsorbent Sustainability Index (ADSUS) of 0.85 was excellent sustainability. The integrated evaluation of the waste derived immobilized biochar by batch adsorption, continuous fixed-bed treatment, regeneration, scale-up and sustainability assessment constitutes the main innovation of this work.

W7223374659.abstract: Polylactic acid (PLA) is a biodegradable polymer with good processability, but its poor flame retardancy limits its wider practical use. In this work, an ethanol-assisted pre-assembled g-C3N4/fumed silica hybrid (gCNFS) was introduced into a PLA/ammonium polyphosphate (APP)/lignin system to improve its flame-retardant performance. The pre-assembly strategy was designed to improve the interfacial contact between g-C3N4 and fumed silica and regulate char formation and thermal decomposition during burning. The chemical structure and morphology of the composites were analyzed to study their thermal degradation behavior, volatile release, and post-burn char morphology. The results showed that the introduction of pre-assembled gCNFS improved the flame retardancy of the PLA/APP/lignin system. Among all formulations, PLA/Q-gCNFS-3 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a limiting oxygen index (LOI) of 37% and a UL-94 V-0 rating. Compared with neat PLA, its peak heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat release (THR) decreased by approximately 50% and 24%, respectively, indicating effective suppression of burning intensity and total heat output. The flame-retardant mechanism of PLA/APP/Lignin with gCNFS enhanced both condensed-phase and gas-phase flame-retardant actions. In the condensed phase, a continuous and compact expanded char layer with better sealing ability and barrier performance was formed. In the gas phase, nonflammable gas release occurred, which helped reduce the concentration of combustible volatiles. Hence, the ethanol-assisted pre-assembled gCNFS is an effective strategy for improving the flame-retardant efficiency of PLA/APP/lignin composites.
W7223374659.title: G-C3N4-Orchestrated Multi-Component Synergy for Enhanced Flame Retardancy in PLA

W7223375741.abstract: Copper-containing electroplating wastewater is strongly acidic and highly saline, making efficient treatment challenging. Oxalic-acid-modified sugarcane bagasse biochar was prepared as an anode-side flow electrode for asymmetric flow-electrode capacitive deionization (AFCDI). Sugarcane bagasse biochar modified with 1.25 M oxalic acid (1.25OA-SC) was selected for its favorable overall balance of structural, electrochemical, and treatment characteristics. At 2.8 V, AFCDI achieved 98.12 ± 0.36% Cu2+ removal and lowered conductivity from 22.6 to 2.35 ± 0.66 mS/cm. This performance was associated with the combined effects of accessible porosity, oxygen-containing surface functionality, and electrochemical transport properties. Compared with conventional FCDI, AFCDI facilitated Cu2+ migration and cathodic deposit formation while achieving higher charge efficiency and lower electrical energy consumption. At 62.5 mL/g, Cu2+ removal remained above 98%, with an average TDS removal rate of 298.91 ± 7.19 g/(m2·h). During 10 consecutive AFCDI cycles using recovered 1.25OA-SC, Cu2+ removal remained above 98% and SO42− removal close to 80%, indicating short-term system-level performance retention. Cathodic deposits consisted mainly of Cu0 and Cu2O, whereas SO42− migrated through the anion-exchange membrane and was stored mainly by electric-double-layer charge compensation. These results demonstrate a biochar-based AFCDI strategy for coupled copper removal, recovery, and desalination of acidic sulfate-rich wastewater.
W7223375741.title: Asymmetric Flow-Electrode Capacitive Deionization for Copper-Containing Electroplating Wastewater Treatment Using Modified Sugarcane Bagasse Biochar

W7223380938.abstract: End-of-life furniture waste is a rapidly growing and heterogeneous fraction of municipal solid waste (MSW) that is difficult to recycle. This study investigates the co-pyrolysis of pine sawdust with three representative furniture waste residues, synthetic leather, polyurethane foam (PU foam), and textile (cloth), as a resource-oriented treatment pathway for bulky MSW. Experiments were conducted at 550°C with a fixed 10 wt% residue addition, and the bio-oil, biochar, particulate matter (PM), and gas products were characterized using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and Pearson correlation analysis. The three residues exerted distinct regulatory effects on product distribution. Textile addition raised the bio-oil yield from 47.4 to 55.8 wt% while cutting PM to 1.32 wt%. PU foam promoted aromatic hydrocarbons and increased bio-oil phenolics from 8.56 to 20.66%, and textile increased phenolics to 21.76%. Synthetic leather favored gas and char production, raising the gas yield to 41.15 wt% and, through the catalytic action of inorganic fillers, the char specific surface area from 299 to 402 m 2 g −1 . Chlorine-containing organic compounds were not detected in the co-pyrolysis bio-oils, indicating effective in situ retention of chlorine in the solid phase and reduced environmental risk compared with incineration. Pearson correlation analysis quantified and ranked the contribution of each residue to product yields and composition, providing a basis for mixed-waste feedstock design. Overall, co-pyrolysis enables the direct valorization of complex furniture waste streams, offering a cleaner and more flexible alternative to conventional disposal and supporting the transition of MSW management toward circular resource recovery.

W7223383819.abstract: The long-term immobilization of highly mobile Mn2+ in electrolytic manganese residue (EMR) remains a critical challenge for sustainable waste management, as conventional cement-based solidification often suffers from carbon-intensive clinker demand and insufficient interfacial stabilization. Herein, we propose a co-solidification strategy integrating municipal sewage sludge-derived biochar (SBC) into cementitious matrices to enhance Mn immobilization. Multi-scale characterization revealed that SBC functioned as a micro-aggregate to increase pore network tortuosity by 124% and further modified the hydration/interfacial environment of the cementitious matrix. BCR sequential extraction showed that the acid-soluble/exchangeable Mn fraction decreased from 63% in raw EMR to 41% in ECB without SBC and further to 28% after the incorporation of 5 wt% SBC, indicating a progressive redistribution of Mn toward less mobile fractions. These coupled chemical and physical effects reduced Mn leaching from 14.5 mg/L to 0.2 mg/L after 28 days of curing, corresponding to a 98.6% reduction and meeting the relevant leaching criterion for non-hazardous classification. Mechanistic analysis indicated that Mn immobilization was governed by the combined effects of hydration-product association, interfacial interactions, matrix densification, and pore-network refinement. Life-cycle assessment further showed that the climate benefit of the SBC route was dependent on the sludge-management scenario, particularly the energy demand for sludge pretreatment and drying, auxiliary fuel use, and energy recovery. This study elucidates the interfacial engineering principles of SBC-amended cementitious systems and offers a technically feasible pathway for the co-valorization of industrial and municipal solid wastes.

W7223390729.abstract: Biochar derived from bone waste (bone char) is a promising phosphorus fertiliser. However, limited nutrient availability restricts its agricultural application; therefore, different amendments have been investigated to modify nutrient release from biochar. This study evaluated the effects of pyrolysis temperature and the addition of potassium tartrate (KTar) as an in-situ catalyst on the water solubility of selected macro- and micronutrients in chicken bone waste-derived bone char. Chicken bone waste (CBW) was mixed with KTar at a 10 : 1 mass ratio and pyrolysed at 400–800 C for 30 min. The KTar modification strongly affected nutrient retention and extractability. In particular, KTar enhanced sulphur retention at temperatures above 400 C, resulting in total sulphur contents 55–97% higher than those in unmodified bone chars, and promoted almost complete water extractability of sulphur at 400 C. Phosphorus availability was also increased by KTar. The extractable-to-total phosphorus ratios were 6 times higher at 400 C and 1.7–2.5 times higher at higher temperatures compared with unmodified bone chars. In addition, KTar altered micronutrient behaviour as it increased the availability of iron and copper, likely through the formation of soluble salts, promoted zinc volatilisation at 800 C and enhanced the extractability of the remaining zinc fraction. Overall, KTar modification improved the fertilising potential of bone chars by increasing the water-extractable fractions of essential nutrients. Specifically, KTar-modified bone char obtained at 500 C represents the optimal treatment, with a balanced high yield, carbon stability, and water-extractable phosphorus, sulfur, iron, and copper. These findings suggest that KTar-assisted pyrolysis is a promising strategy for producing nutrient-enriched bone chars for agricultural applications.
W7223390729.title: Catalytic pyrolysis of chicken bone waste with potassium tartrate: availability of macro- and micronutrients

W7223397796.abstract: Abstract Fertilization not only influences crop productivity but also plays a pivotal role in regulating soil CO 2 emissions within agricultural ecosystems. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms governing soil CO 2 emissions under different fertilization regimes in the Northeast China Black Soil Region. Field experiments were conducted using four treatments: mineral fertilizer (NPK), and NPK combined with biochar (NPK + BC), organic fertilizer (NPK + OF) or straw (NPK + SF). A comprehensive assessment was performed, including measurements of soil CO 2 flux, physicochemical properties, microbial community composition, plant physiological traits and crop yield. The results showed that, compared with the CK, soybean yields significantly increased by 10.00%, 8.15% and 3.70% under NPK + BC, NPK + OF and NPK + SF, respectively. Regarding mature stage soil properties, NPK + BC, NPK + OF and NPK + SF significantly elevated soil organic matter (SOM) by 16.30%, 23.86% and 1.39%, meanwhile available phosphorus (AP) by 19.76%, 24.00% and 6.78%, respectively. CO 2 flux was reduced by 24.66% in NPK + BC but increased by 41.34% in NPK + OF. Furthermore, fertilization significantly altered microbial diversity; the ACE index increased by 7.82% under NPK + BC in the mature stage. Specifically, Proteobacteria abundance rose by 41.30% under NPK + OF, while Basidiomycota—associated with carbon sequestration—increased by 163.88% under NPK + BC. Structural equation modelling indicated that variation in soil CO 2 flux was associated with SOM and microbial metabolic responses. DNDC model projections suggest that adopting biochar‐based fertilization could reduce CO 2 emissions in Heilongjiang Province by approximately 586,465 tons annually. These findings provide quantitative evidence for developing low‐carbon, yield‐enhancing fertilization strategies in sustainable soybean production.

W7223404962.abstract: Airborne microbial contamination in hospitals is a major driver of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). So far, most commercial air filters capture microorganisms but do not inactivate them, and they rely on non-biodegradable polymers. Here, we engineered bio-derived nanocellulose filters from oil palm empty fruit bunches and endowed them with dual-mode (light/dark) antimicrobial activity by integrating zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) and N/S-doped carbon dots immobilized on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (NS/CDs@MSN). Three-dimensional, highly porous scaffolds were fabricated via tert-butyl alcohol-assisted freeze-drying, yielding interconnected channels that promote airflow and contact between airborne bacteria and the active surface. Hospital air was sampled using a six-stage cascade impactor equipped with a cellulose filter, after that culture-based assays and MALDI-TOF/MS were used to characterize the trapped microorganisms. While pristine nanocellulose filters allowed survival of opportunistic pathogens, including Bacillus cereus, Bacillus thuringiensis and Staphylococcus epidermidis , the ZIF-8+NS-CDs@MSN composite filters achieved wide-ranging suppression of culturable airborne bacteria captured on the filter surface and within the filter matrix. Electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy confirmed the generation of multiple reactive oxygen species (ROS), including •OH, 1 O₂, and •O₂⁻, under both dark and 365 nm irradiation, supporting a dual-mode, ROS-driven inactivation mechanism that is synergistic with the presence of Zn-containing phases. Characterization via Nano-CT and XRF confirmed the uniform distribution of ZIF-8 and MSN within the 3D nanocellulose matrix, which optimized particulate capture and radical-pathogen contact. This study demonstrated a sustainable, ROS-active nanocellulose–MOF–carbon dot platform that bridges real-world hospital air monitoring and on-filter disinfection, offering a promising route to next-generation antimicrobial air-filtration materials for infection control in healthcare environments.

W7223415514.abstract: Abstract The development of sustainable elastomeric materials is an important step toward reducing the environmental impact of conventional synthetic rubbers. In this study, elastomeric electrospun materials were fabricated from blends of amorphous polyhydroxyalkanoate (aPHA) and cellulose acetate (CA) at three compositions (50/50, 75/25, and 90/10). The influence of fiber morphology and interfiber bonding on the mechanical response was investigated. Neat aPHA showed rubber-like behavior but poor dimensional stability after electrospinning. Incorporating CA improved structural stability, thermal resistance, tensile strength, and Young’s modulus. The 90/10 (aPHA/CA) blend retained a hyperelastic response, consistent with the classical Ogden and Mooney–Rivlin strain-energy models, while improving processability. Morphological analysis during stretching–relaxation cycles revealed a bimodal fiber diameter distribution, originating from axial fiber thinning and perpendicular fiber compression due to interfiber fusion points. A permanent diameter increase of perpendicular fibers (∼20%) was observed after the first cycle and stabilized upon repeated deformation. Fitting of uniaxial stress–strain data to Ogden and Mooney–Rivlin functions confirmed that pure aPHA and the 90/10 blend possess rubber-like properties, whereas the 75/25 composition did not. The biodegradation analysis supports the sustainable nature of the developed rubber-like materials, with all blends exhibiting full biodegradation in compost within 37 days. These results show that controlled CA incorporation regulates interfiber bonding and structural stability, enabling the design of fully biobased electrospun elastomeric materials.

W7223439280.abstract: Abstract Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), an invasive aquatic weed, poses environmental challenges in the Panchganga Basin of Kolhapur, Maharashtra, while smallholder farmers face rising agricultural input costs. This study investigates the potential of converting harvested water hyacinth into biochar as a low-cost soil amendment, evaluating its effects on crop growth and estimated input costs under practical farming conditions. A nine-week field pilot involved four smallholder farmers cultivating sugarcane, soybean, and turmeric. Each farm contained a 40 m² treatment plot receiving water hyacinth-derived biochar and an adjacent control plot managed using the farmer’s usual practices. Biochar was produced through low-temperature pyrolysis and incorporated into the soil at planting. Plant height, qualitative soil moisture and pest observations, and estimated input costs were monitored throughout the trial. By week nine, treatment plots recorded an average plant height increase of 34% relative to baseline, compared with 24% in control plots. A growth advantage was observed on three of the four farms, while the turmeric trial showed minimal differences. Estimated input costs were 47–64% lower for biochar treatment than for existing soil amendments. Farmers also reported longer moisture retention in most treatment plots, although pest observations remained qualitative. These preliminary findings suggest that water hyacinth biochar may support sustainable agriculture by linking invasive weed management with potentially lower-cost soil improvement. However, the small sample size, short trial duration, inconsistent monitoring, and absence of laboratory-based soil nutrient analysis limit the conclusions. Larger, multi-season field trials incorporating laboratory soil testing are needed to establish its effectiveness and broader applicability.

W7223441365.abstract: Background: Biochar, a high-carbon material produced by the pyrolysis of organic farm waste, has gained substantial attention owing to its potential to improve soil fertility and support sustainable agricultural practices. Guava is an important fruit crop grown extensively in many parts of the world. However, guava pruning waste is usually discarded or burnt, generating environmental and disposal problems. This study presents a detailed examination of biochar from guava-pruned cuttings, aiming to describe its characteristics in line with the Fertilizer (Control) Order 1985. Methods: In addition to the biochar production, the incubation of other soil media and amendments with biochar were observed for soil microbiome dynamics. The feedstock used for producing biochar was guava pruned shoots. The shoots were collected from the college orchard at SRMCAS. The pyrolysis of biochar from guava cuttings provides a green method for utilizing agricultural waste while increasing soil fertility and sequestering carbon. Result: The biochar had an alkaline pH of 8.4, total organic carbon content of 50.40%, carbon-to-nitrogen ratio of 65:1, cation exchange capacity of 30 cmol/kg and anion exchange capacity of 5 cmol/kg. Its 25% water-holding capacity indicates high carbon stability and good capacity for water and nutrient retention. SEM showed a very porous structure with cracks and microbial colonization and XRD analysis of the mineral phase found calcite as the major mineral phase, with lesser peaks for silica, potassium salts and ash minerals, all of which contribute to support processes of nutrient buffering and exchange. FTIR confirmed the presence of functional groups, which are vital for water adsorption, nutrient retention and association with beneficial soil microbes.

W7223446062.abstract: Biochar produced through lignocellulosic-biomass pyrolysis may improve tropical soil fertility and provide feedstock for charcoal briquettes. This study characterised coconut-shell biochars produced with a locally fabricated pyrolyser under the Agri-resilience project in Porto-Novo and Comè-Grand-Popo, Benin, between December 2025 and February 2026. Analyses conducted at the 2A2S2E laboratory covered major elements (N, P, K, Ca, Mg and Na), trace elements (Zn, Mn, Cu and Fe), organic matter, organic carbon, ash, moisture, dry matter, pH and particle-size distribution. Results were compared with International Biochar Initiative and European Biochar Certificate criteria, and measurement reproducibility was assessed using coefficients of variation. Both biochars broadly complied with the selected IBI criteria for most valid parameters. Porto-Novo biochar contained more than 50% organic carbon and approximately 86.5% organic matter, indicating potential suitability as an agricultural amendment. Comè biochar had a more alkaline pH and higher calcium content, but its measured ash content of 7.9–11.5% may constrain direct energy use. Reproducibility was satisfactory for most parameters, although Fe, Na and Ca exceeded the 5% variability threshold. Improved production control, sample homogenisation and laboratory mass-balance verification are required before definitive use-specific recommendations are made.

W7223448392.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of sustainable electronic systems remains challenged by the dependence on petroleum‐derived substrates, nonbiodegradable conductive materials, and multi‐step fabrication processes. Here, orange peel waste is directly transformed into electronically active laser‐induced graphene (LIG) architectures through laser processing of biomass‐derived bioplastic films. Unlike conventional smart packaging approaches relying on conductive layers, the proposed strategy converts the surface of the bioplastic into porous conductive graphitic networks without requiring conductive inks, metallic coatings, or transfer steps. Structural and chemical characterization confirmed the successful formation of LIG structures with increased sp 2 carbon content and conductive networks. Under optimized laser conditions, conductive patterns with low sheet resistance values were achieved. The resulting platform enabled direct fabrication of capacitive and resistive environmental sensors on biomass films. The capacitive devices exhibited stable thermal behavior together with pronounced humidity sensitivity, while the resistive sensors showed coupled thermo‐hygrometric responses with maximum thermal sensitivity at intermediate humidity conditions. These results demonstrate that agro‐industrial waste can function not only as a biodegradable substrate, but also as an electronically active material compatible with laser‐written carbon electronics. More broadly, this work establishes a scalable route toward sustainable electronic systems and next‐generation smart packaging technologies within a circular economy framework.

W7223451702.abstract: This study experimentally investigates the mechanical, viscoelastic, and tribological behavior of carbon nanotube (CNT) reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) nanocomposites fabricated by fused deposition modeling (FDM). CNT-reinforced PLA filaments were used to produce test specimens, and the influence of CNT addition on tensile, creep, loading–unloading, and wear behavior was systematically evaluated. Tensile tests were conducted to determine the elastic–plastic deformation characteristics, while loading–unloading and creep experiments were employed to characterize the time-dependent viscoelastic and viscoplastic response of the nanocomposites. Tribological performance was assessed using pin-on-disk wear tests under different operating temperatures. The results demonstrate that CNT reinforcement significantly enhances the mechanical strength of PLA, reduces creep deformation, and increased the recovered strain energy while generally reducing the dissipated energy, indicating a more recoverable mechanical response. Furthermore, CNT addition leads to a noticeable reduction in wear rate and generally lowers the coefficient of friction, particularly at elevated temperatures. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), combined with ImageJ-based 2D image analysis, was used to examine the interfilament void morphology and quantify the mean pore area and 2D pore area fraction of the printed specimens. The findings highlight the potential of CNT-reinforced PLA nanocomposites for tribological and structural applications in additively manufactured polymer components.

W7223454019.abstract: Throughout the Pb-contaminated soil rehabilitation procedure, biochar may change the structure of the soil, which has a significant impact on soil freezing. This study examined the change in freezing temperature ( \(ToF\) ) during the biochar remediation of Pb-contaminated soils using machine learning techniques, such as Light Gradient Boosting ( \(LGB\) ), Extreme Gradient Boosting ( \(XGB\) ), Extra Tree Regression ( \(ETR\) ) and Random Forest Regression ( \(RFR\) ). The data used in this research is derived from previously conducted trials. The system's reliability is significantly impacted by hyperparameters, which must be selected using metaheuristic optimization approaches. To accomplish this, a variety of algorithms are used, including the Catch Fish Optimization ( \(CFO\) ). The information, which includes 360 ToF data points, came from studies that were submitted for publication. After studying each element, the study group came to the decision that 80% (288) of the dataset would be utilized for training and model construction, while the other 20% (72) of the dataset would be utilized for validating the model. Randomization, normalization, cross-validation, scaling, and feature significance evaluation were some of the pre-processing methods used to the dataset. The prediction efficacy of \(ETR(CFO)\) and \(RFR(CFO)\) in predicting ToF was assessed using metrics. With the data, ToF can be reliably predicted by both \(ETR(CFO)\) and \(RFR(CFO)\) over other baseline models. The assessment process assessed the reliability and plausibility of each model using evaluation criteria, logical analysis, ranking score, and model difference percentage. In achieving its primary target, the \(RFR(CFO)\) model performs better than the alternative model.

W7223462464.abstract: This study investigates the transient dynamic response of an additively manufactured polylactic acid (PLA) honeycomb sandwich panel with glass-fiber-reinforced plastic (GFRP) face sheets through experimental characterization and finite element analysis. The PLA honeycomb core was fabricated using fused deposition modelling, while the GFRP face sheets were prepared using the hand lay-up technique. Tensile, flexural, and density tests were conducted to experimentally characterize the material properties used in the numerical model. A finite element model was developed in ANSYS using the experimentally obtained effective properties and was initially assessed against benchmark results reported in the literature. The experimental and numerical displacement–time histories under cantilever harmonic excitation at 500 Hz and 0.2 N showed similar trends for the investigated laboratory condition. A separate numerical calculation was performed to examine the early-time global displacement response under a hypothetical prescribed modified Friedlander pressure pulse using a linear-elastic material representation. The blast analysis showed maximum deformation in the central region of the panel and relatively lower displacement near the supported boundaries. Within the 30 ms simulation window, the panel exhibited a bounded transient displacement response. The blast calculations represent early-time global displacement predictions under the assumption of a linear-elastic material. Failure initiation, progressive stiffness degradation, core crushing, and interfacial separation were not modelled, and energy absorption was not quantified. Accordingly, the calculated histories do not establish retained structural integrity or validated blast-protection performance. The study provides experimental characterization and a laboratory assessment of the global dynamic response of the investigated configuration, along with preliminary elastic calculations under the prescribed pressure pulse.

W7223469312.abstract: L'intercettazione dei flussi naturali di carbonio e la rimozione permanente della 〖"CO" 〗_2 atmosferica (Carbon Dioxide Removal, CDR) richiedono strategie scalabili, termodinamicamente efficienti e radicate nei contesti territoriali locali. Il presente lavoro propone un modello di agricoltura circolare in-situ basato sulla combinazione del Lupinus albus (Lupino bianco, con particolare riferimento alle varietà dolci) e substrati vulcanici italiani ad alta reattività (scarti di cava di basalto, pozzolana e tufo). La fisiologia del lupino, caratterizzata dalla formazione di radici a grappolo (cluster roots), attiva un'intensa secrezione di acidi organici (principalmente acido citrico e malico) nella rizosfera. Questo microambiente acido accelera la dissoluzione dei minerali silicatici [es. metasilicato di calcio, 〖"CaSiO" 〗_3] presenti nei substrati vulcanici locali, catalizzando la reazione geochimica di Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW): 〖"CaSiO" 〗_3+2〖"CO" 〗_2+"H" _2 "O"⟶〖"Ca" 〗^(2+)+2〖"HCO" 〗_3^-+〖"SiO" 〗_2. La trasformazione della 〖"CO" 〗_2 in ioni bicarbonato (〖"HCO" 〗_3^-) stabili ed idrosolubili garantisce un sequestro geologico durevole verso le falde e gli oceani, contrastandone contemporaneamente l'acidificazione. Il modello integra un secondo binario di stoccaggio permanente attraverso la conversione termochimica (pirolisi) dei residui colturali della pianta (steli e baccelli) in biochar arricchito di azoto e cationi. Tale ammendante, riapplicato al suolo in combinazione con il tufo, ottimizza la Capacità di Scambio Cationico (CSC), la ritenzione idrica e l'attività microbiota del terreno, incrementando ulteriormente l'efficienza di weathering. Rispetto alle opzioni di geoingegneria oceanica ex-situ o all'impiego energivoro di impianti Direct Air Capture (DAC), l'approccio proposto offre una soluzione win-win: elimina i rischi di anossia bentonica, sfrutta scarti di estrazione mineraria a filiera corta e garantisce la produzione sostenibile di proteine vegetali per uso alimentare o mangimistico senza necessità di deamarizzazione acquosa.

W7223470204.abstract: The exponential rise in plastic waste has become a major problem for the environment and public health because of its high stability, non-biodegradable nature and long-term persistence. This investigation analyzed the effects of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) on wheat plants and the alleviation of its adverse effects using jackfruit shell biochar (JSBC) and potassium silicate (Si). The pot experiment was conducted to evaluate the individual and combined effects of PET, JSBC, and Si treatments on the growth of wheat plants. After treatment, wheat plants were harvested for analysis of morphological and biochemical variables, oxidative stress markers, enzymatic and non-enzymatic antioxidants and glyoxalase enzyme activities. Exposure of wheat plants to PET treatment decreased morphological traits and relative water content, caused photosynthetic damage and increased lipid peroxidation and electrolyte leakage. The combined treatment of JSBC and Si in PET-treated pots reduced electrolyte leakage, levels of H 2 O 2 and O 2 ·− by 29%, 53%, and 31%, respectively, as compared to the PET treatment. Application of JSBC and Si, individually or combined, enhanced growth attributes of wheat plants and alleviated PET-induced oxidative stress by modulating activities of antioxidant and glyoxalase enzymes. The findings of the present study underscore the beneficial effects of the combined applications of biochar and potassium silicate for enhancing growth of wheat plants under plastic stress. Thus, the combined application of JSBC and Si acts as a promising strategy for plastic contaminant mitigation and reutilization of waste materials as renewable assets to combat plastic pollution in the soil ecosystem.
W7223470204.title: Combined application of biochar and silicon on physiological and antioxidant defense mechanism of wheat against plastic induced stress

W7223472466.abstract: Additive manufacturing has long struggled to bridge nanoscale functionalities with complex macroscale geometries, particularly for nanocomposites with high nanofiller loadings and ordered structures. Herein, we report shear alignment polymer extrusion (SHAPE) three-dimensional (3D) printing, a strategy that uses high shear forces to align highly loaded nanomaterials (e.g., boron nitride (BN) nanosheets and carbon nanotubes) along defined directions in polymer matrices, enabling the scalable fabrication of macroscopic nanocomposites with complex 3D architectures. A key advancement is the development of high-loading filaments (e.g., 55 wt% BN in polylactic acid) and a high-shear extrusion system, overcoming the traditional challenges of poor processability and structural integrity in high-filler composites. Post-sintering yields pure nanomaterial architectures that fully replicate the 3D printed geometry with zero volume shrinkage and exceptional thermomechanical stability-withstanding temperatures above the polymer melting and decomposition without structural failure. These materials exhibit tailored functionalities: vertically aligned BN composites show enhanced thermal conductivity (1.07 W/m/K); horizontally aligned BN structures offer efficient thermal insulation (0.071 W/m/K); and BN membranes display robust mechanical performance (a compressive strength of 3.4 MPa). Generalizable to diverse nanomaterials (0D to 2D), SHAPE opens new avenues for cross-scale design in thermal management, energy storage, and advanced structural materials.

W7223476554.abstract: Abstract With the increasing adoption of green walls as a sustainable approach to improve air quality, mitigate urban heat, and enhance space-use efficiency in cities, the need to produce ornamental plants that are resilient and require fewer chemical inputs has become increasingly important. In this context, the use of biochar and mycorrhizal fungi has emerged as an environmentally friendly strategy. This study was conducted to evaluate the synergistic effects of biochar and mycorrhizal fungi on the growth and physiological traits of chrysanthemum ( Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat.) using a factorial experiment arranged in a randomized complete block design with three replications during 2024–2025. Treatments consisted of four biochar levels (0, 2, 3, and 5% w/w of the substrate) and four mycorrhizal inoculation treatments (non-inoculated control, Glomus intraradices , G. mosseae , and a combination of the two strains). The results showed that increasing biochar levels and mycorrhizal inoculation significantly improved growth and morphophysiological indices of chrysanthemum. The treatment consisting of 5% biochar combined with G. intraradices produced the highest leaf number (29.43), leaf dry weight (11.07 g), and growth index (145,559.83 cm 3 ), representing increases of 54%, 103%, and 722%, respectively, compared with the control. The greatest plant height (68.1 cm) was observed in the treatment with 5% biochar combined with G. mosseae . The combined application of 5% biochar and the two fungal strains also resulted in a significant increase in leaf fresh weight (75.15 g) and leaf area (1233.18 mm2). In terms of physiological traits, the highest relative water content (83.71%) was recorded in the 3% biochar treatment with G. intraradices , while the lowest electrolyte leakage (64.01%) was observed under 5% biochar combined with G. mosseae . In addition, chlorophyll a and b concentrations reached their maximum values in the 3% and 0% biochar treatments, respectively, when combined with G. intraradices . In contrast, the highest chlorophyll a/b ratio (2.42) and total pigment content (1.3 mg g −1 fresh weight) were recorded in the 5% biochar treatment with the combined fungal inoculum. Overall, the results demonstrated that biochar application—particularly at the 5% level—when combined with G. intraradices or dual mycorrhizal inoculation, markedly enhanced growth, physiological efficiency, and plant water status in chrysanthemum. This approach can therefore be considered an effective strategy for improving plant performance in outdoor green wall systems while reducing reliance on chemical inputs in urban green infrastructure.
